questions.passage: Linguists rarely have the opportunity to observe a language being born, but the founding of a school for deaf children on the island of Merrow in 1986 provided exactly such a case. Before the school opened, most deaf islanders lived in isolation from one another and communicated with their hearing families through simple, home-made gestures. Once brought together, the first pupils rapidly developed a shared system of signs. This early system, researchers found, was effective but loosely organised: signers varied in how they ordered words and rarely marked who did what to whom. The decisive changes came with the next generation of children, who entered the school at the age of four or five and learned the system from older pupils rather than inventing it. These younger signers did not simply copy what they saw. They regularised it, introducing consistent ways of indicating space, time and grammatical roles that the older signers seldom used, even though the latter had been signing for longer. For many researchers, the Merrow case supports the view that young children are not merely passive learners of the language around them but active contributors to its structure. Others are more cautious, noting that the school also brought increased contact with written language and with visiting teachers, influences that may have shaped the language in ways that are difficult to separate from the children's own contribution.
questions.text: According to the passage, before the school was founded, deaf people on Merrow ----.
options: had already developed a highly structured sign language that was used throughout the island
lacked a common sign language and used gestures developed within their own families
were taught to communicate through written language
attended schools on the mainland
learned sign language from visiting teachers
questions.explanation: Okul açılmadan önce sağır adalıların birbirinden yalıtılmış yaşadığı ve aileleriyle evde geliştirilmiş basit jestlerle iletişim kurduğu belirtilir: 'lacked a common sign language and used gestures developed within their own families'. 'Had already developed a highly structured sign language' parçayla çelişir; yazı diliyle ve ziyaretçi öğretmenlerle temas okulla birlikte başlamıştır.

For many researchers, the Merrow case supports the view that young children are not merely passive learners of the language around them but active contributors to its structure. Others are more cautious, noting that the school also brought increased contact with written language and with visiting teachers, influences that may have shaped the language in ways that are difficult to separate from the children's own contribution.

the visiting teachers
the hearing families
the researchers
the older signers
questions.explanation: 'Even though the latter had been signing for longer' ifadesinde 'the latter', hemen önce anılan iki gruptan ikincisini, yani 'the older signers' grubunu gösterir; daha uzun süredir işaret eden de onlardır. 'The younger signers' cümlenin öznesidir ve okula sonradan gelmiştir; öğretmenler ve aileler bu cümlede anılmaz.

questions.passage: Linguists rarely have the opportunity to observe a language being born, but the founding of a school for deaf children on the island of Merrow in 1986 provided exactly such a case. Before the school opened, most deaf islanders lived in isolation from one another and communicated with their hearing families through simple, home-made gestures. Once brought together, the first pupils rapidly developed a shared system of signs. This early system, researchers found, was effective but loosely organised: signers varied in how they ordered words and rarely marked who did what to whom. The decisive changes came with the next generation of children, who entered the school at the age of four or five and learned the system from older pupils rather than inventing it. These younger signers did not simply copy what they saw. They regularised it, introducing consistent ways of indicating space, time and grammatical roles that the older signers seldom used, even though the latter had been signing for longer. For many researchers, the Merrow case supports the view that young children are not merely passive learners of the language around them but active contributors to its structure. Others are more cautious, noting that the school also brought increased contact with written language and with visiting teachers, influences that may have shaped the language in ways that are difficult to separate from the children's own contribution.
questions.text: The researchers described as 'more cautious' suggest that ----.
options: the second generation did not actually change the language
the Merrow case shows that adults learn languages better than children
factors other than children's own creativity may have contributed to the development of the language
visiting teachers deliberately prevented the language from developing
written language had no influence on the signers
questions.explanation: Temkinli araştırmacılar, yazı diliyle ve ziyaretçi öğretmenlerle artan temasın dili çocukların katkısından ayırt edilmesi güç biçimlerde etkilemiş olabileceğini söyler: 'factors other than children's own creativity may have contributed to the development of the language'. 'Written language had no influence on the signers' bunun tam tersidir; öğretmenlerin gelişimi kasten engellediği de söylenmez.

questions.passage: Recommendation algorithms are often blamed for trapping users in so-called filter bubbles, in which they encounter only views that confirm their existing beliefs. questions.explanation: ‘Until all the evidence had been examined’ kararın ertelendiğini gösterir; ‘put off’ (ertelemek) bu anlamı verir. ‘Give in’ (pes etmek) nesne almaz; ‘take after’ (birine benzemek), ‘run into’ (rastlamak) ve ‘look up to’ (saygı duymak) bir kararla anlamlı bir bağlantı kurmaz.

questions.text: ---- the rapid growth of online shopping, many traditional retailers have had to rethink the way they use their physical stores.
options: Regardless of
On behalf of
In contrast to
Apart from
In response to
questions.explanation: Perakendecilerin mağazalarını yeniden düşünmesi, çevrim içi alışverişin hızla büyümesine verilen bir tepkidir; bu nedenle ‘In response to’ (-e yanıt olarak) doğrudur. ‘Regardless of’ (-e bakmaksızın) neden-sonuç ilişkisini koparır; ‘On behalf of’ (adına), ‘In contrast to’ (-in aksine) ve ‘Apart from’ (-in yanı sıra, dışında) cümlenin mantığına uymaz.

questions.text: By the time the vaccine became widely available, the virus ---- to more than forty countries.
options: had spread
has spread
spreads
would spread
is spreading
questions.explanation: ‘By the time + geçmiş zaman’ yapısı, ana cümledeki eylemin o andan önce tamamlandığını gösterir ve ‘past perfect’ gerektirir: ‘had spread’. ‘Has spread’ ve ‘is spreading’ şimdiki zamana bağlanır; ‘spreads’ genel bir doğruyu anlatır; ‘would spread’ ise geçmişte gelecek anlamı vererek zaman sırasını bozar.

questions.text: Researchers are still uncertain about ---- the ancient settlement on the river bank was abandoned so suddenly.
options: which
whose
what
why
whom
questions.explanation: Boşluktan sonra eksiksiz bir cümle (the settlement was abandoned so suddenly) geldiği için sebep soran bir isim cümleciği bağlacı gerekir: ‘why’. ‘Which’, ‘what’ ve ‘whom’ cümlede eksik bir öğenin yerini tutar, oysa burada eksik öğe yoktur; ‘whose’ ise bir isimle birlikte kullanılmalıdır.

questions.text: Not only ---- the new alloy considerably lighter than steel, but it also resists corrosion far more effectively.
options: does
is
has
it is
being
questions.explanation: ‘Not only’ cümle başında devrik yapı ister; ‘the new alloy ... lighter than steel’ sıfat yüklemi olduğu için yardımcı fiil ‘is’ öne gelir. ‘Does’ ve ‘has’ ardından fiil bekler; ‘it is’ devrik değildir ve fazladan özne içerir; ‘being’ ise çekimli bir fiil olmadığından cümle kuramaz.

questions.text: Participants were asked to avoid caffeine for twelve hours before the experiment ---- their sleep patterns could be measured accurately.
options: unless
whereas
so that
even if
as though
questions.explanation: Kafeinden kaçınmanın amacı uyku düzeninin doğru ölçülebilmesidir; amaç bildiren ‘so that’ ve ardından gelen ‘could’ bu ilişkiyi kurar. ‘Unless’ (-mezse) ve ‘even if’ (-se bile) koşul ve zıtlık bildirir; ‘whereas’ (oysa) iki durumu karşılaştırır; ‘as though’ (sanki) ise anlamsız bir benzetme yapar.

questions.text: If governments ---- more in early childhood education decades ago, many of today's social problems might be less severe.
options: invested
had invested
have invested
would invest
were investing
questions.explanation: ‘Decades ago’ geçmişe, ‘might be less severe’ ise bugüne ait bir sonuca gönderme yapar; bu karma koşul cümlesinde ‘if’ bölümü geçmişte gerçekleşmemiş bir durumu anlatır ve ‘past perfect’ (had invested) ister. ‘Invested’ ve ‘were investing’ şimdiki zamana ait gerçek dışı durum bildirir; ‘have invested’ koşul yapısına uymaz; ‘would invest’ ise ‘if’ bölümünde kullanılmaz.

questions.text: The manuscript, ---- in a monastery library in the 1950s, is believed to be the oldest surviving copy of the poem.
options: discovering
was discovered
which discovered
discovered
to have discovered
questions.explanation: El yazması keşfedilen nesnedir, bu yüzden edilgen anlamlı kısaltılmış sıfat cümleciği ‘discovered’ (= which was discovered) gerekir. ‘Discovering’ ve ‘which discovered’ etken anlam verir; ‘was discovered’ cümlede ikinci bir yüklem oluşturur; ‘to have discovered’ ise hem etkendir hem de yapıya uymaz.

questions.text: The more carefully a study is designed, ---- its results are to be misinterpreted by the public.
options: less likely
the most likely
the less likely
so likely
as likely as
questions.explanation: ‘The more ..., the less ...’ (ne kadar ... o kadar az) karşılaştırma yapısında her iki bölüm de ‘the’ ile başlar: ‘the less likely’. ‘Less likely’ yapıdaki ‘the’ eksik olduğu için hatalıdır; ‘the most likely’ üstünlük bildirir; ‘so likely’ ve ‘as likely as’ ise bu kalıpla kullanılmaz.

questions.text: Some economists argue that the new tax is unlikely to change consumer behaviour, ---- others believe that it will reduce consumption significantly.
options: whereas
because
so that
unless
provided that
questions.explanation: Cümle iki karşıt görüşü karşılaştırır: Bazı ekonomistler verginin etkisiz kalacağını düşünürken diğerleri tüketimi azaltacağına inanır; bu zıtlığı ‘whereas’ (oysa, -iken) kurar. ‘Because’ neden, ‘so that’ amaç, ‘unless’ ve ‘provided that’ ise koşul bildirir ve iki görüş arasındaki karşıtlığı veremez.

questions.text: Patients are advised to keep taking their antibiotics ---- their symptoms disappear within a few days.
options: as soon as
so that
now that
in order that
even if
questions.explanation: Tavsiye, belirtiler birkaç günde geçse bile ilacın bırakılmaması yönündedir; bu nedenle ‘even if’ (-se bile) doğrudur. ‘As soon as’ (-ir -mez) ve ‘now that’ (madem ki) belirtilerin geçmesini devam etmenin nedeni ya da zamanı gibi gösterir; ‘so that’ ve ‘in order that’ ise belirtilerin geçmesini bir amaç gibi sunar.

questions.text: It was not until the invention of the microscope in the seventeenth century ---- scientists could observe individual cells.
options: when
which
that
then
since
questions.explanation: ‘It was not until ... that ...’ (ancak ... olunca) vurgu yapısının sabit bağlacı ‘that’tir. ‘When’ ve ‘since’ zaman bildirse de bu kalıpta kullanılmaz; ‘which’ bir ismi nitelemek ister; ‘then’ ise bağlaç değil zarftır ve iki cümleyi bağlayamaz.

questions.passage: The leaves of the lotus plant stay remarkably clean, even though the plant often grows in muddy water. For centuries this was simply admired, but in the 1970s the German botanist Wilhelm Barthlott examined the leaves under an electron microscope and discovered (1) ---- makes them so clean. Their surface, it turned out, is covered with tiny bumps coated in wax. Water droplets cannot spread out on such a surface; (2) ----, they rest on the tips of the bumps and roll off easily, picking up particles of dirt as they go. This phenomenon, now known as the lotus effect, has inspired materials scientists to develop so-called superhydrophobic coatings, which repel water far more strongly than ordinary materials do. Self-cleaning glass, stain-resistant fabrics and paints that keep the outer walls of buildings clean are among the products that have been (3) ---- on this principle. The coatings are not yet perfect, however. Because their microscopic structures are delicate, they tend to wear away with (4) ---- use, and engineers are still searching for surfaces that can repel water for years (5) ---- just a few months.
questions.text: (1) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: whose
why
that
whether
what
questions.explanation: Boşluktan sonraki ‘makes them so clean’ bölümünün öznesi eksiktir; hem özne görevi gören hem de ‘discovered’ fiilinin nesnesi olan isim cümleciğini ‘what’ (… şeyi) başlatır. ‘Why’ ve ‘whether’ özne eksikliğini gidermez; ‘whose’ ardından bir isim ister; ‘that’ ise burada özne olamaz.

options: instead

questions.explanation: Önceki cümle damlaların yüzeye yayılamadığını, sonraki cümle ise bunun yerine tümseklerin ucunda durup yuvarlandığını anlatır; bu yer değiştirme ilişkisini ‘instead’ (bunun yerine) kurar. ‘Moreover’ (üstelik) ve ‘similarly’ (benzer şekilde) ekleme ve benzerlik bildirir; ‘for example’ örnek verir; ‘otherwise’ (aksi takdirde) ise koşul ilişkisi kurar.

options: insisted

questions.explanation: ‘Be based on’ (-e dayanmak) kalıbı, kendi kendini temizleyen cam ve lekeye dayanıklı kumaş gibi ürünlerin lotus etkisi ilkesine dayandığını anlatır. ‘Insisted’ (ısrar etmek), ‘objected’ (itiraz etmek) ve ‘consisted’ (oluşmak) edilgen yapıda bu anlamı vermez; ‘deprived’ (yoksun bırakılmış) ise ‘of’ ister ve anlamca uymaz.

questions.passage: Languages differ remarkably in the number of basic words they use for colours. Some have only two or three such terms, (1) ---- English is usually said to have eleven. In a famous study published in 1969, the anthropologists Brent Berlin and Paul Kay argued that these differences are far from random. (2) ---- their analysis, languages tend to acquire colour terms in a fairly predictable order: words for dark and light come first, followed by red, and only later by terms such as green, yellow and blue. Their proposal was (3) ---- influential, but it also attracted criticism, partly because many of the languages in their sample were studied through dictionaries rather than through fieldwork with speakers. More recent research has (4) ---- whether colour vocabulary actually shapes perception. Experiments with Russian speakers, whose language obliges them to distinguish light blue from dark blue, suggest that they discriminate between these shades slightly faster than English speakers do. Such effects appear to be small, however, and researchers continue to debate how much language (5) ---- the way we see the world.

so that
unless
as if
whereas
questions.explanation: Cümle iki dili karşılaştırır: Bazı dillerde yalnızca iki üç renk terimi varken İngilizcede on bir tane vardır; bu karşıtlığı ‘whereas’ (oysa) kurar. ‘Because’ neden, ‘so that’ amaç, ‘unless’ koşul bildirir; ‘as if’ (sanki) ise anlamsız bir benzetme yapar.

questions.text: Although lithium-ion batteries have transformed portable electronics, ----.
options: they are now used in mobile phones, laptops and electric cars
since they can be recharged hundreds of times without much loss of capacity
scientists have therefore stopped searching for alternative technologies
the first commercial version appeared on the market in the early 1990s
their production depends on materials that are costly and difficult to extract
questions.explanation: ‘Although’ zıtlık ister: Bataryalar taşınabilir elektroniği dönüştürmüş olsa da üretimleri pahalı ve çıkarılması zor malzemelere ‘depends’ (bağlıdır). ‘Mobile phones’ seçeneği zıtlık değil, olumlu bir devam bildirir; ‘recharged’ ile başlayan seçenek ‘since’ yüzünden ana cümle kuramaz; ‘stopped’ içeren seçenek ‘therefore’ ile zıtlığa ters bir sonuç verir; ‘commercial’ sürümün tarihi ise ilgisiz bir bilgidir.

questions.text: ----, the region's farmers have increasingly turned to drought-resistant crop varieties.
options: Even though water supplies have remained plentiful and reliable
Unless the government provides them with new subsidies
So that the soil would become drier and less fertile
As rainfall has become less predictable over the past two decades
Because the soil in the region has always been unusually wet
questions.explanation: Çiftçilerin kuraklığa dayanıklı çeşitlere yönelmesinin nedeni yağışların öngörülemez hâle gelmesidir; ‘As rainfall has become less predictable’ bu nedeni verir. ‘Plentiful’ su kaynaklarından söz eden seçenek mantıksal olarak çelişir; ‘subsidies’ koşulu ‘have turned’ ile uyuşmaz; ‘fertile’ ile biten seçenek toprağın kurumasını bir amaç gibi sunar; toprağın hep ‘wet’ olması ise kuraklığa dayanıklı ürünlere yönelmeyi açıklamaz.

questions.text: Children who are exposed to two languages from birth tend to perform well on certain attention tasks, ----.
options: possibly because they constantly practise switching between two linguistic systems
unless they had learned to read before starting school
whereas monolingual adults rarely forget their first language
as if they had never been exposed to a second language
so that their parents speak only one language at home
questions.explanation: İki dilli çocukların dikkat görevlerindeki başarısı, sürekli iki dil sistemi arasında geçiş yapmalarıyla açıklanabilir; ‘possibly because ... switching’ seçeneği bu nedeni verir. ‘Unless’ ile başlayan ve ‘read’ içeren seçenek zaman ve anlam açısından uyuşmaz; ‘monolingual adults’ ilgisiz bir karşılaştırmadır; ‘never been exposed’ cümlenin öznesiyle çelişir; ‘parents speak only one language’ ise anlamsız bir amaç bildirir.

questions.text: The archaeologists could not determine the exact age of the wooden tools ----.
options: until they will analyse the surrounding soil next year
so that the museum displayed them immediately
because the samples had been contaminated during an earlier excavation
even though radiocarbon dating was not available to them
which were made entirely of stone and bone
questions.explanation: Aletlerin yaşının belirlenememesinin mantıklı nedeni örneklerin önceki bir kazıda ‘contaminated’ (kirlenmiş) olmasıdır. ‘Until ... will analyse’ yapısı dil bilgisi açısından hatalıdır; ‘museum displayed’ seçeneği anlamsız bir amaç verir; ‘radiocarbon’ seçeneği ‘even though’ ile mantıksız bir zıtlık kurar; ‘stone and bone’ ise aletlerin tahta olmasıyla çelişir.

questions.text: If the central bank had raised interest rates earlier, ----.
options: consumers will borrow less money next year
prices are rising faster than wages
inflation might not have reached such high levels
the economy grew steadily in the following decade
unemployment has fallen to its lowest level
questions.explanation: ‘If + past perfect’ üçüncü tip koşul cümlesidir ve ana cümlede ‘might/would have + V3’ ister: ‘inflation might not have reached’. ‘Will borrow’ birinci tip koşula, ‘are rising’ ve ‘has fallen’ gerçek bir şimdiki duruma, ‘grew steadily’ ise gerçek bir geçmiş olaya aittir; hiçbiri gerçekleşmemiş geçmiş koşulun sonucunu bildirmez.

questions.text: ----, many patients fail to complete their full course of physiotherapy.
options: So that their doctors can monitor their progress more closely
Since the benefits of the exercises often become noticeable only after several weeks
Unless they had been injured in a serious accident
As long as the exercises are short and enjoyable
Whereas physiotherapy was first developed in the nineteenth century
questions.explanation: Hastaların tedaviyi yarıda bırakmasının mantıklı nedeni egzersizlerin yararının ancak haftalar sonra fark edilmesidir; ‘Since the benefits ... become noticeable’ bu nedeni verir. ‘Monitor’ içeren seçenek bırakmayı bir amaç gibi sunar; ‘injured’ koşulu zaman açısından uyuşmaz; ‘enjoyable’ egzersizler bırakma nedeni olamaz; ‘nineteenth century’ bilgisi ise ilgisizdir.

questions.text: The new building material is not only stronger than conventional brick ----.
options: or it is far more expensive to produce
nor has it been approved by safety inspectors
because it contains a large amount of recycled glass

questions.passage: For most of the history of archaeology, the hardened plaque found on ancient teeth was treated as dirt to be scraped away and discarded. Today, it is regarded as one of the richest sources of information about past lives. Dental calculus, as this mineralised plaque is formally known, forms when bacteria in the mouth become trapped in layers of calcium phosphate from saliva. As it builds up over a lifetime, it also captures tiny fragments of whatever passes through the mouth: starch grains from cereals, pollen, plant fibres and even proteins from milk. Because the mineral crust protects these materials from decay, they can survive for thousands of years, long after soft tissues have vanished. Using microscopes and genetic sequencing, researchers have extracted from calculus evidence that Neanderthals cooked plants and may have used medicinal herbs, and that people in certain Bronze Age communities were consuming dairy products well before most adults could digest milk. In one widely reported case, blue pigment embedded in the teeth of a medieval woman in Germany suggested that she had been involved in producing illuminated manuscripts, a task usually associated with men at the time. Such findings are not without limitations, however. Calculus records only what happened to enter the mouth, so it may overrepresent some foods and miss others entirely, and samples can easily be contaminated by modern bacteria during excavation or handling. Moreover, removing calculus from a skeleton is a destructive process, which raises questions about how much of an irreplaceable collection should be sacrificed for analysis. Many archaeologists therefore argue that excavation teams should collect and store calculus routinely, so that future researchers, perhaps equipped with more sensitive techniques, can study it without damaging further remains.

options: the value of ancient dental plaque as a source of evidence about past diets and activities

the techniques used by archaeologists to establish the age of human skeletons

the decline of dental hygiene in prehistoric farming communities

Tunç Çağı'ndaki ‘diseases’ ve diş ‘hygiene’ konusu ele alınmaz; iskeletlerin yaşını belirleme ‘techniques’ söz konusu değildir; mavi pigment ve ‘manuscripts’ ise yalnızca bir örnektir.

questions.passage: Trans fats, produced industrially when vegetable oils are partially hydrogenated, were once found in a vast range of processed foods, from biscuits and margarine to fried snacks. Manufacturers valued them because they are cheap, extend the shelf life of products and give baked goods an appealing texture. From the 1990s onwards, however, a growing body of research linked them to heart disease: unlike most other fats, they appear both to raise levels of harmful LDL cholesterol and to lower levels of protective HDL cholesterol. In 2003, Denmark became the first country to restrict their use, limiting industrially produced trans fats to two per cent of the total fat in any food. Several cities followed, most notably New York, which banned them from restaurant kitchens in 2008. One later study compared counties in New York State that had introduced restrictions with neighbouring counties that had not, and found that hospital admissions for heart attacks and strokes fell by around six per cent more in the counties with restrictions. Encouraged by such results, the World Health Organization called in 2018 for industrial trans fats to be eliminated from the global food supply. Policies of this kind are not without critics, however. Some regard them as an unjustified intrusion by the state into personal choices, arguing that clear labelling would allow consumers to decide for themselves. Others have pointed out that manufacturers sometimes replaced trans fats with palm oil, which is high in saturated fat and whose production has been associated with deforestation in tropical countries. Even so, most public health experts regard the policy as a rare success, largely because it changes what is available to consumers without requiring them to alter their behaviour.
questions.text: Which of the following could be the best title for the passage?

Why Denmark Banned All Processed Foods

How Food Labels Changed Consumer Behaviour

questions.explanation: Parça endüstriyel trans yağları yasaklayan ya da sınırlayan politikaları, sağlık üzerindeki olumlu sonuçlarını ve bu politikalara yöneltilen eleştirileri anlatır; bu yüzden ‘Removing Trans Fats from Food’ başlığı en uygundur. Danimarka tüm ‘Processed’ gıdaları yasaklamamış, yalnızca trans yağı sınırlamıştır; ‘Palm’ yağı doymuş yağ oranı yüksek bir ikame olarak eleştirilir; ‘Labels’ yalnızca eleştirmenlerin önerisidir; ‘Infection’ konusu ise hiç geçmez.

One later study compared counties in New York State that had introduced restrictions with neighbouring counties that had not, and found that hospital admissions for heart attacks and strokes fell by around six per cent more in the counties with restrictions. Encouraged by such results, the World Health Organization called in 2018 for industrial trans fats to be eliminated from the global food supply. Policies of this kind are not without critics, however. Some regard them as an unjustified intrusion by the state into personal choices, arguing that clear labelling would allow consumers to decide for themselves. Others have pointed out that manufacturers sometimes replaced trans fats with palm oil, which is high in saturated fat and whose production has been associated with deforestation in tropical countries. Even so, most public health experts regard the policy as a rare success, largely because it changes what is available to consumers without requiring them to alter their behaviour.

questions.passage: Imagine choosing between two subscriptions to a magazine: an online version for 59 dollars and a combined print and online version for 125 dollars. Many people would opt for the cheaper option. Now suppose a third choice is added: the print version alone, also for 125 dollars. Hardly anyone would select it, since it is obviously inferior to the combined package at the same price. Yet in a well-known classroom demonstration, adding this unattractive option sharply increased the proportion of students who chose the expensive combined package. This phenomenon, known as the decoy effect, contradicts a basic assumption of classical economics, namely that the relative preference between two options should not be altered by the presence of a third one that nobody wants. Behavioural economists explain the effect by pointing out that people rarely evaluate options in absolute terms. Instead, they look for comparisons that make a decision easier to justify, and an inferior decoy provides precisely such a comparison, making the target option seem like an obvious bargain. Businesses have not been slow to exploit this tendency. Cinemas, for example, may price a medium portion of popcorn only slightly below a large one, so that the large portion appears to offer far better value. The effect is not confined to shopping, either: some studies suggest that it may influence choices between job candidates or even political parties. However, attempts to replicate the original findings have produced mixed results, and some researchers argue that the decoy effect is weaker when people are shown realistic information, such as pictures of products, rather than simple tables of numbers. It may therefore be less universal than popular accounts imply.

questions.passage: Seagrasses are often mistaken for seaweeds, but they are in fact flowering plants whose ancestors returned to the sea from land tens of millions of years ago. Today they form extensive underwater meadows in shallow coastal waters on every continent except Antarctica. Although these meadows cover only a tiny fraction of the ocean floor, they are thought to account for a disproportionately large share of the carbon stored in marine sediments. Their dense leaves slow the movement of water, causing suspended particles to settle, while their roots and buried stems accumulate organic matter in oxygen-poor mud, where it decomposes extremely slowly and may remain locked away for centuries. Seagrass meadows also provide nursery grounds for many commercially important fish, stabilise the seabed against erosion and appear to reduce levels of harmful bacteria in the surrounding water. Despite this, they are disappearing at an alarming rate. Estimates suggest that nearly a third of the world's seagrass area may have been lost since the late nineteenth century, mainly because of coastal development, dredging and nutrient pollution from agriculture, which encourages the growth of algae that block the sunlight seagrasses need. When a meadow is destroyed, the carbon held in its sediments can gradually be released back into the water and the atmosphere. Restoration projects have achieved encouraging results in some places. In the US state of Virginia, for instance, volunteers scattered tens of millions of seeds into coastal lagoons over two decades, and the resulting meadows now cover several thousand hectares and have begun to store measurable amounts of carbon. Nevertheless, scientists caution that restoration is slow and costly, and that protecting existing meadows is far more effective than attempting to recreate them once they have gone.
questions.text: According to the passage, the organic matter stored by seagrass meadows decomposes slowly because ----.
options: it is protected by a thick layer of algae

it is constantly moved around by strong currents
the water in coastal areas is unusually cold
it is buried in mud that contains little oxygen
questions.explanation: Parçada organik maddenin ‘oxygen-poor mud’ içinde biriktiği ve orada çok yavaş ayrıştığı belirtilir; yani az oksijenli çamura gömülüdür. ‘Algae’ deniz çayırlarına zarar veren bir etken olarak geçer; ‘sunlight’ ayrışmayla ilişkilendirilmez; yapraklar akıntıyı yavaşlattığı için ‘currents’ seçeneği ters düşer; suyun ‘cold’ olduğu ise söylenmez.

questions.passage: The appealing aroma of freshly baked bread, roasted coffee or a grilled steak owes much to a set of chemical processes known as the Maillard reaction, named after the French chemist Louis-Camille Maillard, who first described it in 1912. The reaction occurs when sugars react with amino acids, the building blocks of proteins, under heat. Unlike caramelisation, which involves sugars alone, it produces hundreds of different compounds, each contributing to the colour, flavour and smell of the final product. The precise mixture depends on the types of sugars and amino acids present, as well as on temperature, moisture and acidity, which is why the crust of bread tastes so different from the surface of roasted meat. Because water keeps the surface of food at around 100 degrees Celsius, the reaction proceeds only slowly in boiled or steamed dishes; this explains why boiled meat remains grey, while meat that has been dried and seared at higher temperatures turns brown. Food manufacturers exploit this knowledge extensively, adjusting baking times, adding small amounts of sugar or altering acidity to produce the colours and flavours that consumers expect. The reaction is not, however, entirely beneficial. In starchy foods such as chips and crisps cooked at high temperatures, it can generate acrylamide, a substance that has caused cancer in laboratory animals when given in large doses. Whether the much smaller amounts found in ordinary diets pose a significant risk to humans remains uncertain, as studies of human populations have so far produced inconsistent results. Nevertheless, food safety agencies generally advise consumers to cook potatoes to a golden yellow rather than a dark brown colour, and many manufacturers have changed their processes to reduce acrylamide levels.

questions.text:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

questions.text:

questions.passage: Language change is often regarded by the public as a sign of decline. ---- Linguists, however, point out that all living languages change constantly and that the forms criticised today were often once innovations themselves. Araya bu gerileme algısını örnekleyen, gençlerin argo ve özensiz dil bilgisiyle dili ‘ruining’ ettiğine dair şikâyet girmelidir. ‘Borrowed’ ve ‘hundred speakers’ cümleleri konuyu değiştirir; ‘Dictionaries’ akışla ilgisizdir; ‘banned’ ise dilbilimcilerin görüşüyle çelişir.

questions.passage: Microplastics have been found almost everywhere scientists have looked, from deep-sea sediments to Arctic snow. questions.text: Despite repeated attempts, the committee failed to ---- the two conflicting reports, as each relied on an entirely different set of data.

questions.text: The early symptoms of the disease are so ---- that many patients do not seek medical help until the condition has reached an advanced stage.

questions.text: The new regulations are intended to ---- small businesses from the sudden price increases that followed the energy crisis.

questions.text: Negotiations between the union and the management ---- after the company refused to discuss the proposed changes to working hours.

questions.text: Although the two species look ---- identical, genetic analysis has shown that they separated from a common ancestor several million years ago.

questions.text: The museum's decision to return the statues to their country of origin was widely seen as an attempt to ---- for the injustices of the colonial era.

questions.text: By the time the first telescope was pointed at the night sky in the early seventeenth century, sailors ---- the stars for navigation for thousands of years.

questions.text: ---- the volunteers been told about the real purpose of the experiment, their responses might have been very different.

questions.text: The ancient manuscript is so fragile that it ---- only under strictly controlled conditions of light and humidity.

questions.explanation: Elyazması incelenen nesnedir, inceleyen değil; bu yüzden edilgen yapı gerekir: ‘can be examined’ (incelenebilir). ‘Can examine’, ‘has examined’, ‘must have examined’ ve ‘was examining’ etken yapıdadır ve elyazmasını işi yapan özne gibi gösterir; ayrıca ‘is so fragile’ ifadesindeki geniş zaman bağlamıyla da uyuşmazlar.

questions.text: Many employees admit ---- work emails late at night, even though they know that it disturbs their sleep.

to check
check

having been checked

questions.text: The decline in bee populations has been attributed ---- a combination of pesticide use, habitat loss and disease.

with
on
from
to

questions.text: ---- the city's population has doubled over the past three decades, the number of public parks has barely changed.

questions.text: The researchers interviewed more than two hundred nurses, many of ---- reported working over fifty hours a week.
options: them
which

whom
those
questions.explanation: ‘Many of’ ifadesinden sonra insanlar için ilgi zamiri olarak nesne biçimi ‘whom’ kullanılır ve iki cümleyi bağlar. ‘Them’ ve ‘those’ bağlaç işlevi görmediği için iki tam cümleyi virgülle bağlayamaz; ‘which’ insanlar için kullanılmaz, ‘who’ ise edattan sonra gelemez.

questions.text: The newer vaccine produced ---- side effects than the original one, which made it far more acceptable to patients.
options: considerably fewer
very fewer
the fewest
so few
as fewer
questions.explanation: ‘Than’ karşılaştırma ister ve ‘side effects’ sayılabilir olduğundan ‘fewer’ kullanılır; ‘considerably’ karşılaştırmayı güçlendirir. ‘Very fewer’ hatalıdır, çünkü ‘very’ karşılaştırma sıfatını nitelemez; ‘the fewest’ üstünlük derecesidir, ‘so few’ ve ‘as fewer’ ise ‘than’ ile kullanılamaz.

questions.text: According to current projections, nearly seventy per cent of the world's population ---- in urban areas by 2050.

has lived
will be living
lived
would have lived
questions.explanation: ‘Current projections’ ve ‘by 2050’ geleceğe yönelik bir tahmin bildirir; bu yüzden ‘will be living’ (yaşıyor olacak) uygundur. ‘Had lived’, ‘has lived’ ve ‘lived’ geçmişe ya da şimdiye gönderme yapar; ‘would have lived’ ise gerçekleşmemiş geçmiş bir durumu anlatır.

questions.text: It remains unclear ---- the painting was completed by the master himself or by one of his assistants.
options: whether
that
unless
which
so
questions.explanation: Cümledeki ‘… or …’ yapısı iki olasılık arasında bir belirsizlik bildirir ve isim cümleciği ‘whether’ (-ip -mediği) ile kurulur: Tablonun ustanın kendisi mi yoksa bir yardımcısı tarafından mı bitirildiği belirsizdir. ‘That’ kesinlik bildirir ve ‘or’ ile çelişir; ‘unless’, ‘which’ ve ‘so’ ise burada isim cümleciği başlatamaz.

questions.passage: In the 1970s, the American astronomer Vera Rubin and her colleague Kent Ford set out to measure how fast stars orbit the centres of spiral galaxies. According to the laws of gravity, stars far from the bright, crowded centre (1) ---- move more slowly, just as the outer planets of our solar system travel more slowly than those (2) ---- to the Sun. Rubin's observations, however, revealed something unexpected: stars near the edges were moving almost as fast as those near the centre. At such speeds, the galaxies should have flown apart, (3) ---- the visible matter alone could not produce enough gravity to hold them together. The most widely accepted explanation is that each galaxy is surrounded by a vast halo of invisible material, now known as dark matter. (4) ---- decades of searching, however, physicists have still not identified what this substance is made of, and a minority of researchers argue that our theory of gravity itself may need to be (5) ----.

ought

questions.explanation: Cümle yerçekimi yasalarına göre beklenen durumu anlatır: Merkezden uzak yıldızların daha yavaş hareket etmesi gerekir; bu beklentiyi ‘should’ verir. ‘Used to’ geçmişteki alışkanlığı bildirir ve kurallı bir beklentiye uymaz; ‘ought’ ardından ‘to’ olmadan kullanılamaz; ‘might have’ ve ‘would have’ ise ardından ‘moved’ gibi üçüncü hâl ister ve ‘move’ ile kullanılamaz.

questions.passage: For much of the Renaissance, the most expensive colour on a painter's palette was ultramarine, a deep blue pigment made from the semi-precious stone lapis lazuli. The finest stone came from mines in what is now Afghanistan, and it had to be carried thousands of kilometres before (1) ---- in Venice and other European ports. Turning the stone into pigment was also laborious, (2) ---- it required grinding, mixing with wax and oils, and repeated kneading to separate the blue particles from impurities. Because of its cost, ultramarine was often (3) ---- for the most important figures in a painting, particularly the robes of the Virgin Mary. Some contracts between artists and their patrons even specified the quality of blue to be used, (4) ---- the painter should replace it with a cheaper alternative such as azurite. The situation changed only in the 1820s, (5) ---- a French chemist developed a synthetic version that could be produced at a fraction of the price.

arrived
to arrive
having been arrived
arrives

questions.text: Although the city introduced a congestion charge to reduce traffic in the centre, ----.
options: the charge was designed to cut both traffic and pollution
because many residents already used public transport
traffic in the centre had therefore fallen by a third
unless drivers were willing to pay the daily fee
air quality in the surrounding neighbourhoods appears to have worsened as drivers took longer routes
questions.explanation: ‘Although’ beklenmedik bir sonuç ister: Merkezde trafiği azaltmak için ücret getirilmesine rağmen sürücüler daha uzun yollar kullandığı için çevre mahallelerde hava kalitesi kötüleşmiş görünmektedir. Ücretin ‘designed’ amacını anlatan seçenek zıtlık kurmaz; ‘because’ ve ‘unless’ ile başlayanlar ana cümle oluşturmaz; ‘therefore’ ise ‘although’ ile çelişen bir sonuç bağlacıdır.

questions.text: If the soil had not been so heavily compacted by machinery, ----.
options: farmers will need to plough the fields more deeply
the harvest was smaller than in previous years
rainwater would have soaked into the ground instead of running off the fields
crops are usually planted in early spring
it had been used to grow wheat for centuries
questions.explanation: ‘If + past perfect’ üçüncü tip koşuldur ve ana cümlede ‘would have + V3’ gerektirir: Toprak bu kadar sıkıştırılmasaydı yağmur suyu tarlalardan akıp gitmek yerine toprağa sızardı. ‘Will need to plough’ birinci tip, ‘was smaller’ ve ‘had been used’ düz geçmiş anlatımlardır; ‘usually planted’ ise genel bir bilgi verir ve koşula bağlanmaz.

questions.text: ----, the patients who were given the new drug recovered no faster than those who received a placebo.
options: Since the drug had been tested on thousands of animals
So that the trial could be completed on time
Unless the dosage is increased considerably
Contrary to what the researchers had expected
As the drug proved highly effective
questions.explanation: İlacı alan hastaların plasebo alanlardan daha hızlı iyileşmemesi beklenmedik bir sonuçtur; ‘Contrary to what the researchers had expected’ (araştırmacıların beklediğinin aksine) bunu doğru biçimde tanıtır. İlacın hayvanlarda ‘tested’ olması ya da ‘highly effective’ çıkması sonuçla çelişir; ‘So that … completed on time’ amaç bildirir; ‘Unless the dosage is increased’ ise zaman açısından geçmişteki sonuca uymaz.

questions.text: Not only do night-shift workers sleep less than their colleagues on day shifts, ----.
options: and they had been offered higher wages
so they are less likely to suffer from fatigue
but also the factory operates around the clock
whereas their sleep is usually deeper and longer
but they are also more likely to develop digestive and metabolic problems
questions.explanation: ‘Not only … but also’ yapısı aynı yönde ikinci bir bilgi ekler: Gece vardiyasında çalışanlar hem daha az uyur hem de sindirim ve metabolizma sorunları yaşama olasılıkları daha yüksektir. ‘Fatigue’ yaşama olasılığının düşük olduğunu söyleyen ve uykunun ‘deeper’ olduğunu söyleyen seçenekler mantıkça çelişir; ‘higher wages’ seçeneği ‘but also’ yapısını kurmaz; ‘factory operates’ ise devrik yapının öznesiyle bağlantısızdır.

questions.text: The theory remained largely ignored for decades ----.
options: because most physicists have accepted it today
so that its author could revise it before publication
even though no one had paid attention to it
until new evidence from satellite measurements finally confirmed its main predictions
unless it is supported by experimental data
questions.explanation: Kuram on yıllarca görmezden gelinmiş, ta ki uydu ölçümlerinden gelen yeni kanıtlar tahminlerini doğrulayana kadar; ‘until’ bu süreç sonunu doğru biçimde bildirir. Fizikçilerin bugün kuramı ‘accepted’ etmesi görmezden gelinmenin nedeni olamaz; yazarın ‘revise’ etmesi için görmezden gelinmesi mantıksızdır; ‘no one had paid attention’ zıtlık değil aynı anlamı verir; ‘unless … supported’ ise zaman uyumunu bozar.

questions.text: So few of the medieval painter's works have survived ----.
options: that historians must rely largely on written records to understand his style
as historians rely on written records
than historians had expected
which historians have studied for centuries
because historians rely on written records
questions.explanation: ‘So few … that’ (o kadar az … ki) yapısı sonuç bildirir: Ressamın çok az eseri günümüze ulaştığı için tarihçiler üslubunu anlamak için büyük ölçüde yazılı kaynaklara dayanmak zorundadır. ‘As’ ve ‘because’ ile başlayan seçenekler ‘so’ ile tamamlanmaz; ‘than historians had expected’ karşılaştırma ister, ‘which historians have studied’ ise ilgi cümlesidir ve ‘so few’ yapısını tamamlamaz.

questions.text: Urban planners increasingly argue that wider pavements and safer cycle lanes can reduce car use, ----.
options: unless they had already bought a car
since people tend to walk or cycle more when doing so feels safe and convenient
so that car manufacturers would sell more vehicles
while cycling was invented in the nineteenth century
whereas cars had been banned from city centres
questions.explanation: Geniş kaldırımların ve güvenli bisiklet yollarının araç kullanımını azaltmasının nedeni, insanların güvenli ve rahat hissettiklerinde daha çok yürüyüp bisiklete binmesidir; ‘since’ bu nedeni bildirir. ‘Already bought a car’ koşulu ve ‘manufacturers would sell more’ amacı mantığa aykırıdır; bisikletin ‘invented’ olduğu tarih ile araçların ‘banned’ olduğunu söyleyen seçenekler ise savla ilgisizdir.

questions.text: Unless farmers rotate their crops regularly, ----.
options: soil fertility would have improved over time
crop rotation has been practised since Roman times
they had harvested more wheat than expected
pests and diseases specific to a single crop can build up in the soil
the soil became richer in nitrogen
questions.explanation: ‘Unless’ (-medikçe) olumsuz bir sonuç ister: Çiftçiler ürün nöbeti yapmazsa tek bir ürüne özgü zararlılar ve hastalıklar toprakta birikebilir. ‘Would have improved’ üçüncü tip koşula aittir; ‘practised since Roman times’ genel bir bilgi verir; ‘harvested more wheat’ ve ‘richer in nitrogen’ ise geçmiş zamanlı olup ‘unless’ cümlesinin genel geçer anlamıyla uyuşmaz ve olumlu sonuç bildirir.

questions.text: While some workers welcome the freedom of working from home, ----.
options: others report feeling isolated from their colleagues and struggle to separate work from private life
because offices are expensive to rent in large cities
it has become possible thanks to faster internet connections
so many companies have closed their offices completely
they were therefore given more holidays
questions.explanation: ‘While’ burada zıtlık bildirir: Bazı çalışanlar evden çalışmanın özgürlüğünü severken diğerleri yalnız hissettiklerini ve iş ile özel yaşamı ayırmakta zorlandıklarını söyler. Ofislerin ‘expensive to rent’ olması ‘because’ ile ana cümle kurmaz; ‘faster internet connections’ ve ‘closed their offices’ zıtlık oluşturmaz; ‘therefore … holidays’ ise mantıksız bir sonuç bildirir.

questions.text: The brain is remarkably adaptable; ----.
options: however, it can easily reorganise itself after injury
in contrast, its structure never changes after childhood
therefore, damaged neurons can never be replaced
for instance, after a stroke, undamaged regions can sometimes take over functions once performed by injured areas
otherwise, it would weigh about 1.4 kilograms
questions.explanation: Birinci cümle beynin uyum yeteneğini belirtir; ‘for instance’ ile gelen inme sonrası sağlam bölgelerin görev üstlenmesi örneği bu fikri destekler. ‘However’ aynı fikri zıtlık bağlacıyla verdiği için mantıksızdır; yapının ‘never changes’ olduğunu söyleyen ifade çelişir; ‘never be replaced’ uyum fikrinden çıkan bir sonuç değildir; ‘weigh about 1.4 kilograms’ ise ilgisizdir.

questions.text:

questions.passage:
For a long time, scientists assumed that the brain was more or less complete by the end of childhood. Brain-imaging studies carried out since the 1990s have overturned this view, showing that the adolescent brain undergoes a remarkable period of reorganisation. One of the most striking processes involved is synaptic pruning. In early childhood, the brain produces far more connections between nerve cells, known as synapses, than it will eventually need. During adolescence, connections that are used frequently are strengthened, while those that are rarely used are gradually eliminated. Although the idea of losing connections may sound alarming, pruning is generally thought to make the brain more efficient, much as cutting back the weaker branches of a tree allows the remaining ones to grow more vigorously.
Pruning does not take place evenly across the brain. Regions that handle basic sensory and motor functions tend to mature first, whereas the prefrontal cortex, which is involved in planning, weighing risks and controlling impulses, is among the last to be refined, a process that may continue into the mid-twenties. Some researchers believe that this uneven timetable helps to explain why teenagers are often more willing to take risks than adults: the systems that respond to reward are already highly active, while those that exercise restraint are still developing.
The theory has its critics, however. They point out that risk-taking varies enormously between individuals and cultures, and that teenagers can make perfectly sensible decisions when they are calm and have time to reflect. There is also some evidence that disruptions to pruning may be linked to certain psychiatric conditions, although the nature of this relationship remains far from clear. What is widely agreed is that adolescence is not merely a difficult phase to be endured but a period of considerable opportunity, when experience shapes the brain in lasting ways.
questions.text: The passage is mainly concerned with ----.
options: the reasons why brain-imaging technology was developed in the 1990s
the way the brain continues to be reshaped during adolescence and some possible consequences of this process
the treatment of psychiatric conditions that first appear in childhood
the cultural differences in the way teenagers are raised

questions.explanation: Parça, beynin ergenlikte budama (pruning) yoluyla yeniden şekillendiğini, bunun gençlerin risk alma eğilimiyle olası ilişkisini ve bu görüşe yöneltilen eleştirileri anlatır. Görüntüleme teknolojisinin neden ‘developed’ edildiği anlatılmaz; psikiyatrik durumların ‘treatment’ konusu ele alınmaz; kültürel farklar yalnızca eleştiride geçer; prefrontal korteksin ‘sensory’ işlevlerle değil planlama ve dürtü denetimiyle ilgili olduğu söylenir.

questions.passage:
Anyone who has walked across a park or a university campus has probably noticed narrow strips of worn grass that cut across the lawns, ignoring the paved paths laid out by designers. Planners call these informal routes desire paths or desire lines, because they record the routes people actually prefer to take rather than the ones they have been given. In most cases they reflect a simple calculation: pedestrians tend to choose the shortest or most convenient way between two points, especially when they are in a hurry or the official route involves an awkward detour.
For many years, the typical response of authorities was to treat desire paths as a form of misbehaviour. Fences were put up, signs asked people to keep off the grass, and the worn ground was repeatedly reseeded. Such measures rarely worked for long. Increasingly, however, urban designers regard desire paths not as a problem to be suppressed but as valuable information. Some campuses are said to have delayed paving their walkways until students had trodden their own routes across the grounds, and then simply paved the paths that had emerged. Whether or not such stories are entirely accurate, the principle behind them has gained wide acceptance.
Today, the idea has spread well beyond lawns. Researchers use location data from mobile phones and bicycles to identify where people cross roads away from official crossings or which shortcuts cyclists favour, and city authorities can use this evidence to decide where new crossings or cycle lanes would be most useful. Critics warn that not every desire path deserves official approval, since some cross sensitive habitats or create safety risks. Nevertheless, the broader lesson seems clear: good design begins by observing how people actually behave, not by expecting them to behave as planners would like.
questions.text: Which of the following could be the best title for the passage?

The History of University Campuses

questions.explanation: Parçanın ana fikri, insanların kendiliğinden oluşturduğu kestirme yolların (desire paths) bastırılması gereken bir sorun değil, tasarım için değerli bir bilgi kaynağı olduğudur; bu nedenle en uygun başlık ‘Learning from the Routes People Choose’ olur. Çitlerin işe yaramadığı söylendiği için ‘Stronger Fences’ yanlıştır; kampüslerin ‘History’ konusu ve konum verisinin nasıl ‘Invented’ edildiği anlatılmaz; ‘Careless Visitors’ başlığı da yazarın yaklaşımına aykırıdır.

In many farming systems, fields are left bare for several months between the harvest of one crop and the planting of the next. During this period, exposed soil is vulnerable to wind and rain, which can carry away the fertile topsoil that took centuries to form. Nutrients that the previous crop did not absorb, particularly nitrogen, may also be washed out of the soil and into rivers, where they can contribute to the growth of harmful algae. One increasingly popular way of addressing these problems is to sow cover crops, such as clover, rye or radish, which are grown not to be sold but to protect and improve the soil.
The benefits of cover crops are well documented. Their roots hold the soil in place and create channels through which water can soak into the ground rather than running off the surface. Leguminous species such as clover can take nitrogen from the air and, with the help of bacteria living in their roots, convert it into a form that plants can use, reducing the need for synthetic fertilisers. When the cover crop is cut down and left to decompose, it adds organic matter, which feeds soil organisms and helps the soil retain moisture during dry spells.
Despite these advantages, cover crops are still grown on only a small proportion of farmland in many countries. Seeds and planting cost money and labour, and the benefits for the farmer, such as improved yields, may take several years to appear. In dry regions, a cover crop may even compete with the following cash crop for scarce water. For this reason, some governments now offer financial support to farmers who adopt the practice, on the grounds that healthier soil and cleaner rivers benefit society as a whole.

questions.passage:
In 1983, the American sociologist Arlie Hochschild published The Managed Heart, a study of flight attendants that introduced the concept of emotional labour. Hochschild observed that the attendants were paid not only to serve meals and ensure safety but also to display particular feelings, such as warmth, calm and cheerfulness, even towards rude or frightened passengers. Their employers trained them in how to produce these feelings and monitored whether they did so successfully. In Hochschild's view, the airline was in effect selling the attendants' emotions as part of its product.
Hochschild distinguished between two ways of meeting such demands. In surface acting, workers display the required emotion without actually feeling it, as when a waiter smiles warmly at a customer he privately finds irritating. In deep acting, they try to change their inner feelings, for example by imagining that a difficult passenger is simply anxious about flying. Later research has suggested that surface acting in particular is associated with exhaustion and job dissatisfaction, perhaps because constantly hiding one's true feelings requires sustained effort.
The concept has since been applied far beyond aviation, to nurses, teachers, call-centre staff and many others whose work involves dealing with the public. Some scholars, however, argue that Hochschild's original account was too pessimistic. They note that many service workers find genuine satisfaction in helping others and that friendly interactions with customers can be a source of pride rather than strain. Others point out that emotional labour is unevenly distributed and often poorly rewarded: the jobs that demand the most of it, many of which are held by women, are frequently among the lowest paid. Whatever its limitations, the concept has drawn attention to a form of effort that was long invisible.

questions.passage:
For centuries, scurvy was one of the greatest dangers faced by sailors on long voyages. The disease began with fatigue and swollen, bleeding gums, and in its later stages old wounds could reopen and victims could die. Some historians estimate that it killed more seamen during the age of sail than storms, shipwrecks and battles combined, although reliable figures are difficult to obtain.
In 1747, the Scottish naval surgeon James Lind carried out what is often described as one of the first controlled clinical trials. On board a British warship, he selected twelve sailors with scurvy whose symptoms were as similar as possible and divided them into six pairs. Each pair received a different supplement to the same basic diet, including cider, vinegar, seawater and a daily ration of oranges and lemons. The two men given citrus fruit recovered so rapidly that one was fit for duty within about a week, while the others improved little, if at all.
Surprisingly, Lind's result did not lead to an immediate change in naval practice. In his own writings, he presented citrus fruit as only one of several possible remedies and continued to believe that scurvy had multiple causes, including damp air. Moreover, attempts to preserve lemon juice by heating it, which we now know destroys much of the active substance, produced inconsistent results that made the treatment seem unreliable. It was not until 1795 that the British navy began routinely issuing lemon juice to its sailors, and the underlying cause of the disease, a lack of vitamin C, was identified only in the twentieth century.
The story is often told as a simple triumph of experimental medicine, but it also shows how difficult it can be for even well-founded findings to change established practice.

Beslenmenin tamamen ‘citrus fruit’ olduğu söylenmez; denizcilerin başta iskorbüt belirtisi taşıdığı belirtildiği için ‘no symptoms’ yanlıştır; bir haftada yalnızca bir denizcinin göreve döndüğü, diğerlerinin pek iyileşmediği söylendiğinden ‘all recovered’ yanlıştır; deney tek bir savaş gemisinde yapılmıştır, ‘several different ships’ değil.

questions.passage:
Lena: I read that the council plans to turn the old car park by the river into a public garden.
Omar: Yes, and apparently local residents will be invited to help design it.
Lena: ----
Omar: Probably not, but asking people what they want usually makes them more likely to look after the place once it's finished.
Lena: That makes sense; people tend to care for what they have helped to create.
questions.text: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Do you really think ordinary residents have the expertise to design a garden?
When was the car park originally built?
How many cars can the car park hold at the moment?
Isn't the river too polluted for swimming?
Who will pay for the new bridge across the river?
questions.explanation: Omar ‘Probably not’ diye yanıt verip ardından halka danışmanın yararını anlatır; bu yanıt, sakinlerin bahçe tasarlayacak uzmanlığa sahip olup olmadığını sorgulayan soruya uyar. Otoparkın ne zaman ‘built’ edildiği, kaç araç alabildiği (‘hold’), nehrin yüzmek için ‘polluted’ olup olmadığı ya da köprünün parasını kimin ödeyeceği soruları Omar'ın yanıtıyla bağlantılı değildir.

questions.passage:
Student: Professor, why do astronomers build so many telescopes on remote mountain tops?
Professor: Mainly to get above as much of the atmosphere as possible.
Student: ----
Professor: Because the air bends and blurs the light from stars, and the higher you go, the less air there is to look through.
Student: I see. So that's also why some telescopes are sent into space.
questions.text: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: How long does it take to build such a telescope?
Isn't it very cold to work at such heights?
Who built the first telescope?
Do astronomers ever use telescopes during the day?
Why does the atmosphere matter so much for observations?
questions.explanation: Profesörün ‘Because’ ile başlayan yanıtı havanın yıldız ışığını büktüğünü ve bulanıklaştırdığını açıklar; bu, atmosferin gözlem için neden bu kadar önemli olduğunu soran soruya karşılık gelir. Teleskobun ne kadar sürede ‘build’ edildiği, yükseklikte ‘cold’ olup olmadığı, ilk teleskobu kimin yaptığı ya da gündüz ‘during the day’ kullanılıp kullanılmadığı soruları bu açıklamayla yanıtlanmaz.

questions.passage:
Manager: Our staff survey shows that many employees feel their work isn't appreciated.
HR Director: That's worrying. Have you checked whether it's linked to pay?
Manager: ----
HR Director: Then perhaps we should start by training managers to give more regular feedback.
Manager: Good idea. I'll ask the training team to prepare a short course.
questions.text: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Yes, and most of them told us that a significant pay rise is the only thing that would help.
The survey was sent to every department in March.
I'm afraid I'll be on holiday for most of next week.
Most of our employees have worked here for more than five years.
We did, but what most of them said they missed was recognition from their supervisors, not money.
questions.explanation: İK direktörünün ‘Then’ ile önerdiği çözüm, yöneticilerin daha düzenli geri bildirim vermesidir; bu öneri, çalışanların paradan çok amirlerinden takdir görmeyi özlediğini söyleyen yanıttan doğar. Çalışanların yalnızca ‘pay rise’ istediğini söyleyen yanıt geri bildirim önerisine gerekçe oluşturmaz; anketin ‘March’ ayında gönderilmesi, yöneticinin ‘holiday’ planı ya da çalışanların ‘five years’ kıdemi de önerinin nedeni olamaz.

questions.passage:
Patient: Doctor, my grandmother always says you should feed a cold and starve a fever. Is there any truth in that?
Doctor: Not really. ----
Patient: So I should keep eating normally even if I have a temperature?
Doctor: As far as you can, yes, and above all drink plenty of fluids.
questions.text: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Whether you have a cold or a fever, your body needs energy and fluids to fight the infection.
Colds are caused by viruses, so antibiotics won't help you.
You should avoid eating anything until your temperature returns to normal.
Your grandmother must be very proud of you.
Fevers are much more common in winter than in summer.
questions.explanation: Hasta, ateşi olsa bile normal yemeye devam etmesi gerektiği sonucunu çıkarır; bu çıkarım, soğuk algınlığında da ateşte de vücudun enerji ve sıvıya ihtiyaç duyduğunu söyleyen yanıttan gelir. ‘Antibiotics’ ile ilgili bilgi yemek konusunu açıklamaz; ateş düşene kadar yemekten ‘avoid’ edilmesini öneren yanıt hastanın çıkarımıyla çelişir; büyükannenin ‘proud’ olması ve ateşin ‘winter’ aylarında yaygınlığı da konuyla ilgisizdir.

questions.passage:
Journalist: Your research on Renaissance paintings has attracted a lot of attention. What exactly did you find?
Art historian: We discovered that several well-known works had been painted over an earlier composition.
Journalist: ----
Art historian: With infrared imaging, which allows us to see the layers beneath the visible paint without damaging the picture.
Journalist: That's remarkable. Do you know why the artists changed their minds?
questions.text: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Why did the museum decide to sell those paintings?
Which painter do you personally admire the most?
When will the exhibition open to the public?
How were you able to see what lies underneath without harming the paintings?
Were the paintings stolen from the museum at some point?
questions.explanation: Sanat tarihçisi ‘With infrared imaging’ diyerek bir yöntem açıklar ve resme zarar vermeden alttaki katmanları görebildiklerini söyler; bu, alttakini tabloya zarar vermeden nasıl görebildiklerini soran soruya uyar. Müzenin tabloları neden ‘sell’ ettiği, en çok hangi ressamı ‘admire’ ettiği, sergi ‘exhibition’ tarihi ya da tabloların ‘stolen’ edilip edilmediği soruları bir yöntemle yanıtlanmaz.

questions.passage:
Farmer: This year's harvest was much better than last year's, even though we had less rain.
Agronomist: That's probably because you started leaving the stubble from the previous crop on the fields.
Farmer: ----
Agronomist: It acts like a blanket, so less water evaporates from the soil and more is left for the plants.
Farmer: Then I'll certainly keep doing it next year.
questions.text: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Should I sell my harvest now or wait until prices rise?
How could leaving stubble make any difference to how much water the crops get?
Do you think it will rain more next year?
Which crop would you recommend planting instead?
Isn't stubble a good source of food for farm animals?
questions.explanation: Agronomun yanıtı anızın bir battaniye gibi davranarak topraktan buharlaşmayı azalttığını açıklar; bu, anız bırakmanın bitkilerin aldığı su miktarını nasıl etkilediğini soran soruya karşılık gelir. Ürünü ne zaman ‘sell’ etmesi gerektiği, gelecek yıl daha çok ‘rain’ yağıp yağmayacağı, hangi ürünün ‘instead’ ekileceği ya da anızın hayvanlar için ‘food’ olup olmadığı soruları bu açıklamayla yanıtlanmaz.

questions.text:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

No sooner had the new metro line opened than property prices in the surrounding districts began to rise.
options: Property prices around the new metro line had begun rising long before it opened.
Although the new metro line opened, property prices in the surrounding districts did not rise.
The new metro line was opened because property prices in the surrounding districts were rising.
Property prices rose so much that the opening of the new metro line had to be delayed.
Property prices in the districts around the new metro line started to rise as soon as it opened.
questions.explanation: ‘No sooner … than’ (… -er -mez) iki olayın hemen ardı ardına gerçekleştiğini anlatır: Metro hattı açılır açılmaz çevredeki konut fiyatları yükselmeye başlamıştır; ‘as soon as’ aynı anlamı verir. Fiyatların açılıştan ‘long before’ yükseldiğini ya da hiç yükselmediğini (‘did not rise’) söyleyen cümleler anlamı değiştirir; hattın fiyatlar yükseldiği ‘because’ açıldığını ya da açılışın ‘delayed’ edildiğini söyleyen cümleler ise olmayan bir neden-sonuç ilişkisi kurar.

questions.text:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

Contrary to popular belief, it is not the number of hours employees work but how they use those hours that determines their productivity.
options: As most people believe, employees who work longer hours are generally the most productive.
Employees cannot be productive unless they work a large number of hours.
Employees work fewer hours today, which has reduced their overall productivity.
Although many people think otherwise, employees' productivity depends more on how they use their working time than on how long they work.
How long employees work and how they use their time are equally important for productivity.
questions.explanation: ‘Contrary to popular belief’ (yaygın inancın aksine) ve ‘not … but …’ yapısı, verimliliği belirleyenin çalışılan saat sayısı değil bu saatlerin nasıl kullanıldığı olduğunu anlatır; ‘Although many people think otherwise’ ile başlayan cümle bunu doğru aktarır. ‘Longer hours’ çalışanların en verimli olduğunu ya da çok saat çalışmadan (‘unless’) verimli olunamayacağını söyleyen cümleler anlamı tersine çevirir; ‘fewer hours today’ yeni bir bilgi ekler; ‘equally important’ ise ‘not … but’ yapısındaki ayrımı ortadan kaldırır.

questions.text:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

But for the timely intervention of local volunteers, many of the manuscripts would have been destroyed in the flood.
options: Local volunteers intervened too late to save the manuscripts from the flood.
Many manuscripts were destroyed in the flood although local volunteers intervened in time.
Many of the manuscripts survived the flood only because local volunteers intervened in time.
The flood destroyed the manuscripts before local volunteers could reach them.
If local volunteers had not been warned in time, they would not have intervened during the flood.
questions.explanation: ‘But for’ (… olmasaydı) yapısı gerçekleşmemiş bir durumu anlatır: Gönüllüler zamanında müdahale etmeseydi elyazmalarının çoğu yok olacaktı; yani elyazmaları gönüllüler sayesinde kurtulmuştur. Gönüllülerin ‘too late’ kaldığını, elyazmalarının yine de ‘destroyed’ edildiğini ya da gönüllüler ‘reach’ edemeden yok olduğunu söyleyen cümleler gerçeği tersine çevirir; gönüllülerin ‘warned’ edilmesiyle kurulan koşul ise özgün cümlede yoktur.

questions.passage: Since ancient times, observers have noticed that the planets wander across the sky against the background of the fixed stars. For centuries, the dominant explanation placed the Earth at the centre of the universe, with the Sun, the Moon and the planets moving around it. This model was refined into an elaborate system of circles within circles that could predict planetary positions reasonably well. ---- Copernicus's proposal that the Earth and the other planets revolve around the Sun offered a simpler alternative, although it took more than a century and the telescopic observations of Galileo to win general acceptance.
questions.text: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Galileo was born in Pisa in 1564 and later taught mathematics at Padua.
The Moon has a much weaker gravitational pull than the Earth.
Yet as observations became more precise, the system needed ever more adjustments to match what astronomers actually saw.
Modern telescopes can detect planets orbiting distant stars.
Therefore, astronomers abandoned observation entirely and relied on philosophy alone.
questions.explanation: Boşluktan önce Dünya merkezli modelin oldukça iyi tahminler yaptığı, sonra ise Kopernik'in daha basit bir alternatif sunduğu söylenir; arada modelin giderek daha fazla düzeltme gerektirdiğini belirten ‘Yet …’ cümlesi bu geçişi sağlar ve ‘simpler’ sözcüğünü anlamlı kılar. Galileo'nun ‘Pisa’ doğumlu olması, Ay'ın ‘gravitational pull’ gücü ve modern teleskopların ‘distant stars’ çevresindeki gezegenleri bulması akışı bozar; gözlemin tamamen bırakılıp ‘philosophy’ ile yetinildiği ise yanlış ve mantıksız bir sonuçtur.

questions.passage: In many offices, meetings take up a growing share of the working week. ---- Studies of knowledge workers suggest that frequent interruptions make it difficult to concentrate on complex tasks, since it can take a considerable amount of time to regain full focus after each break. For this reason, some companies have introduced meeting-free days, giving employees long, uninterrupted periods in which to work.
questions.text: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Although meetings can improve coordination, too many of them may leave employees with little time for focused work.
Most office buildings now have at least one large conference room.
Video conferencing became widespread during the early 2020s.
Employees who attend meetings are usually paid more than those who do not.
Consequently, meeting-free days have reduced the number of employees in many companies.
questions.explanation: Boşluktan sonra sık kesintilerin odaklanmayı zorlaştırdığı ve bu yüzden toplantısız günler getirildiği anlatılır; bu nedenle boşluğa çok sayıda toplantının odaklanılmış çalışmaya az zaman bıraktığını söyleyen cümle gelmelidir. Ofislerdeki ‘conference room’ sayısı, görüntülü görüşmenin ‘2020s’ yıllarında yaygınlaşması ve toplantıya katılanların daha çok ‘paid’ edilmesi konunun akışına bağlanmaz; ‘Consequently’ ile başlayan cümle ise toplantısız günlerden henüz söz edilmeden sonuç bildirir ve çalışan sayısıyla ilgisizdir.

questions.passage: Medieval European artists generally showed little interest in creating the illusion of depth on a flat surface. Figures were often arranged according to their importance rather than their position in space, so that a saint might appear much larger than the buildings around him. ---- By using lines that converge on a single point on the horizon, painters could make a flat wall appear to open onto a three-dimensional room. Within a few decades, this technique had become a standard part of artistic training throughout Italy.
questions.text: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Many medieval paintings were commissioned by monasteries and churches.
Saints were often shown holding objects associated with their lives.
This began to change in early fifteenth-century Florence, where artists and architects worked out the rules of linear perspective.
Oil paint was used mainly in northern Europe at that time.
As a result, Italian artists refused to paint buildings at all.
questions.explanation: Boşluktan önce Orta Çağ sanatçılarının derinlik yanılsamasıyla ilgilenmediği, sonra ise ufuktaki tek bir noktada birleşen çizgilerle derinlik yaratıldığı anlatılır; arada bu durumun on beşinci yüzyıl Floransa'sında doğrusal perspektifle değiştiğini söyleyen cümle geçişi sağlar ve ‘this technique’ ifadesine gönderme noktası oluşturur. Resimlerin ‘monasteries’ tarafından ısmarlanması, azizlerin ‘objects’ taşıması ve ‘oil paint’ kullanımı derinlik konusunu sürdürmez; İtalyan sanatçıların bina çizmeyi ‘refused’ ettiğini söyleyen cümle ise paragrafla çelişir.

questions.passage: In the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, patients with tuberculosis were often sent to sanatoriums, institutions usually built in the mountains or the countryside. There, they followed a strict routine of rest, nourishing food and long hours in the fresh air, sometimes even sleeping on open balconies in winter. ---- Nonetheless, sanatoriums may have played a valuable role in public health by separating infectious patients from their families and communities.
questions.text: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Whether this regime actually cured many patients is doubtful, as the disease often returned after they went home.
Tuberculosis is caused by a bacterium that mainly attacks the lungs.
Mountain air is generally colder and drier than air at sea level.
Many sanatoriums were later converted into hotels or private clinics.
Therefore, most sanatoriums were closed soon after they opened.
questions.explanation: Boşluktan sonraki ‘Nonetheless’ (yine de) bağlacı, sanatoryumların değerli bir rol oynamış olabileceğini önceki olumsuz bir bilgiyle karşılaştırır; bu yüzden boşluğa bu rejimin hastaları gerçekten iyileştirip iyileştirmediğinin şüpheli olduğunu söyleyen cümle gelmelidir. Hastalığın bir ‘bacterium’ ile yayıldığı, dağ havasının ‘colder’ olduğu ve binaların ‘hotels’ olarak kullanıldığı bilgileri ‘Nonetheless’ ile bir zıtlık oluşturmaz; sanatoryumların hemen ‘closed’ edildiğini söyleyen cümle ise paragrafla çelişir.

questions.passage: (I) During sleep, the brain does not simply switch off but actively processes the experiences of the day. (II) In particular, the hippocampus appears to replay patterns of activity recorded during learning, helping to transfer new memories to longer-term storage in the cortex. (III) Experiments with rats have shown that the sequences of nerve-cell activity observed while the animals explored a maze are repeated, in compressed form, during subsequent sleep. (IV) The hippocampus was named after the Greek word for seahorse because of its curved shape. (V) When this replay is disrupted, the animals perform worse when they are tested on the maze the next day.
questions.text: Paragrafta anlam bütünlüğünü bozan cümle hangisidir?
options: I
II
III
IV
V
questions.explanation: Paragraf uykuda beynin günün deneyimlerini işlediğini, hipokampüsün öğrenme sırasındaki etkinliği yeniden oynattığını ve bu süreç bozulunca farelerin labirent performansının düştüğünü anlatır. IV numaralı cümle hipokampüsün adının kökenine geçerek bellek ve uyku konusundan sapar. I konuyu tanıtır, II ve III yeniden oynatma sürecini açıklar, V ise ‘this replay’ ifadesiyle doğrudan III'e bağlanır.

questions.passage: (I) Many cities now offer grants to residents who install solar panels on their roofs. (II) Green roofs, which are covered with soil and vegetation, are becoming an increasingly common feature of urban buildings. (III) By absorbing rainwater, they reduce the pressure on drainage systems during heavy storms. (IV) Their plants also cool the surrounding air through evaporation, which can help to lower temperatures in densely built neighbourhoods. (V) In addition, green roofs provide habitats for insects and birds that would otherwise find little space in the city.
questions.text: Paragrafta anlam bütünlüğünü bozan cümle hangisidir?
options: I
II
III
IV
V
questions.explanation: Paragraf yeşil çatıların (green roofs) yağmur suyunu emme, havayı serinletme ve canlılara yaşam alanı sağlama gibi yararlarını anlatır. I numaralı cümle güneş paneli kuran sakinlere verilen hibelerden söz ederek çatılarla ilgili olsa da yeşil çatı konusunun dışında kalır. II konuyu tanıtır; III ve IV ‘they’ ve ‘Their plants’ ifadeleriyle yeşil çatılara gönderme yapar; V ise ‘In addition’ ile yeni bir yarar ekler.

questions.passage: (I) On steep hillsides, farmers in many parts of the world have long built terraces, flat steps cut into the slope and supported by walls of stone or earth. (II) By slowing the flow of water downhill, terraces reduce soil erosion and allow rain to soak into the ground. (III) They also make it possible to grow crops such as rice, which need level fields that can be flooded. (IV) However, terraces require constant maintenance, and when they are abandoned, their walls can collapse within a few years and trigger landslides. (V) Rice, which is grown on many of these terraces, is thought to have been domesticated in China several thousand years ago.
questions.text: Paragrafta anlam bütünlüğünü bozan cümle hangisidir?
options: I
II
III
IV
V
questions.explanation: Paragraf yamaçlardaki teraslı tarımı, terasların erozyonu azaltma ve düz tarla sağlama yararlarını ve bakım gerektirme sorununu anlatır. V numaralı cümle terasları anarak başlasa da pirincin evcilleştirilme tarihine geçer ve terasların işleviyle ilgisizdir. I konuyu tanıtır, II ve III yararları sıralar, IV ise ‘However’ ile terasların sakıncasını ekleyerek bütünlüğü sürdürür.

questions.passage: (I) Detecting forgeries has become an important task for museums and auction houses, as the prices paid for famous works of art have risen sharply. (II) One of the most reliable methods involves analysing the materials used, since a forger may unknowingly use a pigment that was not yet available when the work was supposedly painted. (III) Many famous painters spent years as apprentices in the workshops of older masters before working independently. (IV) Experts can also examine the canvas, the wooden frame and the layers of varnish, all of which change with age in characteristic ways. (V) Even so, some skilled forgers have managed to deceive specialists for decades.
questions.text: Paragrafta anlam bütünlüğünü bozan cümle hangisidir?
options: I
II
