IV
V
questions.explanation: Paragraf sahte sanat eserlerinin nasıl tespit edildiğini, malzeme analizini ve tuval, çerçeve ve vernik incelemesini anlatır. III numaralı cümle ünlü ressamların usta yanında çıraklık yapmasından söz ederek sanat tarihiyle ilgili olsa da sahtecilik tespiti konusundan sapar. I konuyu tanıtır, II ve IV (‘also’) yöntemleri sıralar, V ise ‘Even so’ ile bu yöntemlerin sınırını belirtir.

questions.passage: (I) Over the past fifteen years, digital platforms have allowed millions of people to earn money by delivering food, driving passengers or completing small online tasks. (II) Some of these platforms have become among the most valuable technology companies in the world, attracting billions in investment. (III) Supporters argue that such work offers flexibility, allowing people to choose when and how much they work. (IV) Critics, however, point out that platform workers are usually classified as self-employed and therefore lack benefits such as sick pay and pensions. (V) In response, courts in several countries have begun to examine whether some of these workers should in fact be treated as employees.
questions.text: Paragrafta anlam bütünlüğünü bozan cümle hangisidir?
options: I
II
III
IV
V
questions.explanation: Paragraf dijital platformlarda çalışan insanların durumunu, bu işin esneklik gibi yararlarını, çalışanların sosyal haklardan yoksun kalmasını ve mahkemelerin bu konuyu incelemesini anlatır. II numaralı cümle platform şirketlerinin piyasa değerine ve yatırımlara geçerek çalışanların koşulları konusundan sapar. I konuyu tanıtır, III ve IV destekçi ve eleştirmen görüşlerini karşılaştırır, V ise ‘In response’ ile IV'teki eleştiriye bağlanır.

questions.text: Although the two species of frog look almost identical, genetic analysis has shown that they ---- from a common ancestor more than five million years ago.
options: persisted
retrieved
diverged
dissolved
endorsed
questions.explanation: ‘Diverged’ (ayrıldı, farklılaştı) iki türün ortak bir atadan ayrılarak ayrı yollar izlediğini anlatır; ‘from a common ancestor’ ifadesi bu fiili gerektirir. ‘Persisted’ (sürdü), ‘retrieved’ (geri aldı), ‘dissolved’ (çözündü) ve ‘endorsed’ (onayladı) ortak atadan ayrılma anlamını vermez.

questions.text: The committee's report was widely criticised for being ----, as it offered general recommendations but no concrete measures that governments could actually implement.
options: meticulous
hostile
fragile
abundant
vague
questions.explanation: ‘Vague’ (belirsiz, muğlak) raporun genel öneriler sunup somut önlem içermemesini tam olarak niteler. ‘Meticulous’ (titiz) olumlu bir özelliktir ve eleştiriyle çelişir; ‘hostile’ (düşmanca), ‘fragile’ (kırılgan) ve ‘abundant’ (bol) somut önlem eksikliğiyle ilgili değildir.

questions.text: Life expectancy has risen ---- over the past century, largely as a result of improvements in sanitation, nutrition and vaccination.
options: considerably
reluctantly
deliberately
politely
vaguely
questions.explanation: ‘Considerably’ (önemli ölçüde) yaşam süresindeki artışın büyüklüğünü anlatır ve temizlik, beslenme, aşılama gibi gelişmelerle uyumludur. ‘Reluctantly’ (isteksizce), ‘deliberately’ (kasıtlı olarak) ve ‘politely’ (kibarca) bilinçli bir öznenin davranışını niteler; ‘vaguely’ (belli belirsiz) ise bir artışın miktarını anlatmaz.

questions.text: The negotiations were ---- after the two delegations failed to agree on even the most basic issues, and no further meetings have been scheduled.
options: made up
broken off
looked after
taken over
turned up
questions.explanation: ‘Broken off’ (kesildi, yarıda bırakıldı) heyetlerin anlaşamaması ve yeni toplantı planlanmamasıyla uyumludur. ‘Made up’ (uyduruldu ya da barışıldı), ‘looked after’ (bakıldı), ‘taken over’ (devralındı) ve ‘turned up’ (ortaya çıktı) görüşmelerin sona ermesi anlamını vermez.

questions.text: Because the evidence against the suspect was largely ----, the court could not convict him, even though many observers were convinced of his guilt.
options: conclusive
circumstantial
compulsory
spontaneous
excessive
questions.explanation: ‘Circumstantial’ (dolaylı, ikinci derece) kanıtın mahkûmiyete yetmediğini açıklar. ‘Conclusive’ (kesin) kanıt mahkûmiyeti mümkün kılacağından cümleyle çelişir; ‘compulsory’ (zorunlu), ‘spontaneous’ (kendiliğinden) ve ‘excessive’ (aşırı) kanıtın niteliğini bu bağlamda anlamlı biçimde anlatmaz.

questions.text: ---- its small size, the island supports an extraordinary variety of plant species, many of which are found nowhere else on Earth.
options: Owing to
Instead of
On behalf of
As a result of
Despite
questions.explanation: ‘Despite’ (-e rağmen) adanın küçüklüğü ile tür zenginliği arasındaki zıtlığı kurar. ‘Owing to’ ve ‘As a result of’ küçüklüğü zenginliğin nedeni yapar ki bu mantıksızdır; ‘Instead of’ (yerine) ve ‘On behalf of’ (adına) cümlede anlamlı bir ilişki kurmaz.

questions.text: Since the first commercial wind farm opened in 1980, the cost of electricity generated from wind ---- by more than 80 per cent.
options: fell
had fallen
is falling
has fallen
was falling
questions.explanation: ‘Since + geçmişteki bir başlangıç’ yapısı geçmişten bugüne uzanan bir süreci anlatır ve present perfect gerektirir: ‘has fallen’. ‘Fell’ ve ‘was falling’ geçmişte bitmiş bir zamana bağlanır; ‘had fallen’ geçmişteki başka bir andan öncesini anlatır; ‘is falling’ ise ‘since’ ile kurulan toplam değişimi vermez.

questions.text: The ancient bridge ---- by Roman engineers, as the techniques used in its construction were unknown in the region before the Roman conquest.
options: should have built
can't have been built
had to build
might build
must have been built
questions.explanation: Cümle eldeki kanıta dayanarak geçmişe ilişkin güçlü bir çıkarım yapar ve köprü inşa edilen nesne olduğu için edilgen gerekir: ‘must have been built’. ‘Can't have been built’ kanıtla çelişen bir sonuç çıkarır; ‘should have built’ ve ‘had to build’ etken yapıdadır ve köprüyü özne yapar; ‘might build’ ise geleceğe ya da olasılığa yöneliktir.

questions.text: The researchers interviewed more than 2,000 adults, most of ---- reported sleeping fewer than seven hours a night.
options: whom
who
them
which
whose
questions.explanation: ‘Most of’ gibi miktar ifadelerinden sonra insanlar için ilgi zamiri ‘whom’ kullanılır: ‘most of whom’. ‘Who’ edattan sonra gelmez; ‘them’ iki cümleyi bağlayamaz ve cümleyi bozuk bırakır; ‘which’ insanlar için kullanılmaz; ‘whose’ ise ardından bir isim ister.

questions.text: If governments ---- more heavily in renewable energy several decades ago, the world would now be far less dependent on fossil fuels.
options: invested
have invested
had invested
would invest
were investing
questions.explanation: Geçmişteki bir koşulun bugünkü sonucunu anlatan karma koşul cümlesidir; ‘several decades ago’ geçmişi gösterdiği için koşul kısmında past perfect gerekir: ‘had invested’. ‘Invested’ ve ‘were investing’ bugüne ilişkin gerçek dışı koşul kurar; ‘have invested’ koşul yapısına uymaz; ‘would invest’ ise koşul kısmında kullanılmaz.

questions.text: Many patients stop ---- their antibiotics as soon as they feel better, which can allow the infection to return in a more resistant form.
options: to take
take
having been taken
being taken
taking
questions.explanation: ‘Stop + -ing’ bir eylemi bırakmak anlamına gelir: hastalar antibiyotik almayı bırakır, yani ‘taking’ gerekir. ‘To take’ ile ‘stop to take’ almak için durmak anlamı verir ve bağlama ters düşer; ‘take’ yalın hâlde ‘stop’ ardından gelmez; ‘having been taken’ ve ‘being taken’ edilgendir, oysa ilacı alan hastalardır.

questions.text: ---- the experiment was repeated several times under carefully controlled conditions, the results remained inconsistent, suggesting a fault in the equipment.
options: Because
Unless
So that
Even though
As soon as
questions.explanation: Deneyin özenle defalarca tekrarlanmasına karşın sonuçların tutarsız kalması bir zıtlıktır; bu nedenle ‘Even though’ gerekir. ‘Because’ neden-sonuç kurar ve mantıksızdır; ‘Unless’ olumsuz koşul, ‘So that’ amaç bildirir; ‘As soon as’ ise zıtlık yerine zaman ilişkisi kurar.

questions.text: The new vaccine is not only cheaper to produce but also ---- than the earlier version, since it does not need to be kept frozen.
options: much easier to transport
the easiest to transport
as easy to transport
more easily transport
easy enough transport
questions.explanation: Cümledeki ‘than’ karşılaştırma sıfatı ister; ‘much’ farkı vurgular: ‘much easier to transport’. ‘The easiest’ üstünlük derecesidir ve ‘than’ ile kullanılmaz; ‘as easy’ yapısı ikinci ‘as’ ister; ‘more easily transport’ ve ‘easy enough transport’ dil bilgisi bakımından bozuktur.

questions.text: The success of the reforestation programme will depend largely ---- the willingness of local communities to protect the young trees.
options: in
for
with
at
on
questions.explanation: ‘Depend’ fiili ‘on’ edatıyla kullanılır: ‘depend largely on’ (büyük ölçüde -e bağlı olmak). ‘In’, ‘for’, ‘with’ ve ‘at’ bu fiille kalıp oluşturmaz.

questions.text: Not until the late nineteenth century ---- that many infectious diseases are caused by microorganisms.
options: most scientists accepted
did most scientists accept
had most scientists been accepted
most scientists did accept
accepting most scientists
questions.explanation: ‘Not until’ ile başlayan cümlede ana cümlede devrik yapı gerekir: ‘did most scientists accept’. ‘Most scientists accepted’ ve ‘most scientists did accept’ düz sıradadır; ‘had most scientists been accepted’ edilgendir ve bilim insanlarını kabul edilen yapar; ‘accepting most scientists’ ise çekimli fiil içermez.

questions.text: The panel recommended that every new public building ---- with a system for collecting and storing rainwater.
options: equips
be equipped
was equipping
will equip
has equipped
questions.explanation: ‘Recommend that’ ardından yalın fiil (subjunctive) gelir; bina donatılan nesne olduğu için edilgen gerekir: ‘be equipped’. ‘Equips’, ‘was equipping’, ‘will equip’ ve ‘has equipped’ etkendir, binayı donatan özne yapar ve öneri yapısına uymaz.

questions.passage: In the dry regions of Iran, people have relied for thousands of years on qanats, underground channels that carry water from mountain aquifers to villages and fields far below. A qanat begins with a vertical "mother well" dug at the foot of a hill, where workers must first confirm that the water table is (1) ---- high to supply a steady flow. From there, a gently sloping tunnel is excavated towards the surface, with additional shafts dug at regular intervals to remove soil and allow fresh air (2) ---- the diggers. Because the water flows by gravity alone, the system requires no pumps, and since the channel runs underground, very little water is lost to evaporation (3) ---- the intense summer heat. Some qanats (4) ---- for many centuries and still supply water today. In recent decades, however, many have dried up, (5) ---- the spread of motorised wells has lowered groundwater levels across the region.
questions.text: (1) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: scarcely
excessively
such
so much
sufficiently
questions.explanation: İşçiler su seviyesinin düzenli akış sağlayacak kadar yüksek olduğunu doğrulamalıdır; ‘sufficiently high’ (yeterince yüksek) bunu anlatır. ‘Scarcely’ (neredeyse hiç) anlamı tersine çevirir; ‘excessively’ (aşırı) istenmeyen bir durumu anlatır; ‘such’ sıfattan önce tek başına gelmez; ‘so much’ ise sıfatı nitelemez.

questions.text: (2) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: reaching
reached
reach
to reach
having reached
questions.explanation: ‘Allow + nesne + to-infinitive’ kalıbı gerekir: ‘allow fresh air to reach the diggers’ (temiz havanın kazıcılara ulaşmasına izin vermek). ‘Reaching’, ‘reached’, ‘reach’ ve ‘having reached’ bu kalıba uymaz.

questions.text: (3) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: owing to
instead of
apart from
according to
despite
questions.explanation: Yoğun yaz sıcağı buharlaşmayı artırmalıdır, ancak kanal yer altında olduğu için çok az su kaybedilir; bu zıtlığı ‘despite’ kurar. ‘Owing to’ sıcağı az kaybın nedeni yapar ki mantıksızdır; ‘instead of’, ‘apart from’ ve ‘according to’ cümlede anlamlı bir ilişki kurmaz.

questions.text: (4) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: had operated
are operated
have been operating
would operate
operate
questions.explanation: ‘For many centuries’ ve ‘still supply water today’ ifadeleri geçmişte başlayıp bugüne süren bir eylemi anlatır; bu nedenle ‘have been operating’ gerekir. ‘Had operated’ geçmişteki bir andan öncesini anlatır; ‘are operated’ edilgendir ve süreyi vermez; ‘would operate’ ve ‘operate’ ise bugüne uzanan süreyi ifade etmez.

questions.text: (5) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: unless
although
so that
as
until
questions.explanation: Kanatların kuruması, motorlu kuyuların yeraltı suyunu düşürmesinin sonucudur; neden bildiren ‘as’ (çünkü) gerekir. ‘Unless’ koşul, ‘although’ zıtlık, ‘so that’ amaç, ‘until’ ise zaman sınırı bildirir ve neden-sonuç ilişkisini kurmaz.

questions.passage: Long before scientists understood how it worked, observers had noticed that many plants open and close their leaves according to a daily schedule. In 1729, the French astronomer Jean-Jacques d'Ortous de Mairan placed a mimosa plant in a dark cupboard and found that its leaves continued to open and fold at roughly the usual times, (1) ---- the plant could no longer detect sunlight. This simple experiment suggested that the rhythm was (2) ---- by something inside the plant rather than by the environment alone. Modern research has confirmed that plants possess a molecular clock (3) ---- several genes switch one another on and off in a cycle lasting about 24 hours. This clock allows a plant to anticipate dawn, (4) ---- the machinery needed for photosynthesis before the sun actually rises. Experiments have shown that plants whose internal clocks match the length of the external day tend to grow faster and survive better than those (5) ---- clocks are out of step with it.
questions.text: (1) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: so that
even though
in case
unless
as long as
questions.explanation: Bitki güneş ışığını algılayamamasına rağmen yapraklar her zamanki saatlerde açılıp kapanmaya devam etmiştir; bu zıtlığı ‘even though’ kurar. ‘So that’ amaç, ‘in case’ önlem, ‘unless’ olumsuz koşul, ‘as long as’ ise koşul bildirir ve zıtlık anlamı vermez.

questions.text: (2) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: prevented
generated
abandoned
concealed
rejected
questions.explanation: Deney ritmin çevreden çok bitkinin içindeki bir şey tarafından üretildiğini gösterir; ‘generated’ (üretilmiş, oluşturulmuş) bu anlamı verir. ‘Prevented’ (engellenmiş), ‘abandoned’ (terk edilmiş), ‘concealed’ (gizlenmiş) ve ‘rejected’ (reddedilmiş) ritmin kaynağını anlatmaz.

questions.text: (3) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: what
in which
whose
whom
that
questions.explanation: Boşluktan sonra öznesi ve nesnesi tam bir cümle gelir (several genes switch one another on and off); saati niteleyen ve ‘içinde’ anlamı veren ‘in which’ gerekir. ‘What’ isimden sonra ilgi zamiri olarak kullanılmaz; ‘whose’ ardından sahip olunan bir isim ister; ‘whom’ insanlar içindir; ‘that’ ise eksiksiz bir cümleyi bağlayamaz.

questions.text: (4) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: prepared
prepares
having been prepared
to be prepared
preparing
questions.explanation: Virgülden sonra gelen ve aynı özneye (bitki) bağlı eşzamanlı eylemi anlatan etken ortaç gerekir: ‘preparing the machinery’ (düzeneği hazırlayarak). ‘Prepared’ ve ‘having been prepared’ edilgen anlam taşır; ‘prepares’ bağlaçsız çekimli fiildir; ‘to be prepared’ ise edilgendir ve nesneyi alamaz.

This clock allows a plant to anticipate dawn, (4) ---- the machinery needed for photosynthesis before the sun actually rises. Experiments have shown that plants whose internal clocks match the length of the external day tend to grow faster and survive better than those (5) ---- clocks are out of step with it.
questions.text: (5) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: whose
which
that
whom
what
questions.explanation: ‘Those’ bitkileri gösterir ve ardından gelen ‘clocks’ bu bitkilere aittir; iyelik bildiren ‘whose’ gerekir. ‘Which’ ve ‘that’ ardından isim alıp iyelik bildiremez; ‘whom’ insanlar içindir; ‘what’ ise ilgi zamiri olarak isimden sonra kullanılmaz.

questions.text: Unless farmers receive financial support during the transition to organic methods, ----.
options: organic food had become increasingly popular in cities
many of them will be unable to survive the initial fall in yields
since the use of chemical fertilisers is declining
which is why the government introduced subsidies
although consumers would pay higher prices
questions.explanation: ‘Unless’ ile kurulan gerçek koşul cümlesi gelecek zamanlı bir ana cümle ister: Destek almazlarsa çiftçilerin çoğu verimdeki ilk düşüşü atlatamayacaktır. Organik gıdanın ‘popular’ olduğunu söyleyen seçenek koşulla bağlantısızdır ve zamanı uyumsuzdur; ‘since’ ve ‘although’ ile başlayanlar ana cümle oluşturmaz; ‘subsidies’ ile biten ilgi cümlesi de ana cümle değildir.

questions.text: The museum's collection of early maps is so fragile that ----.
options: only a small part of it can be displayed at any one time
the maps were drawn by sailors and merchants
because light can damage old paper
as if they had been printed recently
than any other collection in the country
questions.explanation: ‘So … that’ (o kadar … ki) yapısı sonuç ister: Koleksiyon o kadar kırılgandır ki aynı anda yalnızca küçük bir kısmı sergilenebilir. Haritaları ‘sailors’ ve tüccarların çizdiği bilgisi sonuç bildirmez; ‘because’ ile başlayan seçenek ‘that’ ardından gelemez; ‘printed’ içeren ‘as if’ yapısı ve ‘than’ ile kurulan karşılaştırma da ‘so … that’ kalıbını tamamlamaz.

questions.text: ----, the researchers were unable to determine whether the treatment had any long-term benefits.
options: As long as the patients follow the instructions carefully
Even if the treatment turns out to be expensive
Since most participants dropped out of the study after six months
So that the results could be published quickly
Once the treatment had been approved by regulators
questions.explanation: Uzun vadeli yararların belirlenememesinin nedeni katılımcıların çoğunun altı ay sonra çalışmayı bırakmasıdır; bu neden-sonuç ilişkisini ‘Since most participants dropped out …’ kurar. ‘As long as … follow’ şimdiki zamanlı bir koşul kurar ve zaman uyumu yoktur; tedavinin pahalı (‘expensive’) çıkması belirleyememenin nedeni değildir ve ‘Even if’ zaman uyumu da bozuktur; ‘So that … published’ amaç bildirir; onaylanmanın (‘approved’) belirleyememeyle bir ilgisi yoktur.

questions.text: Whereas the earliest electronic computers filled entire rooms, ----.
options: they were mainly used by governments and universities
engineers had to cool them with large fans
today's smartphones are far more powerful and fit easily into a pocket
because transistors gradually replaced vacuum tubes
which made them extremely expensive to build
questions.explanation: ‘Whereas’ iki durumu karşılaştırır: İlk bilgisayarlar odaları doldururken bugünün akıllı telefonları çok daha güçlüdür ve cebe sığar. ‘Governments’ tarafından kullanıldıklarını ya da ‘fans’ ile soğutulduklarını söyleyen seçenekler aynı bilgisayarları anlatır ve karşıtlık kurmaz; ‘because’ ile başlayan seçenek ve ‘expensive’ içeren ilgi cümlesi ana cümle oluşturmaz.

questions.text: The more frequently a memory is recalled, ----.
options: the more stable it tends to become
it becomes much more stable
so it is less likely to be forgotten
unless it is linked to strong emotions
as clear as it was originally
questions.explanation: ‘The more …, the more …’ (ne kadar çok …, o kadar …) kalıbı ikinci kısımda da ‘the + karşılaştırma’ ister: ‘the more stable it tends to become’. ‘It becomes much more stable’ kalıbın ikinci yarısını kurmaz; ‘so … forgotten’ sonuç bağlacıyla başlar; ‘unless … emotions’ koşul bildirir; ‘as clear as … originally’ ise karşılaştırma kalıbını eksik bırakır.

questions.text: It was not until satellite images became widely available ----.
options: that scientists could accurately measure the rate of deforestation in remote regions
when scientists measured deforestation in remote regions
because most of the forests had already disappeared
which scientists used to monitor distant forests
so remote regions became easier for tourists to visit
questions.explanation: ‘It was not until … that …’ (ancak … olunca) kalıbı ‘that’ ile tamamlanır: Bilim insanları ormansızlaşmanın hızını ancak uydu görüntüleri yaygınlaşınca doğru ölçebildi. ‘When … measured’ kalıbı tamamlamaz; ‘because … disappeared’ neden bildirir; ‘which … monitor’ ilgi cümlesidir; ‘tourists’ ile ilgili sonuç cümlesi de hem kalıba hem anlama uymaz.

questions.text: Some economists argue that raising the minimum wage reduces employment, ----.
options: so that workers can afford basic necessities
if employers had hired more staff
while others maintain that its effect on jobs is small or even positive
which proves that higher wages always create jobs
unless they had studied the issue carefully
questions.explanation: Cümle bazı ekonomistlerin görüşünü verir; ‘while others maintain …’ karşıt görüşü ekleyerek dengeli bir tamamlama yapar. ‘So that … afford’ amaç bildirir ve ‘argue’ ile ilgisizdir; ‘if employers had hired’ zaman uyumsuz bir koşuldur; ‘always create jobs’ diyen ilgi cümlesi ilk görüşle çelişir; ‘unless … studied’ ise mantıksız bir koşul kurar.

questions.text: Had the early warning system been installed a few years earlier, ----.
options: the villagers will be evacuated more quickly next time
the flood is expected to reach the coast by evening
the government installs such systems in all coastal towns
many of the villagers might have escaped before the flood arrived
most of the villagers left their homes the day before
questions.explanation: ‘Had … been installed’ devrik üçüncü tip koşuldur ve ana cümlede ‘might/would have + V3’ gerekir: ‘might have escaped’. ‘Will be evacuated’ ve ‘is expected’ gelecek ya da şimdiki zamana aittir; ‘installs’ geniş zamandır; ‘left their homes’ ise gerçekleşmiş bir olayı anlatır ve koşulun sonucunu vermez.

questions.text: Even though octopuses have no backbone and a relatively short lifespan, ----.
options: they belong to the same group of animals as snails and squid
they are capable of solving surprisingly complex problems
because they spend most of their lives on the sea floor
as most invertebrates have fairly simple nervous systems
unless they are kept in captivity for research
questions.explanation: ‘Even though’ beklenmedik bir sonuç ister: Omurgaları olmamasına ve kısa yaşamalarına rağmen ahtapotlar şaşırtıcı derecede karmaşık sorunları çözebilir. questions.passage:
The waters surrounding Antarctica are among the coldest on Earth, with temperatures that remain close to -1.9°C for much of the year. Because seawater contains salt, it freezes at a lower temperature than fresh water, but the blood of most fish would freeze well before this point. For a long time, therefore, biologists were puzzled by the fact that the Southern Ocean supports a rich community of fish, dominated by a group known as notothenioids.
Part of the answer emerged in the late 1960s, when the American biologist Arthur DeVries found that these fish produce special antifreeze proteins. Rather than lowering the freezing point of the blood in the way that salt does, these molecules bind to tiny ice crystals as soon as they form and prevent them from growing larger. As a result, the fish can survive in water that is colder than the normal freezing point of their own body fluids. Genetic studies later suggested that the main antifreeze gene in notothenioids evolved from part of a gene that originally had an unrelated function in digestion, a striking example of how evolution can put existing material to new uses.
Life in such cold water, however, appears to have come at a cost. Some notothenioids, known as icefish, have lost the red blood cells and haemoglobin that carry oxygen in almost all other vertebrates. They are able to survive largely because very cold water holds more dissolved oxygen than warm water, and because they have evolved larger hearts and wider blood vessels. Researchers fear that such specialised species may be particularly vulnerable to warming. Even an increase of a few degrees could reduce the oxygen available to them while raising their metabolic needs, and laboratory studies indicate that many Antarctic fish cannot tolerate temperatures much above those they currently experience.

options: the reasons why seawater freezes at a lower temperature than fresh water
the career of the scientist who first studied fish in the Southern Ocean

the methods used to measure ocean temperatures near the poles

Deniz suyunun neden daha düşük sıcaklıkta donduğu (‘seawater’) yalnızca giriş bilgisidir; DeVries'in ‘career’ konusu işlenmez; sindirimin (‘digestion’) evrimi tek bir örnekte geçer; sıcaklık ölçme yöntemlerinden (‘methods’) hiç söz edilmez.

questions.passage:
Long before it reached Europe, rubber was familiar to the peoples of Central and South America. As early as 1600 BCE, communities in what is now Mexico were collecting latex, the milky sap of certain trees, and mixing it with the juice of a local vine to make solid balls for a ritual ball game. Researchers who have analysed such objects suggest that these early craftsmen deliberately varied the proportions of the two ingredients to obtain rubber with different properties, from bouncy balls to hard-wearing sandal soles.
In Europe and North America, by contrast, early rubber products proved disappointing. In the 1820s and 1830s, a short-lived boom in waterproof coats, shoes and other goods collapsed when buyers discovered that the material became sticky and foul-smelling in summer and stiff and brittle in winter. The American inventor Charles Goodyear spent years experimenting with additives in an attempt to solve the problem, often while deeply in debt. Around 1839, he found that heating rubber with sulphur produced a material that remained firm and elastic across a wide range of temperatures, a process later called vulcanisation. Although Goodyear patented his method in the United States, the English manufacturer Thomas Hancock had already obtained a British patent for a similar process, and Goodyear died in 1860 owing large sums of money.
Vulcanisation turned rubber into an essential industrial material, used in machine belts, hoses and, eventually, tyres for bicycles and cars. Demand soared, and the Amazon basin, where the main rubber tree grew wild, experienced a boom that brought great wealth to a few traders while many collectors, often Indigenous people, worked under brutal conditions. The boom ended abruptly in the 1910s, when plantations in Southeast Asia, grown from seeds taken out of Brazil in the 1870s, began to produce rubber far more cheaply.

options: From Ritual Balls to Tyres: How Rubber Became an Industrial Material

Waterproof Coats as a Lasting Commercial Success

Hancock'un yaşamı (‘Hancock’) yalnızca bir cümlede geçer; ağaçların Brezilya dışında yetişemediği (‘Cannot Grow’) bilgisi Güneydoğu Asya plantasyonlarıyla çelişir; sentetik kauçuktan (‘Synthetic’) hiç söz edilmez; su geçirmez paltoların (‘Lasting’) kalıcı bir başarı olmadığı, kısa süren bir patlamanın çöktüğü belirtilir.

questions.passage:
Long before it reached Europe, rubber was familiar to the peoples of Central and South America. As early as 1600 BCE, communities in what is now Mexico were collecting latex, the milky sap of certain trees, and mixing it with the juice of a local vine to make solid balls for a ritual ball game. Researchers who have analysed such objects suggest that these early craftsmen deliberately varied the proportions of the two ingredients to obtain rubber with different properties, from bouncy balls to hard-wearing sandal soles.
In Europe and North America, by contrast, early rubber products proved disappointing. In the 1820s and 1830s, a short-lived boom in waterproof coats, shoes and other goods collapsed when buyers discovered that the material became sticky and foul-smelling in summer and stiff and brittle in winter. The American inventor Charles Goodyear spent years experimenting with additives in an attempt to solve the problem, often while deeply in debt. Around 1839, he found that heating rubber with sulphur produced a material that remained firm and elastic across a wide range of temperatures, a process later called vulcanisation. Although Goodyear patented his method in the United States, the English manufacturer Thomas Hancock had already obtained a British patent for a similar process, and Goodyear died in 1860 owing large sums of money.
Vulcanisation turned rubber into an essential industrial material, used in machine belts, hoses and, eventually, tyres for bicycles and cars. Demand soared, and the Amazon basin, where the main rubber tree grew wild, experienced a boom that brought great wealth to a few traders while many collectors, often Indigenous people, worked under brutal conditions. The boom ended abruptly in the 1910s, when plantations in Southeast Asia, grown from seeds taken out of Brazil in the 1870s, began to produce rubber far more cheaply.

Vulkanizasyonun yasaklandığı (‘banned’) ya da ağaçların hastalıkla (‘disease’) yok olduğu söylenmez; toplayıcıların ağır koşullarda çalıştığı belirtilir ama çalışmayı reddettikleri (‘refused’) söylenmez; lastik talebinin düştüğü (‘suddenly fell’) değil, talebin hızla arttığı anlatılır.

questions.passage:
Governments have traditionally relied on two tools to make people pay their taxes: the threat of audits and the size of penalties. According to the standard economic model, a rational taxpayer weighs the money that could be saved by hiding income against the probability of being caught and the fine that would follow. Yet this model predicts far more evasion than is actually observed. In many countries, audit rates are so low and fines so modest that, on purely financial grounds, a large proportion of citizens would be expected to cheat. The fact that most do not suggests that other motives are at work.
Researchers use the term "tax morale" to describe these motives, which include a sense of civic duty, trust in government and the belief that other people are paying their share. Several field experiments have tested whether such motives can be strengthened at low cost. In one well-known study in the United Kingdom, the tax authority sent letters to people who had not paid on time. Some letters simply requested payment, while others added that most people in the recipient's area had already paid. The second type of letter produced a noticeably higher rate of payment, apparently because it made non-payment seem unusual.
Behavioural research has also shown that the way a tax is presented can affect behaviour. In one experiment in an American supermarket, displaying prices that already included sales tax, rather than adding the tax at the till, reduced purchases of the labelled goods, even though shoppers knew in principle that the tax would be charged. Such findings suggest that people respond more strongly to costs that are clearly visible. However, researchers caution that the effects of these interventions are often modest and may fade over time, so they are best seen as a complement to, rather than a substitute for, effective enforcement.

questions.passage:
For most of the twentieth century, the mechanisation of agriculture meant building ever larger machines. Bigger tractors and combine harvesters allowed a single farmer to cultivate vast areas, but their weight compacts the soil, making it harder for roots to grow and for rainwater to drain away. A new generation of agricultural robots takes the opposite approach. Instead of one heavy machine, several small, lightweight robots can work a field simultaneously, guided by satellite positioning, cameras and software that learns to recognise individual plants.
One of the most promising applications is weeding. Conventional farms usually control weeds by spraying herbicide across an entire field. Robots equipped with machine vision, by contrast, can identify a weed among crop plants and either remove it mechanically or apply a tiny dose of chemical directly to it. Some trials have reported reductions in herbicide use of more than 90 per cent, although results vary considerably with the crop and the conditions. Other robots are being developed to pick delicate fruit such as strawberries, a task that has proved difficult to automate because the fruit must be located among leaves and handled without bruising.
Despite these advances, robots remain rare on most farms. They are expensive to buy, and many still work slowly or struggle in rain, mud and uneven light. Farmers also worry about reliability during critical periods such as harvest, when a breakdown could mean a serious loss of income. Supporters argue that costs will fall as the technology matures, and that robots may help to address a growing shortage of seasonal workers in many countries. Critics, however, point out that the benefits may go mainly to large farms that can afford the investment, potentially widening the gap between them and smaller producers.

questions.passage:
In many parts of the world, children begin school in a language that they do not speak at home. For decades, education authorities often assumed that the quickest route to success was to immerse such pupils in the dominant language from the first day, discouraging the use of their mother tongue in the classroom. The reasoning seemed straightforward: the more time children spent hearing and using the new language, the faster they would learn it.
Research over the past half-century has complicated this picture. Studies in several countries have found that pupils who first learn to read in a language they already understand often acquire literacy more easily, and that many of the skills they develop, such as recognising how written symbols represent sounds or how a story is organised, appear to transfer to a second language later. The Canadian researcher Jim Cummins described this idea as a "common underlying proficiency", arguing that the two languages draw on shared cognitive resources rather than competing for limited space. Programmes that continue to teach in both languages for several years have, in a number of evaluations, produced better long-term results in the second language than programmes that abandon the first language early.
Nevertheless, putting such programmes into practice is far from simple. In countries where dozens of languages are spoken, it may be difficult to find qualified teachers and suitable textbooks for each of them. Some parents, aware that the dominant language offers access to higher education and well-paid jobs, actively prefer that their children be taught in it as early as possible. Moreover, studies differ in quality, and outcomes depend heavily on how programmes are designed and funded. For these reasons, most specialists now avoid sweeping claims and argue instead that policies should be adapted to local conditions.

İlk günden ‘immersed’ edilme görüşü araştırmalarla sorgulanan eski varsayımdır; programların her yerde ‘failed’ olduğu söylenmez, aksine bazı değerlendirmelerde daha iyi sonuç verdiği belirtilir; bazı velilerin baskın dili tercih ettiği söylendiği için ‘insist’ ve ana dil seçeneği yanlıştır; Cummins iki dilin ortak kaynaklardan beslendiğini savunur, ‘harms’ demez.

questions.passage:
In many parts of the world, children begin school in a language that they do not speak at home. For decades, education authorities often assumed that the quickest route to success was to immerse such pupils in the dominant language from the first day, discouraging the use of their mother tongue in the classroom. The reasoning seemed straightforward: the more time children spent hearing and using the new language, the faster they would learn it.
Research over the past half-century has complicated this picture. Studies in several countries have found that pupils who first learn to read in a language they already understand often acquire literacy more easily, and that many of the skills they develop, such as recognising how written symbols represent sounds or how a story is organised, appear to transfer to a second language later. The Canadian researcher Jim Cummins described this idea as a "common underlying proficiency", arguing that the two languages draw on shared cognitive resources rather than competing for limited space. Programmes that continue to teach in both languages for several years have, in a number of evaluations, produced better long-term results in the second language than programmes that abandon the first language early.
Nevertheless, putting such programmes into practice is far from simple. In countries where dozens of languages are spoken, it may be difficult to find qualified teachers and suitable textbooks for each of them. Some parents, aware that the dominant language offers access to higher education and well-paid jobs, actively prefer that their children be taught in it as early as possible. Moreover, studies differ in quality, and outcomes depend heavily on how programmes are designed and funded. For these reasons, most specialists now avoid sweeping claims and argue instead that policies should be adapted to local conditions.

questions.explanation: ‘Diverge from a common ancestor’ (ortak bir atadan ayrılmak) evrimsel ayrışmayı anlatan kalıptır ve ‘although … look almost identical’ zıtlığıyla uyumludur. ‘Collapsed’ (çöktü), ‘abstained’ (kaçındı), ‘resided’ (ikamet etti) ve ‘deteriorated’ (kötüleşti) bir atadan ayrılma anlamı vermez.

questions.text: The historian's argument is rather ---- because it relies on a single letter whose authenticity has never been confirmed.
options: compelling
abundant
imminent
lucrative
tenuous
questions.explanation: Doğruluğu hiç kanıtlanmamış tek bir mektuba dayanan bir iddia zayıftır; ‘tenuous’ (zayıf, temelsiz) bu anlamı verir. ‘Compelling’ (ikna edici) cümledeki eleştiriyle çelişir; ‘abundant’ (bol), ‘imminent’ (yakın, eli kulağında) ve ‘lucrative’ (kârlı) bir argümanı nitelemek için anlamsızdır.

questions.text: Many patients fail to complete their course of antibiotics, ---- because they begin to feel better after only a few days.
options: barely
scarcely
seldom
largely
hardly
questions.explanation: Hastaların tedaviyi yarıda bırakmasının başlıca nedeni birkaç gün sonra kendilerini iyi hissetmeleridir; ‘largely because’ (büyük ölçüde … nedeniyle) bunu anlatır. ‘Barely’, ‘scarcely’ ve ‘hardly’ (neredeyse hiç) olumsuz anlam taşıyıp nedeni ortadan kaldırır; ‘seldom’ (nadiren) ise sıklık bildirir ve ‘because’ ile uyuşmaz.

questions.text: The negotiations had to be ---- until the following month after one of the delegations failed to arrive.
options: taken over
made up
put off
turned in
set out
questions.explanation: Bir heyet gelmeyince görüşmeler bir sonraki aya ertelenmek zorunda kalmıştır; ‘put off’ (ertelemek) ve ‘until the following month’ birlikte bu anlamı verir. ‘Taken over’ (devralınmak), ‘made up’ (uydurulmak, telafi edilmek), ‘turned in’ (teslim edilmek) ve ‘set out’ (yola çıkmak, ortaya koymak) ertelemeyi anlatmaz.

questions.text: Researchers were surprised to find that the drug's side effects were far less ---- than earlier trials had suggested.
options: obsolete
reluctant
deliberate
pronounced
eligible
questions.explanation: Yan etkilerin önceki denemelerin gösterdiğinden çok daha az belirgin olması şaşırtıcıdır; ‘pronounced’ (belirgin, kendini gösteren) yan etkilerle doğal biçimde kullanılır. ‘Obsolete’ (eskimiş), ‘reluctant’ (isteksiz), ‘deliberate’ (kasıtlı) ve ‘eligible’ (uygun, hak sahibi) yan etkileri nitelemek için anlamsızdır.

questions.text: The bridge, which ---- in 1890, is still used by thousands of commuters every day.
options: has completed
had been completing
is completed
was completed
completes
questions.explanation: Köprü tamamlanan şeydir, yani edilgen yapı gerekir; ‘in 1890’ belirli bir geçmiş zamanı gösterdiği için ‘was completed’ doğrudur. ‘Has completed’ ve ‘had been completing’ etken yapıdadır ve köprüyü işi yapan konuma koyar; ‘is completed’ ve ‘completes’ ise geniş zamandır ve ‘in 1890’ ile uyuşmaz.

questions.text: ---- the high cost of the equipment, many small hospitals have been unable to offer the new scanning service.
options: Owing to
Even though
In case
Provided that
So as to
questions.explanation: Boşluktan sonra bir isim öbeği (‘the high cost of the equipment’) gelir ve neden bildirilir; ‘Owing to’ (… yüzünden) bu işlevi görür. ‘Even though’, ‘In case’ ve ‘Provided that’ ardından tam bir cümle ister; ‘So as to’ ise fiil alır ve amaç bildirir.

questions.text: The committee recommended that every applicant ---- an interview before a final decision is made.
options: be given
will give
has given
giving
was giving
questions.explanation: ‘Recommend that’ yapısından sonra yalın fiil (subjunctive) kullanılır; aday mülakat verilen kişi olduğundan edilgen ‘be given’ gerekir. ‘Will give’, ‘has given’ ve ‘was giving’ çekimli ve etken biçimlerdir, anlamı da bozar; ‘giving’ ise çekimsizdir ve cümleye yüklem olamaz.

questions.text: Not until the late nineteenth century ---- that many infectious diseases are spread by microorganisms.
options: scientists accepted
had scientists been accepting
scientists did accept
did scientists accept
have scientists accepted
questions.explanation: Olumsuz zaman ifadesi ‘Not until …’ cümle başına geldiğinde ana cümlede devrik yapı gerekir; geçmiş zaman için ‘did scientists accept’ kullanılır. ‘Scientists accepted’ ve ‘scientists did accept’ devrik değildir; ‘have scientists accepted’ geçmişteki belirli bir dönemle, ‘had scientists been accepting’ ise anlamca uyuşmaz.

questions.text: Volcanic ash can travel thousands of kilometres, ---- air traffic over a vast area.
options: disrupted
to have disrupted
disrupting
being disrupted
having been disrupted
questions.explanation: Virgülden sonra kül bulutunun yol açtığı sonucu anlatan etken bir ortaç yapısı gerekir: ‘disrupting air traffic’ (hava trafiğini aksatarak). ‘Disrupted’, ‘being disrupted’ ve ‘having been disrupted’ edilgen anlam taşır ve ardından nesne alamaz; ‘to have disrupted’ ise sonucu değil geçmişte tamamlanmış bir eylemi bildirir.

questions.text: The village ---- the ancient coins were discovered has since become a popular destination for tourists.
options: which
where
whose
what
whom
questions.explanation: Sıfat cümlesi kendi içinde tamdır (‘the ancient coins were discovered’) ve yer bildiren ‘village’ ismini niteler; bu nedenle ‘where’ gerekir. ‘Which’ ve ‘whom’ cümlede eksik bir özne ya da nesne ister; ‘whose’ ardından isim alır, ‘what’ ise bir ismi nitelemek için kullanılamaz.

questions.text: Unless additional funding ---- soon, the research station will have to close before the winter.
options: will be found
had been found
would be found
was being found
is found
questions.explanation: Ana cümle ‘will have to close’ olduğu için birinci tip koşul kurulur; ‘unless’ cümlesinde gelecek anlamı geniş zamanla verilir ve fon bulunan şey olduğundan edilgen ‘is found’ gerekir. ‘Will be found’ koşul cümlesinde kullanılmaz; ‘had been found’, ‘would be found’ ve ‘was being found’ ise zaman açısından ana cümleyle uyuşmaz.

questions.text: The success of the vaccination programme depends largely ---- the willingness of parents to have their children immunised.
options: with
on
at
for
by
questions.explanation: ‘Depend’ fiili ‘on’ edatıyla kullanılır: ‘depend on’ (… -e bağlı olmak). ‘With’, ‘at’, ‘for’ ve ‘by’ edatları bu fiille ‘bağlı olmak’ anlamını kurmaz.

questions.text: The museum's collection is so fragile ---- it can only be displayed under carefully controlled lighting.
options: as
than
that
which
such
questions.explanation: ‘So + sıfat + that’ yapısı sonuç bildirir: Koleksiyon o kadar kırılgandır ki yalnızca kontrollü ışıkta sergilenebilir. ‘As’ ve ‘than’ karşılaştırma kurar, ‘which’ sıfat cümlesi başlatır ve ‘so’ ile eşleşmez; ‘such’ ise isimden önce kullanılır ve sonuç cümlesini bağlamaz.

questions.text: Neither the manager nor the employees ---- aware of the new safety regulations until the inspection took place.
options: were
has been
have been
is
are
questions.explanation: ‘Neither … nor’ yapısında fiil kendisine en yakın özneyle (‘the employees’) uyum gösterir, dolayısıyla çoğul olmalıdır; ‘until the inspection took place’ geçmişi gösterdiği için ‘were’ doğrudur. ‘Has been’ ve ‘is’ tekildir; ‘have been’ ve ‘are’ ise geçmişteki bir olaya kadar süren durumu anlatmak için zamanca uygun değildir.

questions.passage: Carbon capture and storage refers to a group of technologies designed to trap carbon dioxide before it (1) ---- the atmosphere. In a typical system, the gas is separated from the exhaust of a power station or cement factory, compressed into a dense, liquid-like state and then transported by pipeline to a suitable site, (2) ---- it is injected deep underground into porous rock formations. Supporters argue that the approach is essential for heavy industries such as steel and cement production, (3) ---- their emissions arise not only from burning fuel but also from the chemical reactions involved in manufacturing. Critics, (4) ----, point out that the technology remains expensive and that only a tiny fraction of global emissions is currently captured. They also warn that relying on it could (5) ---- efforts to cut emissions at their source by encouraging companies to postpone more fundamental changes.
questions.text: (1) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: will reach
reaches
reached
has been reaching
reaching
questions.explanation: Metin genel bir işleyişi geniş zamanla anlatır ve ‘before’ ile kurulan zaman cümlesinde gelecek zaman kullanılmaz; bu nedenle ‘reaches’ doğrudur. ‘Will reach’ zaman bağlacından sonra kullanılmaz; ‘reached’ ve ‘has been reaching’ metnin geniş zaman anlatımıyla uyuşmaz; ‘reaching’ ise çekimsizdir ve ‘it’ öznesine yüklem olamaz.

questions.text: (2) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: which
when
whose
where
that
questions.explanation: Boşluk ‘a suitable site’ (uygun bir yer) ismini niteler ve ardından gelen cümle tamdır (‘it is injected …’); yer bildiren ‘where’ bu nedenle gerekir. ‘Which’ ve ‘that’ cümlede eksik bir öğe ister; ‘when’ zaman bildirir; ‘whose’ ise ardından isim almalıdır.

questions.passage: Carbon capture and storage refers to a group of technologies designed to trap carbon dioxide before it (1) ---- the atmosphere. In a typical system, the gas is separated from the exhaust of a power station or cement factory, compressed into a dense, liquid-like state and then transported by pipeline to a suitable site, (2) ---- it is injected deep underground into porous rock formations. Critics, (4) ----, point out that the technology remains expensive and that only a tiny fraction of global emissions is currently captured. They also warn that relying on it could (5) ---- efforts to cut emissions at their source by encouraging companies to postpone more fundamental changes.
questions.text: (3) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: unless
whereas
so that
since
although
questions.explanation: Destekçiler bu teknolojinin çelik ve çimento için vazgeçilmez olduğunu söyler, çünkü bu sektörlerin emisyonu yalnızca yakıttan değil kimyasal tepkimelerden de kaynaklanır; neden bildiren ‘since’ uygundur. ‘Unless’ koşul, ‘so that’ amaç bildirir; ‘whereas’ ve ‘although’ ise iki cümle arasında olmayan bir zıtlık kurar.

questions.passage: Carbon capture and storage refers to a group of technologies designed to trap carbon dioxide before it (1) ---- the atmosphere. In a typical system, the gas is separated from the exhaust of a power station or cement factory, compressed into a dense, liquid-like state and then transported by pipeline to a suitable site, (2) ---- it is injected deep underground into porous rock formations. Supporters argue that the approach is essential for heavy industries such as steel and cement production, (3) ---- their emissions arise not only from burning fuel but also from the chemical reactions involved in manufacturing. Critics, (4) ----, point out that the technology remains expensive and that only a tiny fraction of global emissions is currently captured. They also warn that relying on it could (5) ---- efforts to cut emissions at their source by encouraging companies to postpone more fundamental changes.
questions.text: (4) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: therefore
likewise
for instance
however
in other words
questions.explanation: Önceki cümlede destekçilerin görüşü, bu cümlede ise eleştirmenlerin itirazları verilir; zıtlık bildiren ‘however’ gerekir. ‘Therefore’ sonuç, ‘likewise’ benzerlik bildirir; ‘for instance’ örnek, ‘in other words’ ise açıklama getirir ve iki karşıt görüşü bağlamaz.

questions.text: (5) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: accelerate
reinforce
undermine
inspire
justify
questions.explanation: Eleştirmenler bu teknolojiye güvenmenin şirketleri köklü değişiklikleri ertelemeye iteceğini, yani emisyonu kaynağında azaltma çabalarını zayıflatacağını söyler; ‘undermine’ (baltalamak) bu anlamı verir. ‘Accelerate’ (hızlandırmak), ‘reinforce’ (güçlendirmek) ve ‘inspire’ (esinlendirmek) olumlu etkiler bildirir ve eleştiriyle çelişir; ‘justify’ (haklı çıkarmak) ise anlamca uymaz.

questions.passage: Nutrition labels, which list the energy, fat, sugar and salt content of packaged foods, have been compulsory in many countries (1) ---- the 1990s. Their purpose is to help consumers make healthier choices, yet research suggests that relatively few shoppers read them carefully, (2) ---- when they are in a hurry. One reason is that the information is often printed in small type and expressed in units that many people find difficult to interpret. (3) ---- this problem, several governments have introduced simplified front-of-pack systems that use colours or letter grades to indicate how healthy a product is. Early studies indicate that such labels can (4) ---- purchasing behaviour, although the effect is usually modest. Interestingly, some manufacturers have responded by quietly changing the recipes of their products (5) ---- avoid receiving a poor rating.
questions.text: (1) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: since
for
during
until
by
questions.explanation: Present perfect (‘have been compulsory’) ile bir başlangıç noktası belirtilir: 1990'lardan beri zorunlu olmuştur; bu nedenle ‘since’ gerekir. ‘For’ bir süre ister (örneğin ‘for thirty years’); ‘during’ ve ‘until’ bu zaman yapısıyla başlangıç bildiremez; ‘by’ ise ‘had been’ ya da ‘will have been’ gibi yapılarla kullanılır.

Early studies indicate that such labels can (4) ---- purchasing behaviour, although the effect is usually modest. questions.text: (2) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: particularly
hardly
rarely
merely
instead
questions.explanation: Alışverişçilerin etiketleri dikkatle okumadığı, özellikle aceleleri olduğunda bunun daha da belirgin olduğu anlatılır; ‘particularly’ (özellikle) bu vurguyu yapar. ‘Hardly’ ve ‘rarely’ cümleye ters bir anlam katar; ‘merely’ (yalnızca) ve ‘instead’ (bunun yerine) ise anlamlı bir bağlantı kurmaz.

questions.passage: Nutrition labels, which list the energy, fat, sugar and salt content of packaged foods, have been compulsory in many countries (1) ---- the 1990s. Early studies indicate that such labels can (4) ---- purchasing behaviour, although the effect is usually modest. Interestingly, some manufacturers have responded by quietly changing the recipes of their products (5) ---- avoid receiving a poor rating.
questions.text: (3) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: Despite
To address
Regardless of
Instead of
Contrary to
questions.explanation: Hükümetler bilgilerin anlaşılmasının zor olduğu sorununu çözmek amacıyla sadeleştirilmiş etiketler getirmiştir; amaç bildiren ‘To address’ (… ile başa çıkmak için) uygundur. ‘Despite’ ve ‘Regardless of’ sorunun yok sayıldığını anlatır; ‘Instead of’ ve ‘Contrary to’ ise sorunu ortadan kaldırma amacını vermez.

questions.passage: Nutrition labels, which list the energy, fat, sugar and salt content of packaged foods, have been compulsory in many countries (1) ---- the 1990s. questions.text: (4) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: postpone
overlook
influence
abandon
conceal
questions.explanation: Etkinin genellikle ‘modest’ (sınırlı) olduğu söylendiğine göre etiketler satın alma davranışını bir ölçüde etkileyebilmektedir; ‘influence’ (etkilemek) doğrudur. ‘Postpone’ (ertelemek), ‘overlook’ (gözden kaçırmak), ‘abandon’ (terk etmek) ve ‘conceal’ (gizlemek) davranış üzerindeki bir etkiyi anlatmaz.

questions.passage: Nutrition labels, which list the energy, fat, sugar and salt content of packaged foods, have been compulsory in many countries (1) ---- the 1990s. (3) ---- this problem, several governments have introduced simplified front-of-pack systems that use colours or letter grades to indicate how healthy a product is. Early studies indicate that such labels can (4) ---- purchasing behaviour, although the effect is usually modest. Interestingly, some manufacturers have responded by quietly changing the recipes of their products (5) ---- avoid receiving a poor rating.
questions.text: (5) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: in order that
so that
so as to
as long as
in case
questions.explanation: Boşluktan sonra yalın fiil (‘avoid’) gelir ve amaç bildirilir; ‘so as to’ bu yapıyı kurar. ‘In order that’ ve ‘so that’ de amaç bildirir ancak ardından tam bir cümle (özne + yüklem) ister; ‘as long as’ koşul, ‘in case’ ise önlem bildirir ve yine cümle gerektirir.

questions.text: Even though the ancient manuscript had been badly damaged by water, ----.
options: it had been stored in a damp cellar for centuries
because the ink was made from soot and gum
unless it is kept in a climate-controlled room
so that scholars could study it more easily
conservators managed to recover most of its text using infrared imaging
questions.explanation: ‘Even though’ beklenmedik bir sonuç ister: Elyazması sudan zarar görmüş olmasına rağmen uzmanlar metnin çoğunu kurtarmayı başarmıştır; ‘conservators managed to recover’ bunu verir. Nemli bir ‘cellar’ içinde saklandığını söyleyen seçenek zıtlık kurmaz; ‘because’, ‘unless’ ve ‘so that’ ile başlayan seçenekler ana cümle oluşturamaz.

questions.text: ----, the number of reported cases is likely to underestimate the true extent of the disease.
options: As soon as the vaccine became widely available
Whereas the disease was first identified decades ago
So that patients can be treated at home
Since many people with mild symptoms never visit a doctor
Unless the symptoms were severe enough
questions.explanation: Bildirilen vaka sayısının hastalığın gerçek boyutunu olduğundan az göstermesinin nedeni, hafif belirtisi olanların doktora gitmemesidir; ‘Since many people with mild symptoms never visit a doctor’ bu nedeni verir. Aşının ‘vaccine’ yaygınlaşması ve hastalığın ‘identified’ edildiği tarih eksik sayımı açıklamaz; ‘So that … treated at home’ amaç, ‘Unless … severe’ ise anlamsız bir koşul kurar.

questions.text: The researchers chose to conduct the survey online ----.
options: whereas face-to-face interviews were completely free
although they had already collected all the data they needed
unless the participants had never used a computer
as if the questionnaire were written in another language
so that they could reach participants in remote rural areas at low cost
questions.explanation: Anketi çevrimiçi yapmanın amacı uzak kırsal bölgelerdeki katılımcılara düşük maliyetle ulaşmaktır; ‘so that they could reach participants’ bu amacı bildirir. Yüz yüze görüşmelerin ‘free’ olması tercihi açıklamaz, tersine çevirir; verilerin ‘already collected’ olması anketi gereksiz kılar; ‘computer’ koşulu ve ‘another language’ benzetmesi ise anlamsızdır.

questions.text: If governments had invested in flood defences a decade ago, ----.
options: the storms will cause less damage in the future
the coastal towns were rebuilt within a year
flood defences are usually built along rivers
the damage caused by this year's storms would probably have been far less severe
the residents had to leave their homes
questions.explanation: ‘If + past perfect’ üçüncü tip koşuldur ve ana cümlede ‘would have + V3’ gerektirir; ‘would probably have been far less severe’ bunu karşılar. ‘Will cause less damage’ birinci tip koşula aittir; kasabaların ‘rebuilt’ edilmesi ve sakinlerin evlerini ‘leave’ etmesi düz geçmiş zamandadır; ‘usually built along rivers’ ise genel bir bilgidir ve koşula bağlanmaz.

questions.text: Unlike earlier generations of solar panels, which converted only a small proportion of sunlight into electricity, ----.
options: solar energy has long been considered an expensive source of power
modern panels can turn more than a fifth of the light that falls on them into usable power
they were often installed on the roofs of houses
the price of electricity has risen sharply in many countries
early panels were mainly used to power satellites
questions.explanation: ‘Unlike’ eski panellerle yeni paneller arasında bir karşıtlık ister: Eskiler ışığın küçük bir kısmını dönüştürürken modern paneller beşte birinden fazlasını dönüştürebilir; ‘modern panels can turn more than a fifth’ bunu verir. Güneş enerjisinin ‘expensive’ sayılması, panellerin çatılara ‘installed’ edilmesi, elektrik fiyatının ‘risen’ olması ve eski panellerin ‘satellites’ için kullanılması bu karşıtlığı kurmaz.

questions.text: ----, whereas others are able to recover fully within a few weeks.
options: Most patients recover fully within a few weeks
Because the infection spreads easily in crowded places
The infection was first identified in the early twentieth century
If patients rest and drink plenty of fluids
Some patients continue to experience fatigue for months after the infection
questions.explanation: ‘Whereas others’ ifadesi, ilk bölümde ‘some’ ile başlayan ve karşıt bir durum anlatan bir grup ister: Bazı hastalar aylarca yorgunluk yaşarken diğerleri birkaç haftada iyileşir; ‘Some patients continue to experience fatigue’ bunu verir. Hastaların çoğunun ‘within a few weeks’ iyileştiğini söyleyen seçenek zıtlık kurmaz; ‘Because … crowded places’ ve ‘If … fluids’ ana cümle olamaz; enfeksiyonun ‘identified’ edildiği tarih ise ilgisizdir.

questions.text: The documents reveal that the treaty was signed in haste, ----.
options: as long as both sides agree to its terms
so that it will come into force next year
unless the parliament had rejected it beforehand
whereas many treaties are written in more than one language
which may explain why several of its clauses were later found to contradict one another
questions.explanation: Antlaşmanın aceleyle imzalanması, maddelerinin neden birbiriyle çeliştiğini açıklayabilir; ‘which may explain why … contradict one another’ önceki cümlenin tamamına gönderme yapan mantıklı bir sonuç verir. ‘As long as … agree’ ve ‘so that … next year’ zaman açısından uyuşmaz; ‘parliament’ ile kurulan koşul anlamsızdır; antlaşmaların birden çok dilde ‘written’ olması ise ilgisiz bir karşılaştırmadır.

questions.text: Only when the cause of the malfunction had been identified ----.
options: engineers were allowed to restart the reactor
the reactor has operated safely ever since
do engineers usually restart such reactors
that engineers were allowed to restart the reactor
were engineers allowed to restart the reactor

questions.text: Although the new drug proved effective in laboratory tests, ----.

the laboratory tests were carried out on mice

questions.text: The city council decided to plant thousands of trees along its main streets ----.
options: even though trees absorb carbon dioxide from the air
unless the residents had objected to the plan
as if the streets were too narrow for cars
in the hope that they would provide shade and lower summer temperatures
whereas the trees had been cut down decades earlier
questions.explanation: Ağaç dikme kararının amacı gölge sağlamak ve yaz sıcaklıklarını düşürmektir; ‘in the hope that they would provide shade’ bu amacı bildirir. Ağaçların karbondioksit ‘absorb’ etmesi bir yarar olduğundan ‘even though’ ile zıtlık kurulamaz; ‘objected’ ile kurulan koşul, ‘narrow’ benzetmesi ve ağaçların ‘decades earlier’ kesildiğini söyleyen karşıtlık ise anlamsızdır.

Uzmanlar, düzenli egzersizin yalnızca fiziksel sağlığı değil, aynı zamanda ruh sağlığını da iyileştirdiğini vurgulamaktadır.

questions.passage:
The idea that curved pieces of glass can make objects appear larger is surprisingly old. Ancient writers, including the Roman philosopher Seneca, noted that letters seen through a glass globe filled with water looked bigger and clearer. Yet for more than a thousand years this observation remained a curiosity rather than the basis of a practical tool. The decisive step seems to have been taken in northern Italy towards the end of the thirteenth century, when craftsmen began to grind small convex lenses and mount them in frames that could be balanced on the nose. A sermon delivered in Florence in 1306 mentions that spectacles had been invented less than twenty years earlier, although the name of the inventor was not recorded.
The impact of this modest invention was considerable. Before spectacles, scholars, scribes and craftsmen whose eyesight weakened with age often had to give up close work in their forties. Reading glasses effectively extended their working lives by decades, and some historians have argued that this helped to preserve skills and knowledge at a time when books were copied by hand. Lenses for short-sighted people, which are concave rather than convex, appeared later and were rarer, probably because they were harder to grind accurately.
The growing expertise of glass-makers eventually had consequences that no one could have foreseen. Around 1600, spectacle makers in the Netherlands discovered that combining two lenses in a tube could make distant objects appear closer, and within a few years Galileo had turned such a device towards the night sky. At roughly the same time, other lens combinations led to the first microscopes. In this sense, the instruments that transformed astronomy and biology grew directly out of a trade originally devoted to helping ageing eyes read.
questions.text: The passage is mainly concerned with ----.
options: the origins of spectacles and the way lens-making later contributed to major scientific instruments
the reasons why ancient philosophers were interested in the properties of water
the difficulties scribes faced when copying books by hand
a comparison between the telescope built by Galileo and modern telescopes
the scientific explanation of why some people become short-sighted
questions.explanation: Metin gözlüğün 13. yüzyıl sonunda İtalya'da ortaya çıkışını, etkisini ve gözlük ustalarının birikiminin teleskop ile mikroskobun doğuşuna nasıl yol açtığını anlatır; ‘the origins of spectacles and the way lens-making later contributed’ bu bütünü kapsar. Antik filozofların suyun özelliklerine ‘philosophers’ ilgisi ve yazıcıların kitap kopyalarken yaşadığı ‘difficulties’ yalnızca ayrıntıdır; ‘modern telescopes’ ile karşılaştırma ve miyopluğun bilimsel nedeni (‘explanation’) metinde yoktur.

questions.passage:
Pirates are usually remembered as lawless adventurers, but a number of economists and historians have argued that the pirate ships of the early eighteenth century were, in some respects, remarkably well-organised enterprises. At the height of what is often called the golden age of Atlantic piracy, roughly between 1715 and 1725, several thousand pirates operated in the Caribbean and along the coasts of North America and West Africa. Many of them were former sailors who had served on merchant or naval vessels, where wages were low, discipline was harsh and captains could punish crew members almost at will.
On many pirate ships, by contrast, crews drew up written agreements, known as articles, before setting out. These documents typically specified how any captured goods would be divided, with the captain often receiving only one and a half or two shares compared with one share for an ordinary member of the crew. Some articles even promised compensation to men who lost a limb in battle, a form of insurance that was almost unknown in legitimate shipping at the time. Captains were generally elected and could be removed by a vote if the crew lost confidence in them.
The economist Peter Leeson has suggested that these arrangements arose not from any commitment to equality but from practical necessity. Since pirates could not rely on courts or governments to enforce agreements, they needed rules that would prevent quarrels and stop captains from abusing their power. Pirates also had an interest in maintaining a fearsome reputation: if merchant crews believed that resistance would be punished brutally, they were more likely to surrender without a fight, which reduced the costs and risks of each attack. Not all historians accept this interpretation, however, and some caution that surviving articles may describe ideals more often than everyday practice.
questions.text: The main idea of the passage is that ----.
options: pirates were mainly motivated by a desire to create a fairer society
pirate crews of the early eighteenth century developed rules that served their own practical interests
naval vessels offered better working conditions than pirate ships
governments eventually defeated piracy by enforcing strict laws
most pirates were captured within a few years of starting their careers
questions.explanation: Metin, 18. yüzyıl başındaki korsan gemilerinin yazılı kurallarla iyi örgütlendiğini ve Leeson'a göre bu düzenin eşitlik idealinden değil pratik zorunluluktan doğduğunu anlatır; ‘developed rules that served their own practical interests’ ana fikirdir. Metin ‘not from any commitment to equality’ dediği için ‘fairer society’ seçeneği yanlıştır; donanma gemilerinde koşulların ‘harsh’ olduğu söylendiğinden ‘better working conditions’ yanlıştır; hükümetlerin korsanlığı ‘defeated’ etmesi ve korsanların ‘captured’ edilmesi metinde yer almaz.

Pirates are usually remembered as lawless adventurers, but a number of economists and historians have argued that the pirate ships of the early eighteenth century were, in some respects, remarkably well-organised enterprises. At the height of what is often called the golden age of Atlantic piracy, roughly between 1715 and 1725, several thousand pirates operated in the Caribbean and along the coasts of North America and West Africa. Many of them were former sailors who had served on merchant or naval vessels, where wages were low, discipline was harsh and captains could punish crew members almost at will.
On many pirate ships, by contrast, crews drew up written agreements, known as articles, before setting out. These documents typically specified how any captured goods would be divided, with the captain often receiving only one and a half or two shares compared with one share for an ordinary member of the crew. Some articles even promised compensation to men who lost a limb in battle, a form of insurance that was almost unknown in legitimate shipping at the time. Captains were generally elected and could be removed by a vote if the crew lost confidence in them.
The economist Peter Leeson has suggested that these arrangements arose not from any commitment to equality but from practical necessity. Since pirates could not rely on courts or governments to enforce agreements, they needed rules that would prevent quarrels and stop captains from abusing their power. Pirates also had an interest in maintaining a fearsome reputation: if merchant crews believed that resistance would be punished brutally, they were more likely to surrender without a fight, which reduced the costs and risks of each attack. Not all historians accept this interpretation, however, and some caution that surviving articles may describe ideals more often than everyday practice.

questions.passage:
Dolphins have long been regarded as among the most intelligent animals, but measuring their cognitive abilities has proved difficult, partly because experiments designed for land animals cannot simply be transferred to the sea. Over the past few decades, however, researchers have gathered a body of evidence that points to unusually complex mental capacities.
One of the most striking findings concerns the use of signature whistles. Bottlenose dolphins appear to develop a distinctive whistle within the first months of life, and they continue to produce it for many years. Other members of their group have been observed copying a particular individual's whistle, apparently in order to call that individual, in a way that some researchers compare to the use of names. In playback experiments, wild dolphins responded more strongly to recordings of the signature whistles of relatives than to those of unfamiliar animals, even after long periods of separation.
Dolphins have also passed versions of the mirror test, in which an animal is marked in a place it can see only with the help of a mirror. Individuals that were marked spent more time in front of the mirror and twisted their bodies to inspect the marked area, behaviour that is usually interpreted as a sign of self-recognition. Only a few species, including great apes and elephants, have shown comparable responses.
Nevertheless, some scientists urge caution. They note that many studies involve small numbers of captive animals, whose behaviour may not reflect that of dolphins in the wild, and that it is easy to read human qualities into actions that may have simpler explanations. In their view, describing whistles as names risks overstating what the evidence actually shows. Such debates illustrate a broader challenge in the study of animal minds: how to design tests that are fair to species whose senses and environments differ so greatly from our own.

questions.passage:
Among the most remarkable documents to survive from the ancient world are the astronomical diaries kept by scholars in Babylon, in what is now Iraq. Written on clay tablets in cuneiform script, the diaries record observations made night after night over a period of roughly six centuries, beginning in the seventh century BCE. The scribes noted the positions of the Moon and planets, eclipses, the appearance of comets and the weather, but they also included the price of barley, the level of the river Euphrates and important political events.
The reason for combining such different kinds of information lies in the purpose of Babylonian astronomy. The scribes worked within a tradition of celestial divination, which held that events in the sky were signs sent by the gods to warn of what might happen on Earth, particularly to the king. Recording heavenly phenomena alongside earthly ones may therefore have been intended to reveal connections between them. Whatever their motives, the scribes accumulated data of extraordinary consistency.
These long series of records eventually allowed Babylonian scholars to detect regular cycles. They recognised, for example, that eclipses of the Moon tend to recur after a period of about eighteen years, and they developed arithmetical methods for predicting the positions of planets without relying on any geometrical model of the heavens. Several of their techniques and numerical values were later adopted by Greek astronomers, who combined them with their own geometrical approach.
Today, the diaries continue to prove valuable to researchers. Historians use them to date political events precisely, while some scientists have examined ancient eclipse reports to estimate small, long-term changes in the rate at which the Earth rotates. Ironically, records that were made largely to read the will of the gods now serve as a source of reliable data for modern science.

questions.passage:
For much of the twentieth century, ideas about crowds were shaped by the French writer Gustave Le Bon, who argued in 1895 that individuals lose their capacity for reason when they become part of a crowd. According to Le Bon, people in crowds become anonymous, suggestible and prone to sudden, violent emotions, so that even educated citizens may behave in a primitive way. This view proved highly influential, and it continues to inform the way some authorities plan for large public events, treating gatherings primarily as a threat to be contained.
Since the 1980s, however, a number of social psychologists have challenged this picture. Researchers such as Stephen Reicher and Clifford Stott have argued that people in crowds do not lose their identity but rather adopt a shared social identity, for instance as fans of a particular team or supporters of a cause. Behaviour in a crowd, in this view, is guided by the norms and values of that group rather than by blind emotion. Studies of emergencies support this idea: survivors of disasters frequently describe strangers helping one another, and mass panic, in the sense of selfish, uncontrolled flight, appears to be relatively rare.
The newer approach also has practical implications. If crowd behaviour depends on how members see themselves and others, then the way a crowd is treated can affect what it does. Studies of football matches have suggested that heavy-handed policing, which treats every fan as a potential troublemaker, may unite the crowd against the police and make conflict more likely. In contrast, officers who communicate with fans and respond only to the specific individuals who cause trouble appear to reduce disorder. Several police forces in Europe have adopted strategies based on this research, although critics argue that it may underestimate the danger posed by organised violent groups.

options: the life and writings of Gustave Le Bon

Taraftarlarla iletişim (‘communicate’) ve ortak değerlerin (‘shared values’) belirleyiciliği yeni yaklaşıma aittir; etkinliklerin tümüyle durdurulduğu (‘stopped’) söylenmez; paniğin nadir olduğu (‘extremely rare’) görüşü de Le Bon'un değil yeni araştırmaların bulgusudur.

questions.passage:
For much of the twentieth century, ideas about crowds were shaped by the French writer Gustave Le Bon, who argued in 1895 that individuals lose their capacity for reason when they become part of a crowd. According to Le Bon, people in crowds become anonymous, suggestible and prone to sudden, violent emotions, so that even educated citizens may behave in a primitive way. This view proved highly influential, and it continues to inform the way some authorities plan for large public events, treating gatherings primarily as a threat to be contained.
Since the 1980s, however, a number of social psychologists have challenged this picture. Researchers such as Stephen Reicher and Clifford Stott have argued that people in crowds do not lose their identity but rather adopt a shared social identity, for instance as fans of a particular team or supporters of a cause. Behaviour in a crowd, in this view, is guided by the norms and values of that group rather than by blind emotion. Studies of emergencies support this idea: survivors of disasters frequently describe strangers helping one another, and mass panic, in the sense of selfish, uncontrolled flight, appears to be relatively rare.
The newer approach also has practical implications. If crowd behaviour depends on how members see themselves and others, then the way a crowd is treated can affect what it does. Studies of football matches have suggested that heavy-handed policing, which treats every fan as a potential troublemaker, may unite the crowd against the police and make conflict more likely. In contrast, officers who communicate with fans and respond only to the specific individuals who cause trouble appear to reduce disorder. Several police forces in Europe have adopted strategies based on this research, although critics argue that it may underestimate the danger posed by organised violent groups.
questions.text: The word ‘it’ in the last sentence of the passage refers to ----.
options: heavy-handed policing
the crowd
disorder
the research on which the strategies are based
Europe
questions.explanation: Son cümlede eleştirmenlerin, stratejilerin dayandığı araştırmanın örgütlü şiddet gruplarının tehlikesini küçümseyebileceğini söylediği anlatılır; ‘it’ bu nedenle ‘this research’ ifadesine, yani ‘the research on which the strategies are based’ seçeneğine gönderme yapar. ‘Heavy-handed policing’ yeni yaklaşımın zaten eleştirdiği yöntemdir; ‘the crowd’, ‘disorder’ ve ‘Europe’ ise bir tehlikeyi küçümseme eylemini gerçekleştiremez.

questions.passage:
Doctor: Your blood test results are mostly normal, but your vitamin D level is quite low.
Patient: ----
Doctor: Not necessarily. Many people who work indoors have low levels, especially in winter.

questions.text: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?

Could you recommend a good dentist nearby?
Why did you take the sample from my left arm?
questions.explanation: Doktor ‘Not necessarily’ diyerek kapalı mekânda çalışanlarda düşük D vitamini düzeyinin yaygın olduğunu açıklar; bu yanıt, düşük düzeyin ciddi bir hastalık anlamına gelip gelmediğini soran ‘Does that mean I have some kind of serious illness?’ sorusuna uyar. Sonuçların ne zaman ‘ready’ olacağı zaten bellidir; testin fiyatı (‘cost’), bir diş hekimi önerisi (‘dentist’) ve örneğin neden sol koldan (‘left arm’) alındığı soruları doktorun yanıtıyla bağlantılı değildir.

questions.passage:
Anna: Did you see that the city museum is going to return some of its artefacts to the countries they came from?
Ben: Yes, I did. ----
Anna: I don't think so. If anything, people may become more interested in the history of the collection.
Ben: That's a fair point; the publicity might even attract new visitors.
questions.text: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Which countries have the largest museums in the world?
Won't that make the museum far less popular with visitors?
How old is the museum building itself?
Have you ever worked in a museum?
Do you know when the museum closes on Sundays?
questions.explanation: Anna ‘I don't think so’ der ve insanların koleksiyonun tarihine daha çok ilgi duyabileceğini ekler; bu yanıt, eserlerin iadesinin müzeyi daha az popüler yapıp yapmayacağını soran ‘Won't that make the museum far less popular with visitors?’ sorusuna karşılık gelir. En büyük müzelerin hangi ülkelerde olduğu (‘largest’), binanın yaşı (‘building’), müzede çalışıp çalışmadığı (‘worked’) ve pazar kapanış saati (‘Sundays’) soruları bu yanıtla anlam kazanmaz.

questions.passage:

Researcher: ----

questions.text: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Only one: heavy rain at two of the sites meant we had to take some measurements a week late.
Yes, I'll start writing the report next week.
The sites were chosen by the previous team.
