The last shower of this kind took place more than a century ago.
Why did you stay outside for so long?
questions.explanation: Tom ‘Really? I had no idea’ diyerek yeni bir bilgi öğrendiğini belirtir ve ertesi gece yeniden denemeye karar verir; bu, meteorların çoğunun gece yarısından sonra görüldüğünü açıklayan cümleye uyar. Dürbün sorusu (‘binoculars’) ve neden uzun süre dışarıda kaldığını soran soru (‘stay outside’) ‘Really?’ yanıtına uymaz; televizyondan izlemek (‘television’) yeni bir bilgi vermez; son yağmurun bir yüzyıl önce olduğunu (‘century’) söylemek ise yeniden deneme kararıyla çelişir.

questions.text:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

Had it not been for the invention of the telescope, the moons of Jupiter would have remained unknown for much longer.
options: The telescope was invented in order to discover the moons of Jupiter.
Even without the telescope, the moons of Jupiter would have been discovered just as early.
The moons of Jupiter were known long before the telescope was invented.
The invention of the telescope delayed the discovery of Jupiter's moons.
The moons of Jupiter were discovered relatively early only because the telescope had been invented.
questions.explanation: ‘Had it not been for …’ (… olmasaydı) yapısı teleskop olmasaydı uyduların çok daha uzun süre bilinmeyeceğini, yani erken keşfin teleskop sayesinde olduğunu anlatır; ‘only because the telescope had been invented’ bunu verir. Teleskobun bu amaçla icat edildiği (‘in order to’), teleskop olmadan da aynı erkenlikte keşfedileceği (‘Even without’), uyduların çok önceden bilindiği (‘long before’) ve icadın keşfi geciktirdiği (‘delayed’) iddiaları özgün anlamla çelişir.

questions.text:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

The new screening programme is expected to save lives, but only if a sufficient number of people take part in it.
options: The screening programme will save lives regardless of how many people take part.
Many lives have already been saved by the new screening programme.
Few people are expected to take part in the programme because it does not save lives.
If too many people take part, the programme will fail to save lives.
Unless participation is high enough, the screening programme is unlikely to save lives.
questions.explanation: ‘Only if a sufficient number of people take part’ katılımın yeterli olmasını zorunlu koşul yapar; ‘Unless participation is high enough … unlikely to save lives’ aynı anlamı verir. Katılımdan bağımsız (‘regardless’) başarı, şimdiden kurtarılmış hayatlar (‘already been saved’), programın hayat kurtarmadığı için az katılım beklenmesi (‘expected’) ve fazla katılımın başarısızlık getirmesi (‘fail’) özgün cümleyle çelişir.

questions.text:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

The merchants were less concerned about the danger of shipwreck than about the risk of having their goods seized by pirates.
options: For the merchants, the risk of piracy was a greater worry than the danger of shipwreck.
The merchants were equally worried about shipwreck and piracy.
Shipwrecks worried the merchants more than piracy did.
The merchants were not concerned about either shipwreck or piracy.
Pirates often wrecked ships deliberately in order to seize the merchants' goods.
questions.explanation: ‘Less concerned about shipwreck than about … pirates’ tüccarların korsanlıktan daha çok kaygılandığını anlatır; ‘the risk of piracy was a greater worry’ bunu doğru aktarır. ‘Equally worried’ eşitlik kurar; batmanın daha çok kaygılandırdığını söyleyen ‘Shipwrecks worried’ karşılaştırmayı tersine çevirir; hiç kaygılanmadıklarını söyleyen ‘not concerned’ ve korsanların gemileri kasten batırdığı (‘deliberately’) iddiası ise özgün cümlede yoktur.

questions.passage: For several centuries, the English treasury recorded payments not on paper but on wooden sticks known as tallies. When a sum was paid, notches of different sizes, representing pounds, shillings and pence, were cut across a stick of hazel or willow. ---- Because the grain of the wood was unique, the two pieces would fit together perfectly only with each other, which made forgery extremely difficult. The system was finally abolished in 1826, and the burning of a vast stock of old tallies in 1834 is said to have started the fire that destroyed much of the old Palace of Westminster.
questions.text: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Hazel and willow trees grow widely across the British Isles.
Paper, by contrast, remained expensive in medieval England.
As a result, the treasury stopped accepting payments in coin.
The stick was then split lengthwise through the notches, and the payer and the treasury each kept one half.
Many tallies have survived in museums and archives to this day.
questions.explanation: Boşluktan sonra gelen ‘the two pieces’ (iki parça) ifadesi, çubuğun daha önce ikiye ayrıldığının söylenmesini gerektirir; çubuğun çentiklerden boyuna yarılıp ödeyenin ve hazinenin birer yarısını sakladığını anlatan cümle bunu sağlar. Ağaçların yaygınlığı (‘willow trees’), kâğıdın pahalılığı (‘expensive’), hazinenin madeni para kabul etmeyi bırakması (‘stopped accepting’) ve çubukların müzelerde korunması (‘museums’) ‘the two pieces’ ifadesinin göndereceği bir bölünmeden söz etmez.

questions.passage: For nearly two thousand years, European scholars accepted the ancient view that the heavens beyond the Moon were perfect and unchanging. In November 1572, however, a brilliant new star appeared in the constellation Cassiopeia, remaining visible even in daylight for several weeks. ---- His careful measurements showed that the object displayed no detectable shift in position against the background stars, which meant that it lay far beyond the Moon. The observation dealt a serious blow to the belief that change could occur only in the region close to the Earth.
questions.text: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Today, astronomers know that such objects are stars exploding at the end of their lives.
Cassiopeia is easily recognised by its W-shaped pattern of bright stars.
The Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe set out to determine whether the object was closer to the Earth than the Moon or much farther away.
Many people at the time interpreted the new star as a sign of coming disaster.
Telescopes would not be invented for almost another four decades.
questions.explanation: Boşluktan sonra gelen ‘His careful measurements’ ifadesi, ölçüm yapan bir kişinin önceden tanıtılmasını gerektirir; cismin Ay’dan yakın mı uzak mı olduğunu belirlemeye çalışan Tycho Brahe’yi anlatan cümle bunu sağlar. Bugünkü bilgiyi veren ‘exploding’ cümlesi, takımyıldızın biçimini anlatan ‘W-shaped’ cümlesi, halkın yorumunu anlatan ‘disaster’ cümlesi ve ‘Telescopes’ ile başlayan cümle ‘His’ zamirinin göndereceği bir kişi içermez.

questions.passage: Australia has one of the highest rates of skin cancer in the world, largely because a population of mainly European descent lives under intense sunlight. In the early 1980s, health authorities launched a national campaign urging people to cover their skin, apply sunscreen and wear a hat whenever they went outdoors. ---- Over the following decades, rates of the most dangerous form of skin cancer among younger Australians began to fall, a trend that many experts attribute at least partly to these efforts.
questions.text: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Skin cancer can also be caused by the use of artificial tanning beds.
Sunlight is also necessary for the body to produce vitamin D.
The message was later reinforced by policies such as requiring children to wear hats in school playgrounds.
However, the campaign was quickly abandoned because of its high cost.
Millions of tourists visit Australia's beaches every summer.
questions.explanation: Paragraf kampanyayı tanıtır ve sonunda ‘these efforts’ (bu çabalar) ile birden fazla önleme atıf yapar; boşluğa kampanyanın okul bahçelerinde şapka zorunluluğu gibi politikalarla pekiştirildiğini söyleyen cümle gelmelidir. Solaryumun (‘tanning beds’) da kansere yol açması ve D vitamini (‘vitamin’) bilgisi kampanyanın etkisi konusundan sapar; kampanyanın hemen terk edildiği (‘abandoned’) iddiası sonraki düşüşle çelişir; turistler (‘tourists’) ise konu dışıdır.

questions.passage: Since 2019, private companies have launched thousands of small satellites into low orbit to provide internet access around the world. ---- Astronomers have warned that, as the number of satellites grows, a significant proportion of the images taken by wide-field telescopes may be affected. İlk yapay uydunun 1957’de fırlatılması (‘Soviet Union’) ve kırsal bölgelerde internet erişimi (‘rural’) sorunu açıklamaz; uyduların coşkuyla karşılandığı (‘welcomed’) uyarılarla çelişir; iklimi izleyen uydular (‘climate’) ise konu dışıdır.

questions.passage: (I) Founded in 1602, the Dutch East India Company is often described as one of the first companies to issue shares that could be freely bought and sold by the public. (II) Long voyages to Asia required enormous sums of money and could take years to produce a return, which made them too risky for individual merchants. (III) By dividing the ownership of the company into many small shares, it spread this risk among thousands of investors. (IV) The spices brought back from Asia, such as nutmeg and cloves, were used both to flavour food and to make medicines. (V) Moreover, because shares could be sold on the Amsterdam exchange, investors were not obliged to wait for a voyage to end in order to recover their money.

options: I
II
III
IV

questions.explanation: Paragraf Hollanda Doğu Hindistan Şirketi’nin hisse senedi yoluyla riski yatırımcılara nasıl dağıttığını ve hisselerin borsada satılabilmesini anlatır. IV numaralı cümle Asya’dan getirilen baharatların yemekte ve ilaçta kullanılmasına geçerek şirketin finansman yönteminden sapar. questions.passage: For most of the twentieth century, agricultural research concentrated on monocultures, in which a single crop is grown across an entire field. Yet many traditional farming systems (1) ---- on intercropping, the practice of growing two or more crops together in the same field. A well-known example is the three sisters system of North America, in which maize, beans and squash were planted side by side: the maize provided a frame for the beans to climb, (2) ---- the broad leaves of the squash shaded the ground and suppressed weeds. Field trials on several continents suggest that such combinations often produce more food from a given area of land than the same crops grown separately, largely because each plant draws on light, water and nutrients in slightly different ways. Mixed fields may also be less (3) ---- to pests, since insects that specialise in one crop find it harder to locate their host. Why, then, has intercropping not been adopted more widely? The main obstacle is practical: modern machinery is designed to sow, spray and harvest one crop at a time, and managing several crops together (4) ---- more labour and knowledge. Researchers are now testing equipment that can handle crops grown in narrow alternating strips, an approach (5) ---- may allow some of the benefits of intercropping to be combined with mechanisation.

questions.passage:
Every organ in the body produces metabolic waste, and in most tissues this waste is carried away by the lymphatic system, a network of vessels that drains excess fluid back into the bloodstream. The brain, however, was long thought to lack such vessels, which left researchers puzzled as to how an organ with such high energy demands disposes of its by-products. A partial answer emerged in the early 2010s, when experiments on mice suggested that cerebrospinal fluid, the clear liquid surrounding the brain and spinal cord, is pumped along the narrow spaces that encircle blood vessels and then flows through brain tissue, collecting waste molecules before draining away. Because the process appeared to depend on a type of supporting cell called glia, its discoverers named it the glymphatic system.
The most striking finding concerned sleep. In sleeping mice, the spaces between brain cells expanded considerably, allowing fluid to flow more freely, and certain proteins were cleared markedly faster than in animals that were awake. Among them was beta-amyloid, which accumulates in clumps in the brains of people with Alzheimer's disease. The observation offered an appealing explanation for why we sleep at all: perhaps the brain must periodically go offline in order to clean itself. It also raised the possibility that chronically poor sleep might contribute to neurodegenerative disease.
Such conclusions, however, should be treated with caution. Most of the evidence still comes from rodents, whose brains differ from ours in size and structure, and some studies have questioned whether fluid really moves through brain tissue in the way first proposed, rather than merely spreading by diffusion. Measuring these flows in living humans also remains technically difficult. Even so, the idea has prompted a wave of research, and few scientists now doubt that sleep plays some part in maintaining the chemical environment of the brain.

Beneath almost any field or forest lies an extensive network of fungal threads, many of which are intimately connected to the roots of plants. These partnerships, known as mycorrhizas, are thought to involve the great majority of land plant species, including most major crops such as wheat, maize and soybeans. The arrangement is essentially a trade. The plant supplies the fungus with sugars produced through photosynthesis, which can amount to a significant share of the carbon it fixes. In return, the fungal threads, far thinner than roots and able to penetrate tiny pores in the soil, extend the plant's reach and deliver nutrients that would otherwise be hard to obtain, phosphorus in particular. Some studies also suggest that colonised plants cope better with drought and with certain diseases that originate in the soil.
Modern agriculture, however, has not always been kind to these partners. Repeated ploughing tears the fungal networks apart, and when crops receive abundant phosphorus fertiliser, many plants appear to reduce the amount of carbon they allocate to the fungus, presumably because they no longer need its services. Long periods of bare soil between crops can also deprive the fungi of the living roots on which they depend. As a consequence, intensively managed fields often contain far less fungal activity than undisturbed grassland.
Growing interest in the subject has given rise to a market for commercial inoculants, products containing fungal spores that farmers can add to the soil. questions.passage:
When legislators pass a law, they usually expect it to remain in force until it is deliberately repealed. A sunset clause reverses this assumption: it specifies that a law, or part of it, will expire automatically on a given date unless the legislature votes to renew it. The idea is far from new. The Roman Republic, for instance, granted emergency powers to a dictator for no more than six months, a limit intended to prevent temporary authority from becoming permanent. In modern times, sunset clauses have most often been attached to legislation passed in response to crises, such as the surveillance powers that several governments introduced after major terrorist attacks.
Advocates claim that such clauses offer two main benefits. First, they make it easier to pass urgent measures, since opponents may be more willing to accept controversial powers if they know these will lapse. Second, they compel lawmakers to revisit a law and examine whether it has actually achieved its aims, rather than allowing it to remain on the statute books through mere inertia. In principle, then, a sunset clause combines speed with accountability.
Critics, however, point out that this promise often goes unfulfilled. Renewal votes frequently take place under time pressure and with little genuine evaluation, so that measures described as temporary are extended again and again until they become permanent in all but name. Moreover, the expiry dates themselves may create uncertainty for businesses and public agencies that need to plan for the long term. Some scholars have also warned that the very existence of a sunset clause can make legislators less careful when drafting a law, on the assumption that any flaws can be corrected later. Whether these clauses strengthen democratic oversight thus appears to depend less on their wording than on the willingness of legislators to conduct serious reviews.

questions.passage:
After the amputation of an arm or a leg, a large majority of patients report that they can still feel the missing limb. Some describe it as moving, itching or clenched in an awkward position, and many experience phantom pain, which can be severe and remarkably persistent. For centuries, such reports were attributed to irritated nerve endings in the stump or even dismissed as imagination. Research since the late twentieth century, however, has located much of the explanation in the brain itself.
The surface of the brain contains a map of the body, in which neighbouring regions of the cortex receive sensations from neighbouring body parts. In this map, the area representing the hand happens to lie next to the area representing the face. When an arm is lost, the hand area no longer receives its usual input, and the surrounding regions appear to take it over. In a number of patients, touching the cheek has produced a vivid sensation in the phantom fingers, a finding consistent with this kind of reorganisation. Some researchers have proposed that a mismatch between what the brain expects and the absence of sensory feedback contributes to phantom pain, although the precise mechanism is still disputed.
This line of thinking inspired an unusually simple treatment. In mirror therapy, the patient places the intact limb in front of a mirror positioned so that its reflection appears exactly where the missing limb would be. When the patient moves the intact hand, the brain receives visual feedback suggesting that the phantom is moving too, and some patients report that cramps and pain ease. Clinical trials, however, have produced mixed results, and many of them involved only small numbers of participants. Mirror therapy is therefore generally regarded as a low-cost option worth trying rather than a reliable cure, and it is often combined with medication and other forms of rehabilitation.

In many criminal justice systems, the familiar image of a trial in which evidence is tested before a judge or jury bears little resemblance to the way most cases are actually resolved. In the United States, for instance, it is commonly estimated that well over ninety per cent of criminal convictions result not from trials but from guilty pleas, many of them obtained through plea bargaining. In such negotiations, the prosecution offers a concession, typically a reduced charge or a lighter sentence, in exchange for the defendant's admission of guilt, which spares the state the cost and uncertainty of a trial.
Defenders of the practice regard it as indispensable. Courts, they argue, could not possibly hold full trials for every case without an enormous increase in funding, and defendants who have genuinely committed an offence may benefit from a more lenient outcome and a quicker resolution. Victims, too, are spared the ordeal of giving evidence in court.
Critics, however, see serious dangers. The gap between the sentence offered in a bargain and the one likely to follow a conviction at trial, sometimes described as a trial penalty, can be so large that even innocent defendants may judge it safer to plead guilty, particularly if they are held in custody while awaiting trial. Because negotiations take place in private, they are also difficult to scrutinise, and the outcome may depend heavily on the skill of the defence lawyer. Indeed, among the convictions later overturned on the basis of new evidence are a number of cases in which the defendant had pleaded guilty to a crime he or she did not commit.
Although the practice is closely associated with the American system, versions of it have spread to a number of other countries, including several with civil-law traditions that once rejected it. Reformers there have generally tried to limit the risks by requiring judges to examine the evidence before approving any agreement.

options: why plea bargaining is so widely used and what risks it carries

questions.passage:
In many criminal justice systems, the familiar image of a trial in which evidence is tested before a judge or jury bears little resemblance to the way most cases are actually resolved. In the United States, for instance, it is commonly estimated that well over ninety per cent of criminal convictions result not from trials but from guilty pleas, many of them obtained through plea bargaining. In such negotiations, the prosecution offers a concession, typically a reduced charge or a lighter sentence, in exchange for the defendant's admission of guilt, which spares the state the cost and uncertainty of a trial.
Defenders of the practice regard it as indispensable. Courts, they argue, could not possibly hold full trials for every case without an enormous increase in funding, and defendants who have genuinely committed an offence may benefit from a more lenient outcome and a quicker resolution. Victims, too, are spared the ordeal of giving evidence in court.
Critics, however, see serious dangers. The gap between the sentence offered in a bargain and the one likely to follow a conviction at trial, sometimes described as a trial penalty, can be so large that even innocent defendants may judge it safer to plead guilty, particularly if they are held in custody while awaiting trial. Because negotiations take place in private, they are also difficult to scrutinise, and the outcome may depend heavily on the skill of the defence lawyer. Indeed, among the convictions later overturned on the basis of new evidence are a number of cases in which the defendant had pleaded guilty to a crime he or she did not commit.
Although the practice is closely associated with the American system, versions of it have spread to a number of other countries, including several with civil-law traditions that once rejected it. Reformers there have generally tried to limit the risks by requiring judges to examine the evidence before approving any agreement.

options: the difference between the sentence offered in a bargain and the probable sentence after a conviction at trial

questions.passage: (I) In ancient Athens, the assembly could decide once a year to hold a vote that would send a prominent citizen into exile, a procedure known as ostracism. questions.passage: Aviation is usually discussed in climate terms as a source of carbon dioxide, but a substantial part of its warming effect may in fact come from the thin white trails that aircraft leave behind them. Contrails form when the hot, humid exhaust of a jet engine mixes with the cold air of the upper troposphere, (1) ---- the water vapour to condense and freeze onto tiny soot particles. In dry air they vanish within seconds; in air that is already close to saturation with respect to ice, (2) ----, they can persist for hours and spread into extensive sheets of cirrus-like cloud. Such clouds reflect some incoming sunlight back to space, but they trap a greater amount of the heat radiated from the surface, particularly at night, so their net effect, on balance, appears to be one of (3) ----. Because only a small fraction of flights seem to produce the most persistent contrails, researchers have proposed that aircraft could avoid them by changing altitude slightly when crossing humid layers of air. The idea is attractive, (4) ---- it is not without difficulties: rerouting usually burns extra fuel, and forecasts of ice-saturated layers remain too imprecise (5) ---- airlines to rely on them routinely.
questions.text: (5) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: of
for
with
by
from
questions.explanation: ‘Too + sıfat + for + kişi + to do’ kalıbı gerekir: tahminler havayolu şirketlerinin güvenmesi için fazla belirsizdir, yani ‘for’. ‘Of’, ‘with’, ‘by’ ve ‘from’ mastarın öznesini bu kalıpta tanıtamaz.

questions.text: Had researchers not begun measuring carbon dioxide continuously at a remote mountain observatory in the late 1950s, ----.
options: the measurements are still being taken there every day
which is located far from any major source of pollution
because the instruments of the time were relatively crude
unless the observatory is supplied with more modern equipment
the steady rise in its atmospheric concentration might have been documented considerably later

questions.text: ----, philosophers of science have long debated whether the predictive success of a theory gives us good reason to believe that the unobservable entities it postulates actually exist.

So that experiments could be repeated more cheaply in the future
As soon as the first microscopes were constructed in the seventeenth century
Since a number of theories that once made accurate predictions were later abandoned as false

questions.text: The thymus, the organ in which T cells learn to distinguish the body's own tissues from foreign invaders, begins to shrink after puberty and is largely replaced by fat in old age, ----.
options: which may partly explain why older adults respond less effectively to infections they have never met before
so that the immune system could have recognised more pathogens
whereas the T cells that leave it had already been destroyed
even though it had been surgically removed in most patients
as if it were the largest organ in the human body

questions.text: Although attribution studies cannot establish that a particular heatwave was caused by climate change, ----.
options: because heatwaves have occurred throughout recorded history
since meteorologists had forecast it several days in advance
they can estimate how much more likely or intense global warming has made such an event
which means that its effects were confined to urban areas
if the temperatures had been recorded more accurately

questions.text: So rapidly do some respiratory viruses alter their surface proteins ----.

unless they are exposed to direct sunlight for several hours
than the bacteria that normally live in the human gut

that antibodies produced after one infection may fail to recognise the next variant

questions.text: ----, Galileo concluded that heavy and light bodies must fall at the same rate, without needing to drop anything at all.

Unless air resistance is ignored in such calculations
So that his students could attend the public demonstration
Because the bell tower in his city was visibly leaning

questions.text: Mast cells, which are abundant in the skin and in the lining of the airways, release histamine within seconds of detecting certain substances, ----.
options: an immediate response that helps against some parasites but also underlies many allergic symptoms
although they had been discovered before antibodies were described
so that the substances will be detected more slowly next time

whose number had doubled by the time the patient was born

questions.text: The higher the concentration of heat-trapping gases in the atmosphere, ----.

since water vapour is the most abundant of these gases
the greater the proportion of the heat radiated by the Earth's surface that is prevented from escaping to space

questions.text: David Hume argued that our confidence that the sun will rise tomorrow rests on nothing more than the habit formed by past experience, ----.

a challenge to the justification of inductive reasoning that philosophers have struggled to answer ever since
so that the problem could finally be solved by observation

since trillions of microbes live in the human intestine

İklim duyarlılığı, atmosferdeki karbondioksit miktarının iki katına çıkması durumunda yüzey sıcaklığının sonunda ne kadar artacağını ifade eder.

Tissues such as the eye and the brain are fully protected from inflammation because the immune system never reaches them.
Because the eye and the brain are rarely damaged permanently, the immune system can safely trigger strong inflammation there.

Inflammation in the eye and the brain is usually mild, although the immune system attacks these tissues more often than others.

Rakip iki açıklamadan daha az varsayıma dayananı tercih etme ilkesi, doğruluğun kesin bir ölçütü olmaktan çok pratik bir yol göstericidir.
options: The principle of preferring the explanation with fewer assumptions is the most reliable criterion of truth, as well as a practical guide.
The principle that rival explanations should rest on as many assumptions as possible is a practical guide rather than a criterion of truth.
Since the explanation with fewer assumptions is always true, the principle of preferring it is a definitive criterion rather than a practical guide.

İlkeyi en ‘reliable’ ölçüt sayan çeviri ‘olmaktan çok’ karşıtlığını kaybeder; ‘as many assumptions as possible’ ilkeyi tersine çevirir; ‘always true’ ifadesi asıl anlamla çelişir; daha çok varsayımlı açıklamanın ‘usually more practical’ olduğu iddiası ise cümlede yoktur.

questions.passage:
High above the Arctic in winter, at altitudes of roughly 15 to 50 kilometres, a vast cyclone of frigid air known as the stratospheric polar vortex circulates around the pole. Its westerly winds, which strengthen as the polar night deepens and the temperature contrast with lower latitudes grows, ordinarily act as a kind of barrier, confining the coldest air to high latitudes. Every few winters, however, this arrangement is dramatically disrupted. Large-scale atmospheric waves, generated when air flows over mountain ranges and across the temperature contrasts between land and sea, propagate upwards from the lower atmosphere and break in the stratosphere, decelerating the vortex and, in the most extreme cases, reversing its winds altogether. Within a matter of days, temperatures in the polar stratosphere can rise by 30 to 50 degrees Celsius, an event that atmospheric scientists, with characteristic understatement, call a sudden stratospheric warming.
What makes these episodes consequential for people at the surface is that their effects do not remain aloft. Over the following weeks, the disturbance frequently works its way downwards, weakening the westerly flow nearer the ground and causing the jet stream to meander. The result, though by no means inevitable, is an increased likelihood of prolonged cold spells over parts of northern Europe, Asia and North America, as Arctic air spills southwards. The severe cold that gripped much of Europe in early 2018 followed one such warming.
For forecasters, the phenomenon represents an unusual opportunity. Because the downward influence unfolds over several weeks, an observed warming offers advance indication of conditions well beyond the range of conventional weather forecasts, which typically lose much of their skill after about ten days. The signal is probabilistic rather than deterministic, however: roughly a third of such events appear to have little discernible influence at the surface, and the reasons for this variability are still debated. Whether a warming Arctic will make these disruptions more or less frequent is likewise uncertain, with different models yielding conflicting answers, and researchers caution against attributing any single harsh winter to climate change through this mechanism.
questions.text: The passage is mainly concerned with ----.
options: how disturbances high above the Arctic can influence weather near the ground weeks later, and why this matters for forecasting
the reasons why the polar vortex has weakened permanently as a result of climate change
the instruments that meteorologists use to measure temperatures in the stratosphere
the history of exceptionally severe winters in Europe over the past century
the role of mountain ranges in strengthening the westerly winds of the jet stream
questions.explanation: Metin stratosferdeki ani ısınmaların haftalar sonra yüzeydeki havayı nasıl etkileyebildiğini ve bunun tahmin için önemini anlatır; doğru seçenek budur. Kutup girdabının ‘permanently’ zayıfladığı iddiası metnin belirsizlik vurgusuyla çelişir; ölçüm ‘instruments’ ve Avrupa kışlarının ‘history’ konusu ele alınmaz; dağların ‘strengthening’ etkisi ise tersine, girdabı yavaşlatan dalgalarla ilgilidir.

High above the Arctic in winter, at altitudes of roughly 15 to 50 kilometres, a vast cyclone of frigid air known as the stratospheric polar vortex circulates around the pole. Its westerly winds, which strengthen as the polar night deepens and the temperature contrast with lower latitudes grows, ordinarily act as a kind of barrier, confining the coldest air to high latitudes. Every few winters, however, this arrangement is dramatically disrupted. Large-scale atmospheric waves, generated when air flows over mountain ranges and across the temperature contrasts between land and sea, propagate upwards from the lower atmosphere and break in the stratosphere, decelerating the vortex and, in the most extreme cases, reversing its winds altogether. Within a matter of days, temperatures in the polar stratosphere can rise by 30 to 50 degrees Celsius, an event that atmospheric scientists, with characteristic understatement, call a sudden stratospheric warming.
What makes these episodes consequential for people at the surface is that their effects do not remain aloft. Over the following weeks, the disturbance frequently works its way downwards, weakening the westerly flow nearer the ground and causing the jet stream to meander. The result, though by no means inevitable, is an increased likelihood of prolonged cold spells over parts of northern Europe, Asia and North America, as Arctic air spills southwards. The severe cold that gripped much of Europe in early 2018 followed one such warming.

The signal is probabilistic rather than deterministic, however: roughly a third of such events appear to have little discernible influence at the surface, and the reasons for this variability are still debated. Whether a warming Arctic will make these disruptions more or less frequent is likewise uncertain, with different models yielding conflicting answers, and researchers caution against attributing any single harsh winter to climate change through this mechanism.

questions.passage:
Textbook accounts of the immune system have traditionally drawn a sharp distinction between its two branches. The innate system, comprising cells such as macrophages and natural killer cells, responds within hours to broad molecular patterns shared by many microbes, but it was long assumed to have no memory: its reaction to a pathogen encountered for the hundredth time was thought to be no more effective than its reaction on the first occasion. Memory, by this account, was the exclusive preserve of the adaptive system, whose B and T lymphocytes take days to mount a response to a new threat but, once they have done so, leave behind long-lived cells that recognise that particular invader with remarkable precision.
Over the past two decades, this tidy division has been called into question. Experiments in mice, together with epidemiological observations in humans, have indicated that certain exposures can leave innate cells in a heightened state of readiness that persists for weeks or even months. The most widely studied example involves the tuberculosis vaccine BCG, which, according to several studies, appears to reduce deaths from infections unrelated to tuberculosis among infants in some low-income settings. The proposed explanation, termed trained immunity, is that the vaccine induces lasting changes in the way the DNA of innate cells and their precursors in the bone marrow is packaged, so that genes involved in inflammation can be switched on more rapidly whenever a subsequent threat appears.
Trained immunity differs from adaptive memory in one crucial respect: it is non-specific. The enhanced response is directed not against the original stimulus alone but against a broad range of pathogens, which is precisely what makes it attractive as a means of strengthening general resistance to infection. The same property, however, has a less welcome side. An innate system kept in a state of permanent alert might contribute to chronic inflammation, and some researchers suspect that inappropriate training could play a part in conditions such as atherosclerosis, the build-up of fatty deposits in the walls of arteries. Determining how to induce the beneficial effects without the harmful ones has therefore become a central challenge for the field.

questions.passage:
A widely held picture of science holds that a hypothesis is tested by deriving a prediction from it and checking that prediction against observation: if the prediction fails, the hypothesis is refuted. At the beginning of the twentieth century, the French physicist and historian Pierre Duhem pointed out a difficulty with this picture that has occupied philosophers ever since. A hypothesis, he observed, never yields a prediction on its own. To derive any observable consequence from a claim about, say, the nature of light, a physicist must also rely on a host of auxiliary assumptions concerning the functioning of the instruments, the absence of interfering factors and the accuracy of the other theories on which the design of the experiment depends. When the predicted result fails to appear, logic tells us only that at least one member of this whole collection is false; it does not tell us which.
The American philosopher W. V. O. Quine later extended the point in a more radical direction, arguing that, in principle, any statement could be retained in the face of recalcitrant evidence, provided that sufficiently drastic adjustments were made elsewhere in our system of beliefs. A related and stronger thesis holds that for any body of evidence there will always be more than one theory compatible with it, so that the evidence alone can never settle which theory we ought to accept.
It would be a mistake, however, to conclude that scientific choices are therefore arbitrary. Duhem himself maintained that scientists rely on what he called good sense to judge which assumption is most plausibly at fault, and the history of science bears this out. When the orbit of Uranus deviated from its predicted path in the nineteenth century, astronomers did not abandon Newtonian mechanics; they postulated an unseen planet, and Neptune was duly found. Yet when Mercury's orbit displayed a comparable anomaly, the analogous postulate of an undiscovered planet proved fruitless, and the discrepancy was eventually explained only by Einstein's general theory of relativity. Underdetermination, on this view, does not render rational choice impossible; it shows that such choice depends on a kind of judgement that logic alone cannot supply.

questions.passage:
From an immunological perspective, pregnancy poses a puzzle that has intrigued researchers since the 1950s, when the British biologist Peter Medawar first articulated it clearly. Because half of a fetus's genes are inherited from the father, the fetus carries proteins that the mother's immune system should, in principle, recognise as foreign. Organ grafts between genetically mismatched individuals are rejected unless the recipient's immunity is suppressed with powerful drugs, yet a fetus, which is in effect a partially mismatched graft, normally survives for nine months in intimate contact with maternal tissues. How this is achieved has turned out to be considerably more complicated than early researchers anticipated.
Medawar proposed three possible explanations: that the fetus is anatomically separated from the mother, that its tissues are immunologically immature, or that the maternal immune system is somehow suppressed during pregnancy. Each has since proved to contain an element of truth while being inadequate on its own. The placenta constitutes an interface rather than a sealed barrier, and fetal cells routinely cross into the mother's bloodstream, where some may persist for decades. Nor is the mother's immunity simply switched off; pregnant women continue to fight most infections effectively, although they are more vulnerable to certain ones, such as influenza.
Current evidence instead points to a combination of local and highly specific mechanisms. The cells of the placenta that come into direct contact with maternal blood display an unusual set of surface molecules that make them less conspicuous to some immune cells. Within the lining of the uterus, a population of regulatory T cells expands during pregnancy and appears to restrain responses directed specifically against fetal proteins. Remarkably, experiments in mice suggest that some of these regulatory cells persist after delivery and may make subsequent pregnancies with the same partner more successful. Failures of these mechanisms are thought to contribute to complications such as pre-eclampsia, a condition in which a disturbed relationship between the placenta and the maternal blood vessels raises the mother's blood pressure dangerously, though its causes are not yet fully understood.

The placenta constitutes an interface rather than a sealed barrier, and fetal cells routinely cross into the mother's bloodstream, where some may persist for decades. Nor is the mother's immunity simply switched off; pregnant women continue to fight most infections effectively, although they are more vulnerable to certain ones, such as influenza.
Current evidence instead points to a combination of local and highly specific mechanisms. The cells of the placenta that come into direct contact with maternal blood display an unusual set of surface molecules that make them less conspicuous to some immune cells. Within the lining of the uterus, a population of regulatory T cells expands during pregnancy and appears to restrain responses directed specifically against fetal proteins. Remarkably, experiments in mice suggest that some of these regulatory cells persist after delivery and may make subsequent pregnancies with the same partner more successful. Failures of these mechanisms are thought to contribute to complications such as pre-eclampsia, a condition in which a disturbed relationship between the placenta and the maternal blood vessels raises the mother's blood pressure dangerously, though its causes are not yet fully understood.

questions.passage:
For much of the twentieth century, an influential ideal held that science, at least in its core activity of evaluating hypotheses, should be free of ethical and political values. Values might legitimately influence which problems scientists choose to investigate or how their findings are applied, but the question of whether the evidence supports a hypothesis was regarded as a purely epistemic matter, to be settled by logic and data alone. In 1953 the philosopher Richard Rudner challenged this ideal with an argument that has since been considerably developed under the label of inductive risk.
Rudner's starting point was the observation that no empirical hypothesis is ever verified with certainty. In accepting or rejecting a hypothesis, therefore, a scientist must decide whether the evidence is strong enough, and how strong is enough depends on how serious the consequences of being wrong would be. We would demand far more evidence, he suggested, before declaring that a toxic ingredient in a medicine falls below a lethal level than before concluding that a batch of belt buckles is free of defects. Since judging the seriousness of an error is unavoidably a value judgement, values enter into the very heart of scientific reasoning.
Critics have responded in several ways. One influential reply holds that scientists need not accept or reject hypotheses at all; they can simply report probabilities and leave the decision to policymakers. Defenders of the argument point out, however, that this merely relocates the problem, since choices about which statistical methods to use, how to characterise ambiguous data and when to stop gathering evidence are themselves exposed to the risk of error. Recognising this does not imply that anything goes. Most proponents distinguish carefully between values that legitimately determine the level of evidence required and values that would improperly substitute for evidence, as when a desired conclusion is accepted regardless of the data. The challenge, on this view, is not to eliminate values from science, which may well be impossible, but to make their role transparent so that others can scrutinise it.
questions.text: The passage is mainly concerned with ----.
options: the history of regulations governing the safety of medicines since the 1950s
a proposal that policymakers should receive formal training in statistics
an argument that value judgements are involved in deciding whether the evidence is sufficient to accept a hypothesis
the reasons why scientists choose to investigate some problems rather than others
a plan to remove all ethical considerations from scientific research

İlaç güvenliği düzenlemelerinin ‘history’ konusu ele alınmaz; politika yapıcıların ‘training’ alması önerilmez; araştırma konusunun seçimi (‘investigate’) yalnızca değerlerin meşru olduğu kabul edilen alan olarak geçer; değerlerin tümüyle ‘remove’ edilmesi ise metnin sonunda olanaksız olabileceği söylenen bir hedeftir.

Student: I read that ice ages are set off by slow changes in the Earth's orbit. But surely those changes are far too small to bury whole continents under ice?
Lecturer: ----
Student: So the orbit only provides the initial push, and the climate system itself does the rest.
Lecturer: Exactly, which is one reason why scientists take the warming effect of today's rising carbon dioxide so seriously.
questions.text: Diyalogdaki boşluğa hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: On their own, they would be. But a slight cooling lets snow survive the summer, and the spreading ice and falling carbon dioxide levels then amplify the change.
The most recent glacial period ended roughly twelve thousand years ago.
You are right, and that is why there have never actually been any ice ages.
The Earth takes about 365 days to complete one orbit around the sun.
Most of the ice on the planet today is found in Antarctica and Greenland.
questions.explanation: Öğrenci yörüngenin yalnızca ilk itkiyi verdiğini, gerisini iklim sisteminin yaptığını söyler; bu, küçük yörünge değişimlerinin tek başına yetersiz olduğunu ama karın yazı atlatması, buzun yayılması ve karbondioksitin azalmasıyla etkinin büyüdüğünü anlatan yanıttan çıkar. Son buzul döneminin ‘twelve thousand’ yıl önce bitmesi ve buzun bugün ‘Antarctica’ ile Grönland’da bulunması soruyu yanıtlamaz; buzul çağlarının ‘never actually’ yaşanmadığı iddiası öğrencinin sonucuyla çelişir; ‘365 days’ bilgisi ise yükseltme mekanizmasını açıklamaz.

Because the information is gathered after the diagnosis, cases may search their memories far more thoroughly than controls, (3) ---- a distortion known as recall bias. A mother whose child was born with a malformation, for instance, is likely to scrutinise every medication she took during pregnancy, whereas the mother of a healthy infant may simply have forgotten a brief course of tablets. The resulting difference in reported exposure can produce an association that (4) ---- entirely to memory rather than to any genuine effect. To reduce this risk, investigators increasingly rely on records (5) ---- before the outcome was known, such as prescription databases.
questions.text: (3) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: in spite of
on behalf of
giving rise to
at the expense of
regardless of
questions.explanation: Vakaların belleklerini kontrollerden daha ayrıntılı taraması ‘recall bias’ denen çarpıklığa yol açar; bu sonucu ‘giving rise to’ (-e yol açarak) bildirir. ‘In spite of’ ve ‘regardless of’ karşıtlık ya da önemsememe anlatır; ‘on behalf of’ (adına) ve ‘at the expense of’ (pahasına) çarpıklığın ortaya çıkışını anlatmaz.

is due
results
relies

questions.text: (5) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: compiling
compiled
to compile
having compiled
compile
questions.explanation: Kayıtlar sonuç bilinmeden önce derlenmiştir; isimden sonra gelen edilgen sıfat-fiil ‘compiled’ (… önce derlenmiş kayıtlar) gerekir. ‘Compiling’ ve ‘having compiled’ etken anlam verir ve kayıtları derleyen özne yapar; ‘to compile’ amaç ya da gelecek bildirir; ‘compile’ ise çekimsiz yalın fiil olarak burada dilbilgisel değildir.

questions.passage: In 1957 the economist Anthony Downs formalised an idea that had been sketched decades earlier: if voters can be arranged along a single left-right dimension and each supports the party closest to their own position, two competing parties will tend to (1) ---- towards the centre, (2) ---- neither can expect to win if it drifts away from the voter in the middle of the distribution. This so-called median voter theorem offered an elegant explanation for why the platforms of major parties often appear strikingly similar. Its assumptions, however, are (3) ---- restrictive. Real electorates rarely divide along a single dimension, turnout is far from universal, and parties depend on activists and donors (4) ---- views tend to be more extreme than those of the average citizen. Empirical studies have found that politicians frequently diverge from the median position, (5) ---- in systems where primary elections reward ideological commitment.
questions.text: (1) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: collapse
deviate
retaliate
abstain
converge
questions.explanation: İki partinin ortadaki seçmenden uzaklaşamayacağı için merkeze doğru ‘converge’ (yakınsamak, birbirine yaklaşmak) etmesi beklenir; sonraki cümlede programların ‘strikingly similar’ olması bunu doğrular. ‘Deviate’ (sapmak) tam tersi anlamdadır; ‘collapse’ (çökmek), ‘retaliate’ (misilleme yapmak) ve ‘abstain’ (çekimser kalmak) merkeze doğru bir hareketi anlatmaz.

questions.text: (2) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: since
unless
whereas
in case
even if
questions.explanation: Partilerin merkeze yaklaşmasının nedeni, hiçbirinin ortadaki seçmenden uzaklaşırsa kazanmayı bekleyememesidir; neden bildiren ‘since’ gerekir. ‘Unless’ koşul, ‘whereas’ karşıtlık, ‘in case’ önlem (-e karşı) ve ‘even if’ karşıt koşul bildirir; bunların hiçbiri iki yargı arasındaki neden-sonuç ilişkisini kurmaz.

questions.text: (3) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: scarcely
reluctantly
accidentally
unanimously
considerably
questions.explanation: ‘However’ kuramın varsayımlarının oldukça kısıtlayıcı olduğunu bildirir ve sonraki cümle bu kısıtları sıralar; derece bildiren ‘considerably’ (oldukça, epeyce) uyar. ‘Scarcely’ (neredeyse hiç) anlamı tersine çevirir; ‘reluctantly’ (isteksizce), ‘accidentally’ (kazara) ve ‘unanimously’ (oybirliğiyle) ‘restrictive’ sıfatını anlamlı biçimde nitelemez.

questions.passage: In 1957 the economist Anthony Downs formalised an idea that had been sketched decades earlier: if voters can be arranged along a single left-right dimension and each supports the party closest to their own position, two competing parties will tend to (1) ---- towards the centre, (2) ---- neither can expect to win if it drifts away from the voter in the middle of the distribution. questions.text: (4) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: which
whom
whose
what
where
questions.explanation: Boşluktan sonra gelen ‘views’ ismi ‘activists and donors’a aittir (onların görüşleri); iyelik bildiren ‘whose’ gerekir. ‘Which’ ve ‘whom’ ardından bir isim almadan ilgi cümlesi kurar; ‘what’ önünde bir isim varken kullanılamaz; ‘where’ ise yer bildirir.

questions.passage: In 1957 the economist Anthony Downs formalised an idea that had been sketched decades earlier: if voters can be arranged along a single left-right dimension and each supports the party closest to their own position, two competing parties will tend to (1) ---- towards the centre, (2) ---- neither can expect to win if it drifts away from the voter in the middle of the distribution. questions.text: (5) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: scarcely
accordingly
otherwise
particularly
whereby
questions.explanation: Politikacıların ortanca konumdan sapması özellikle ön seçimlerin ideolojik bağlılığı ödüllendirdiği sistemlerde görülür; ‘particularly’ (özellikle) bu vurguyu yapar. ‘Scarcely’ (neredeyse hiç) anlamı çelişkili kılar; ‘accordingly’ (buna göre) ve ‘otherwise’ (aksi takdirde) bir edat öbeğinden önce bu anlamı vermez; ‘whereby’ ise ardından tam bir cümle ister.

questions.text: Because the founding population of the island consisted of only a few dozen individuals, ----.
options: the island had remained uninhabited until the arrival of European sailors
certain inherited disorders that are rare elsewhere occur there at unusually high frequencies
unless genetic testing is made available to all of its residents
whereas most mainland populations are descended from many thousands of founders
the climate of the island had become considerably warmer by then
questions.explanation: Kurucu topluluğun çok küçük olması, başka yerlerde nadir görülen kalıtsal bozuklukların adada sık görülmesinin nedenidir; ‘because’ ile kurulan neden-sonuç ilişkisini bu seçenek tamamlar. Adanın Avrupalı denizcilere kadar ‘uninhabited’ kalması ve iklimin ‘warmer’ hâle gelmesi kurucu sayısının sonucu değildir; ‘unless’ ve ‘whereas’ ile başlayan yan cümleler ise ana cümle olmadığından cümleyi tamamlamaz.

questions.text: ----, the researchers concluded that the apparent protective effect of the vitamin had probably been an artefact of the healthier lifestyles of those who chose to take it.
options: Unless the observational studies are repeated in other countries
So that the participants would not know which pill they were taking
When a large randomised trial found no difference between the vitamin and placebo groups
Even though the trial had confirmed the earlier observational findings
Since the vitamin is both cheap and widely available
questions.explanation: Gözlemsel çalışmalardaki koruyucu etkinin sağlıklı yaşam tarzından kaynaklanan bir yanılsama olduğu sonucuna, randomize bir denemede vitamin ve plasebo grupları arasında fark bulunamayınca varılır. ‘Unless … repeated’ şimdiki/gelecek koşul kurar ve geçmiş ana cümleyle uyuşmaz; ‘So that … pill’ körleme amacını anlatır, sonucu açıklamaz; ‘confirmed’ içeren seçenek sonuçla çelişir; vitaminin ‘cheap’ olması da böyle bir sonucun gerekçesi olamaz.

questions.text: The government set up a sovereign wealth fund so that ----.
options: oil prices had fallen sharply during the previous decade
which was modelled on similar funds in other oil-exporting states
since the fund's managers are appointed by parliament
it will have been abolished by the time of the next election
a portion of the oil revenues could be saved for future generations rather than spent immediately
questions.explanation: ‘So that’ amaç bildirir; fonun kurulma amacı petrol gelirlerinin bir kısmının hemen harcanmak yerine gelecek kuşaklar için biriktirilmesidir. Fiyatların ‘fallen’ olduğunu söyleyen geçmiş zamanlı cümle amaç bildirmez; ‘which … modelled’ ilgi cümlesi ve ‘since … appointed’ neden cümlesi ‘so that’ ardından gelemez; fonun ‘abolished’ edilmesi ise kuruluş amacı olamaz.

questions.text: Just as the wings of bats and birds evolved independently from different ancestral structures, ----.
options: bats are classified as mammals, whereas birds are descended from dinosaurs
the camera-like eyes of octopuses and vertebrates arose separately in lineages that had diverged long before either acquired them
if flight had not evolved more than once in the history of life
which explains why fossils of the earliest birds are so rare
many flying insects are active only at night
questions.explanation: ‘Just as’ benzerlik kurar: yarasa ve kuş kanatları gibi ahtapot ve omurgalı gözleri de birbirinden bağımsız olarak ortaya çıkmıştır; iki örnek aynı olguyu (bağımsız evrim) gösterir. Yarasaların ‘mammals’ olarak sınıflandırılması ve böceklerin ‘night’ etkinliği bağımsız evrimin ikinci bir örneği değildir; ‘if flight had not’ koşulu ve ‘which explains … fossils’ ilgi cümlesi ana cümle oluşturmaz.

questions.text: Unless an exposure can be shown to precede the outcome it is thought to cause, ----.
options: it cannot plausibly be regarded as a cause of that outcome
the study had been designed to measure it accurately
researchers measured both of them at the same time
whether the association between them is strong or weak
although many cross-sectional surveys ignore this requirement
questions.explanation: ‘Unless’ ile kurulan koşul (etkenin sonuçtan önce geldiği gösterilemezse) gelecek/genel bir sonuç ister: o etken sonucun nedeni sayılamaz. Geçmiş zamanlı ‘had been designed’ ve ‘measured both’ cümleleri gerçek koşulla uyuşmaz ve anlamca bağlanmaz; ‘whether … strong’ ve ‘although … surveys’ ise yan cümle olduğundan ana cümle kuramaz.

questions.text: Far from reducing corruption, ----.
options: most citizens welcomed the anti-corruption campaign launched in the capital
since the courts had been thoroughly reformed several years earlier
the privatisation programme enabled a small circle of well-connected businessmen to acquire state assets at a fraction of their value
which had been the principal aim of the international lenders
corruption had already been declining steadily before the reforms
questions.explanation: ‘Far from reducing corruption’ (yolsuzluğu azaltmak şöyle dursun) bir şeyin yolsuzluğu tam tersine artırdığını bildirir ve ana cümlenin öznesi bu işi yapan şey olmalıdır: özelleştirme programı devlet varlıklarının bir avuç iş insanına ucuza geçmesine yol açmıştır. Vatandaşların kampanyayı ‘welcomed’ etmesi ve yolsuzluğun ‘declining’ olması bu karşıtlığı kurmaz; ‘since … courts’ ve ‘which … lenders’ ise ana cümle değildir.

questions.text: The peacock's elaborate tail, which seems only to impair its owner's chances of escaping predators, ----.
options: whereas peahens are considerably less colourful than males
is it more common among birds living in tropical regions
because predators find it harder to spot in dense forest
although Darwin had travelled widely in South America
posed a puzzle for Darwin until he proposed that it had evolved because females preferred to mate with males possessing it
questions.explanation: Özne ‘The peacock's elaborate tail’ ve ilgi cümlesinden sonra ana fiil gerekir; ‘posed a puzzle …’ hem yüklemi verir hem de kuyruğun dişilerin tercihiyle (eşeysel seçilim) evrimleştiği açıklamasını sunar. ‘Whereas … peahens’, ‘because … predators’ ve ‘although … travelled’ yan cümledir ve yüklem sağlamaz; ‘is it more common’ ise soru düzenindedir ve bildirme cümlesine uymaz.

questions.text: The trial was designed in such a way that neither the patients nor the doctors treating them knew ----.
options: so that the results could be analysed more quickly
although the trial lasted for more than two years
since the placebo tasted exactly like the drug
had they been informed about the risks
who was receiving the active drug and who was receiving the placebo
questions.explanation: Çift körleme düzeninde ne hastalar ne de doktorlar kimin etkin ilacı, kimin plaseboyu aldığını bilir; ‘knew’ fiilinin nesnesi olacak bir isim cümlesi gerekir. ‘So that … analysed’ amaç, ‘although … lasted’ karşıtlık ve ‘since … tasted’ neden bildirir ve ‘knew’ fiilinin nesnesi olamaz; ‘had they been informed’ ise devrik koşul yapısıdır ve cümleyi tamamlamaz.

questions.text: So heavily did the economy depend on cocoa exports that ----.
options: farmers generally prefer to grow cocoa rather than coffee
cocoa is grown mainly in humid regions near the equator
a single poor harvest could push the government into a budget crisis
unless world prices remain stable for several years
although the government had taxed cocoa exports heavily
questions.explanation: ‘So heavily … that’ yapısı aşırı bağımlılığın sonucunu ister: tek bir kötü hasat hükümeti bütçe krizine sürükleyebilir. Çiftçilerin kakaoyu ‘coffee’ yerine tercih etmesi ve kakaonun ‘equator’ yakınında yetişmesi bağımlılığın sonucu değildir; ‘unless … prices’ ve ‘although … taxed’ ise yan cümledir ve sonuç cümlesi oluşturmaz.

questions.text: Whereas most human traits are shaped by a large number of genes, each with only a small effect, ----.
options: genes are made of DNA, which is found in nearly every cell of the body
if environmental factors are also taken into account
which makes their influence difficult to detect
the effect of each gene can be measured by comparing siblings
a few conditions, such as sickle-cell disease, result from a change in a single gene
questions.explanation: ‘Whereas’ karşıtlık kurar: çoğu özellik küçük etkili çok sayıda gene bağlıyken orak hücre hastalığı gibi birkaç durum tek bir gendeki değişiklikten kaynaklanır. Genlerin ‘DNA’dan oluşması ve etkilerin ‘siblings’ karşılaştırmasıyla ölçülmesi tek gen–çok gen karşıtlığını kurmaz; ‘if … environmental’ koşulu ve ‘which makes …’ ilgi cümlesi ise ana cümle değildir.

questions.text:
Aşağıdaki İngilizce cümlenin anlamca en yakın Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir?

Had the trial lasted longer, rare side effects that appear only after several years of use might have been detected.
options: Deneme uzun sürdüğü için birkaç yıllık kullanımdan sonra görülen seyrek yan etkiler de saptanmıştır.
Deneme daha uzun sürseydi, ancak birkaç yıllık kullanımdan sonra ortaya çıkan seyrek yan etkiler saptanabilirdi.
Seyrek yan etkiler ortaya çıkmadan önce denemenin birkaç yıl daha sürdürülmesine karar verilmiştir.
Deneme daha uzun sürseydi bile, birkaç yıl sonra ortaya çıkan yan etkilerin hiçbiri saptanamazdı.
Birkaç yıllık kullanımdan sonra ortaya çıkan yan etkiler nedeniyle deneme erken sonlandırılmıştır.
questions.explanation: ‘Had the trial lasted longer’ (deneme daha uzun sürseydi), ‘appear only after several years’ (ancak birkaç yıl sonra ortaya çıkan) ve ‘might have been detected’ (saptanabilirdi) doğru karşılıkta eksiksizdir. ‘Sürdüğü için … saptanmıştır’ koşulu gerçekleşmiş bir olguya çevirir; sürdürmeye ‘karar’ verildiği ve denemenin ‘sonlandırılmıştır’ olduğu bilgileri cümlede yoktur; ‘bile … hiçbiri saptanamazdı’ ise anlamı tersine çevirir.

questions.text:
Aşağıdaki İngilizce cümlenin anlamca en yakın Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir?

The extent to which a country benefits from its natural resources depends less on the size of its reserves than on the quality of its institutions.
options: Bir ülkenin doğal kaynaklarından yararlanabilmesi için hem büyük rezervlere hem de güçlü kurumlara sahip olması gerekir.
Kurumların niteliği, bir ülkenin elindeki rezervlerin miktarıyla doğrudan orantılıdır.
Bir ülkenin doğal kaynaklarından ne ölçüde yararlandığı, rezervlerinin büyüklüğünden çok kurumlarının niteliğine bağlıdır.
Doğal kaynakları sınırlı olan ülkeler, kurumlarını güçlendirerek rezerv eksikliklerini telafi edebilir.
Bir ülkenin doğal kaynaklardan elde ettiği gelir, rezervleri büyüdükçe kurumlarının niteliğini de artırır.
questions.explanation: ‘The extent to which’ (ne ölçüde) ve ‘depends less on … than on …’ (…den çok …e bağlıdır) yapıları doğru karşılıkta aynen korunmuştur. Her ikisinin de ‘gerekir’ olduğunu söyleyen seçenek karşılaştırmayı ortadan kaldırır; kurumların rezervlerle ‘orantılıdır’ demesi ve rezervler ‘büyüdükçe’ kurumların iyileşmesi ilişkiyi tersine çevirir; eksikliklerin ‘telafi’ edilmesi ise cümlede yoktur.

questions.text:
Aşağıdaki İngilizce cümlenin anlamca en yakın Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir?

Far from being a ladder of progress, evolution is better described as a branching bush in which many lineages have died out.
options: Evrim, bir ilerleme merdiveni olmaktan çok, birçok soy hattının yok olduğu dallı budaklı bir çalı olarak tanımlanmaya daha uygundur.
Evrim, her basamağında türlerin daha gelişmiş hâle geldiği bir ilerleme merdiveni olarak tanımlanabilir.
Birçok soy hattı yok olduğu için evrimin bir çalıya benzediği düşüncesi artık terk edilmiştir.
Evrim bir ilerleme merdivenine benzese de bazı soy hatları zamanla dallanarak çoğalmıştır.
Soyu tükenen türlerin çoğu, evrim merdiveninin en alt basamaklarında yer alır.
questions.explanation: ‘Far from being a ladder of progress’ (bir ilerleme merdiveni olmaktan çok) ve ‘better described as a branching bush’ (dallı budaklı bir çalı olarak tanımlanmaya daha uygun) doğru karşılıkta vardır. Evrimi her basamağında ‘gelişmiş’ türlerin yer aldığı bir merdiven olarak tanımlayan seçenek anlamı tersine çevirir; çalı benzetmesinin ‘terk’ edildiği, evrimin merdivene ‘benzese’ de denilmesi ve ‘tükenen’ türlerin alt basamaklarda olduğu iddiaları özgün cümleyle çelişir.

questions.text:
Aşağıdaki Türkçe cümlenin anlamca en yakın İngilizce karşılığı hangisidir?

Gözlemsel çalışmalar iki değişken arasında bir ilişki ortaya koyabilse de birinin diğerine neden olduğunu tek başına kanıtlayamaz.
options: Observational studies cannot reveal any association between two variables unless one causes the other.
Since observational studies prove that one variable causes another, they are preferred to experiments.
Although observational studies can reveal an association between two variables, they cannot on their own prove that one causes the other.
Observational studies can reveal an association only if they are combined with other kinds of evidence.
Although two variables may be associated, observational studies usually show that neither causes the other.
questions.explanation: ‘Ortaya koyabilse de’ (although … can reveal), ‘tek başına’ (on their own) ve ‘kanıtlayamaz’ (cannot prove) doğru karşılıkta eksiksizdir. ‘Unless’ ile kurulan koşul, çalışmaların nedenselliği kanıtladığını söyleyip deneylere ‘preferred’ olduğunu belirten seçenek, ilişkinin ancak başka kanıtla ‘combined’ edildiğinde görüleceği iddiası ve hiçbirinin neden olmadığını (‘neither’) gösterdikleri yargısı özgün cümlede yoktur.

questions.text:
Aşağıdaki Türkçe cümlenin anlamca en yakın İngilizce karşılığı hangisidir?

Ticaret engellerinin kaldırılması bir ülkenin toplam refahını artırsa bile bazı sektörlerdeki işçiler bundan zarar görebilir.
options: Removing trade barriers harms workers in all sectors, so it reduces a country's overall welfare.
Because some workers are harmed, countries should not remove their trade barriers.
Trade barriers increase a country's overall welfare only if workers in every sector benefit from them.
Workers in some sectors benefit from the removal of trade barriers, whereas the overall welfare of the country declines.
Even if removing trade barriers increases a country's overall welfare, workers in some sectors may be harmed by it.
questions.explanation: ‘Artırsa bile’ (even if … increases), ‘toplam refah’ (overall welfare) ve ‘bazı sektörlerdeki işçiler … zarar görebilir’ (workers in some sectors may be harmed) doğru karşılıkta vardır. Tüm sektörlerin zarar görüp refahın ‘reduces’ olduğunu söyleyen seçenek, engellerin kaldırılmaması gerektiğini (‘should’) savunan öneri, refahın ancak her sektör ‘benefit’ sağlarsa artacağı koşulu ve refahın ‘declines’ olduğu iddiası özgün anlamı bozar.

Aşağıdaki Türkçe cümlenin anlamca en yakın İngilizce karşılığı hangisidir?

Kardeşler arasında görülen benzerliklerin ne kadarının genlerden, ne kadarının ortak yetiştirilme ortamından kaynaklandığını belirlemek oldukça güçtür.
options: Siblings resemble each other mainly because they share the same genes rather than the same upbringing.
Determining whether siblings share the same genes is more difficult than measuring their upbringing.
The similarities between siblings are easier to explain than those between unrelated children raised together.
It is rather difficult to determine how much of the similarity observed between siblings stems from genes and how much from a shared upbringing.

questions.passage:
For much of the twentieth century, the history of life was depicted as a tree whose branches, once separated, never rejoined: genes were assumed to pass only vertically, from parents to offspring, so that the relationships between organisms could in principle be reconstructed by comparing their inherited sequences. The sequencing of microbial genomes from the 1990s onwards seriously complicated this picture. It became apparent that bacteria and archaea routinely acquire genetic material from unrelated organisms, a process known as horizontal or lateral gene transfer. Such material may be taken up directly from the environment after the death of another cell, carried between cells by viruses, or exchanged through direct contact by means of small circular DNA molecules called plasmids.
The practical consequences of this capacity are most evident in medicine. Genes conferring resistance to antibiotics are frequently located on plasmids, and a resistance trait that has arisen in one bacterial species may therefore spread to others, including dangerous pathogens, far more rapidly than would be possible through mutation and vertical inheritance alone. Hospitals, where antibiotics are used intensively and many bacterial species coexist, provide particularly favourable conditions for such exchanges.
The theoretical consequences are no less significant. Because a single bacterial genome may contain genes of diverse origins, different genes can yield conflicting accounts of the same organism's ancestry, and some microbiologists have argued that, at least among microbes, the history of life resembles a web or network more closely than a tree. Others regard this conclusion as premature, pointing out that a core of genes involved in fundamental processes such as protein synthesis appears to be transferred only rarely and continues to support a broadly tree-like pattern. What is no longer seriously disputed is that, for single-celled organisms, inheritance cannot be understood as a strictly vertical affair.
questions.text: The passage is mainly concerned with ----.
options: how the discovery of gene exchange between unrelated microbes has affected both medicine and the way evolutionary history is represented
the development of new antibiotics designed specifically to destroy plasmids
the reasons why viruses are more dangerous than bacteria in hospitals
a method for sequencing microbial genomes more cheaply than before
the debate over whether archaea should be classified as a kind of bacteria

Plazmitleri yok eden yeni ‘antibiotics’ geliştirilmesi, virüslerin hastanelerde daha ‘dangerous’ olması, genom dizilemenin ucuz bir ‘method’u ve arkelerin ‘classified’ edilmesi tartışması metinde ele alınmaz.

questions.passage:
Observational epidemiology faces a persistent difficulty: people who differ in one respect, such as how much alcohol they drink, usually differ in many others as well, and some of these other characteristics may themselves influence health. Statistical adjustment can reduce the resulting distortion, known as confounding, but only for factors that have been measured, and measured accurately. Randomised trials avoid the problem by assigning exposures by chance, yet for many exposures of interest, including long-term alcohol consumption or body weight, such trials would be impractical, unethical or prohibitively expensive.
Mendelian randomisation attempts to exploit a natural substitute for the investigator's coin toss. Because the variants of a gene that an individual inherits are allocated more or less randomly at conception, and are fixed before any disease develops, a genetic variant that reliably influences an exposure can serve as a proxy for it. If people carrying a variant associated with higher levels of a particular blood lipid also turn out to have more heart disease, and the variant has no other route to the heart, the comparison suggests that the lipid itself plays a causal role. Since the genetic difference cannot have been caused by the disease, the method also guards against reverse causation, in which an early stage of illness alters the very behaviour under study.
The approach rests, however, on assumptions that are difficult to verify. Many variants affect several traits at once, a phenomenon called pleiotropy, and if a variant influences disease through a pathway other than the exposure of interest, the inference collapses. Moreover, most individual variants have only small effects, so very large samples are required to detect anything at all. Practitioners therefore increasingly combine multiple variants and apply a range of sensitivity analyses, while cautioning that the method complements rather than replaces experimental evidence.
questions.text: The first paragraph mainly serves to ----.
options: argue that randomised trials should no longer be used in epidemiology
describe the harmful effects of long-term alcohol consumption on health
show that statistical adjustment can eliminate confounding entirely
explain how genetic variants are allocated at conception
outline the methodological problem that the technique described later is meant to address

Denemelerin ‘no longer’ kullanılmaması önerilmez; alkolün ‘harmful’ etkileri yalnızca örnektir; düzeltmenin karıştırıcılığı ‘eliminate’ ettiği iddiası metinle çelişir; varyantların ‘conception’ sırasında dağılımı ise ikinci paragrafın konusudur.

questions.passage:
It might seem self-evident that a country endowed with abundant oil, gas or minerals should enjoy faster economic growth than one without such wealth. Yet from the 1990s onwards a substantial body of research suggested the opposite: on average, economies heavily dependent on natural resource exports appeared to have grown more slowly over the preceding decades than comparable economies with fewer resources, and many were also more prone to authoritarian rule and civil conflict. This apparent paradox came to be known as the resource curse.
Several mechanisms have been proposed to account for it. Large export revenues tend to raise the value of the national currency, which makes manufacturing and agriculture less competitive abroad, a process often labelled Dutch disease after the effects of natural gas discoveries in the Netherlands. Commodity prices, moreover, are notoriously volatile, so that governments which expand spending during booms may be forced into abrupt cuts when prices collapse. Perhaps most importantly, revenues flowing directly into state coffers can free rulers from the need to tax their citizens, thereby weakening one of the principal channels through which populations have historically demanded accountability in return for their contributions.
More recent scholarship has nonetheless qualified the original findings. Some economists contend that the statistical association partly reflects how resource dependence was measured: a country that exports little apart from oil may appear dependent precisely because the rest of its economy has failed, rather than failing because of oil. Moreover, the experience of countries such as Norway and Botswana, which managed their resource wealth comparatively prudently, suggests that the curse is not inevitable. The prevailing view is thus that natural resources tend to amplify the effects of existing institutions: where these are accountable and transparent, resource revenues can finance development, whereas where they are weak, such revenues may entrench those already in power.

options: How the Netherlands Discovered Natural Gas
The Rise of Manufacturing in Oil-Rich Countries
Why Commodity Prices Always Rise in the Long Run
When Wealth Becomes a Burden: Reassessing the Resource Curse

Hollanda'nın doğal gazı nasıl ‘Discovered’ ettiği yalnızca bir terimin kaynağıdır; imalatın ‘Rise’ı metindekinin tersidir; fiyatların ‘Always Rise’ ettiği iddiası metindeki ‘volatile’ ile çelişir; ‘Civil War in Northern Europe’ ise metinde ele alınmaz.

questions.passage:
From an evolutionary standpoint, sexual reproduction is something of an embarrassment. An asexual female produces daughters that can each bear offspring of their own, whereas a sexual female devotes roughly half of her reproductive effort to sons, who cannot bear young. All else being equal, an asexual lineage should therefore increase in number about twice as fast as a sexual one, a handicap that the biologist John Maynard Smith termed the twofold cost of sex. Sex additionally requires finding and courting a partner and, by reshuffling genes in every generation, it can break up combinations that have already proved successful. That most complex organisms nevertheless reproduce sexually implies that sex must confer some substantial benefit.
One of the most influential explanations, the Red Queen hypothesis, locates that benefit in the perpetual contest between hosts and their parasites. The name alludes to the character in Lewis Carroll's Through the Looking-Glass who explains that it takes all the running one can do to remain in the same place. Parasites, which typically have far shorter generation times than their hosts, rapidly evolve to exploit whichever host genotypes are most common. By generating offspring with novel genetic combinations, sexual reproduction turns the host population into a moving target, so that any given genotype is less likely to be one to which local parasites are already adapted.
Support for the idea has come from studies of a freshwater snail in New Zealand lakes, in which sexual and asexual individuals coexist. Sexual individuals have been reported to be more frequent where parasitic worms are abundant, and asexual clones that become common tend subsequently to suffer heavier infection. Such findings are consistent with the hypothesis, although few researchers believe that a single mechanism accounts for the persistence of sex across all organisms; the purging of harmful mutations is widely regarded as a complementary explanation.
questions.text: According to the passage, the 'twofold cost of sex' arises because ----.
options: sexual organisms need twice as long to reach maturity as asexual ones
parasites infect sexual hosts twice as often as asexual hosts
sexual females invest about half of their reproductive effort in offspring that cannot themselves give birth
finding and courting a partner doubles the risk of being caught by predators
reshuffling genes destroys exactly half of all successful combinations
questions.explanation: Birinci paragrafa göre eşeyli bir dişi üreme çabasının yaklaşık yarısını yavru doğuramayan erkek yavrulara harcar; bu yüzden eşeysiz bir soy iki kat hızlı çoğalır. Olgunlaşmanın ‘maturity’ iki kat uzun sürmesi, parazitlerin eşeyli konakları ‘twice’ daha sık enfekte etmesi, eş aramanın yırtıcı riskini ‘doubles’ etmesi ve başarılı kombinasyonların tam yarısının (‘exactly half’) bozulması metinde yer almaz.
