questions.passage:
Governments establish regulatory agencies to restrain industries whose behaviour, left unchecked, might harm the public: utilities that could exploit a monopoly, banks that might take excessive risks, or manufacturers whose products could prove unsafe. A long tradition of scholarship, associated in particular with the economist George Stigler, has nevertheless argued that such agencies are liable to end up serving the very industries they were created to supervise. This phenomenon, known as regulatory capture, need not involve outright bribery. It more commonly arises from an asymmetry of interest and information.
The firms subject to a regulation typically have a great deal at stake in its precise wording, and can afford to employ specialists who follow every consultation and hearing. The costs of a weak rule, by contrast, are usually spread thinly across millions of consumers or taxpayers, none of whom has sufficient incentive to monitor the agency closely. Regulators, moreover, frequently depend on the industry for the technical data on which their decisions are based, and the expertise required to understand a complex sector is often found chiefly among people who have worked in it. The resulting movement of personnel between agencies and firms, sometimes described as a revolving door, may shape officials' outlook even in the absence of any improper conduct, since those who expect to seek employment in the industry may be reluctant to antagonise it.
Critics of the capture thesis caution against treating it as a law of nature. Some agencies have demonstrably acted against the wishes of powerful firms, and the theory risks becoming unfalsifiable if every decision favourable to industry is cited as proof of capture while unfavourable ones are dismissed as exceptions. Proposed remedies accordingly focus less on abolishing regulation than on reducing the asymmetries that make capture possible, for instance by funding independent research, publishing records of lobbying contacts and imposing waiting periods before former officials may join regulated firms.
questions.text: According to the passage, regulatory capture ----.
options: is caused mainly by corrupt payments to regulators
affects only those agencies that supervise banks
was first identified by consumer organisations
has been eliminated in most developed countries
can occur even when no official has received a bribe
questions.explanation: Birinci paragraf bu olgunun ‘need not involve outright bribery’ olduğunu, daha çok çıkar ve bilgi asimetrisinden doğduğunu söyler; yani rüşvet olmadan da ortaya çıkabilir. Olgunun esas olarak ‘corrupt payments’ ile açıklanması bu ifadeyle çelişir; yalnızca ‘banks’ı denetleyen kurumlarla sınırlı olduğu, ilk kez ‘consumer organisations’ tarafından saptandığı ve gelişmiş ülkelerde ‘eliminated’ olduğu bilgileri metinde yoktur.

Coach: After I shouted at the team for their dreadful performance last week, they played much better on Saturday.

Maçın ‘rain’ altında oynanması, bağırmanın en etkili yöntem (‘effective’) olması, ‘injured’ oyuncular ve rakibin ‘previous’ maçı ortalamaya dönüş düşüncesine bağlanmaz.

options: Investors started transferring their funds to other countries as soon as the new capital controls were announced.
Investors had moved their funds abroad long before the new capital controls were announced.
The new capital controls were announced in order to stop investors from moving their funds abroad.
Although the new capital controls were announced, investors kept their funds in the country.
Investors were not informed of the new capital controls until they had moved their funds abroad.
questions.explanation: ‘No sooner had … than’ bir olayın hemen ardından ötekinin geldiğini anlatır: denetimler açıklanır açıklanmaz yatırımcılar fonlarını yurt dışına taşımaya başlamıştır; ‘as soon as’ ile kurulan cümle bunu aktarır. Taşımanın açıklamadan ‘long before’ olduğu, denetimlerin bir amaçla (‘in order to’) açıklandığı, fonların ülkede ‘kept’ edildiği ve yatırımcıların sonradan ‘informed’ edildiği iddiaları özgün anlamı değiştirir.

questions.text:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

It was not so much the drug itself as the extra attention patients received during the trial that accounted for their improvement.
options: The patients improved because the drug and the extra attention contributed in exactly equal measure.
The patients' improvement was due less to the drug than to the additional attention they were given during the trial.
The drug proved effective only for those patients who also received extra attention.
Although the patients received extra attention, the drug alone explains their improvement.
The trial failed to give patients enough attention for the drug to work.
questions.explanation: ‘Not so much X as Y’ (X'ten çok Y) yapısı iyileşmenin asıl nedeninin ilaç değil ek ilgi olduğunu bildirir; ‘due less to the drug than to the additional attention’ bunu aktarır. İkisinin ‘equal’ katkı yaptığı, ilacın ‘only’ ek ilgi görenlerde etkili olduğu, iyileşmeyi ‘alone’ ilacın açıkladığı ve denemenin yeterli ilgiyi sağlamadığı (‘failed’) iddiaları özgün cümleyle çelişir.

questions.text:
Verilen cümleye anlamca en yakın cümle hangisidir?

Were it not for genetic recombination, harmful mutations would accumulate far more readily in a population.
options: Harmful mutations accumulate readily because genetic recombination is so common.
Genetic recombination is the main source of harmful mutations in a population.
Populations that lack harmful mutations have no need for genetic recombination.
Recombination would be impossible if harmful mutations did not accumulate.
Genetic recombination makes it harder for harmful mutations to build up in a population.
questions.explanation: ‘Were it not for X’ (X olmasaydı) yapısı X'in bir şeyi engellediğini anlatır: rekombinasyon olmasaydı zararlı mutasyonlar çok daha kolay birikirdi, yani rekombinasyon birikmeyi zorlaştırır. Birikmenin rekombinasyon yaygın olduğu için (‘common’) gerçekleştiği, rekombinasyonun mutasyonların ‘source’u olduğu, mutasyonsuz popülasyonların ona ‘need’ duymadığı ve rekombinasyonun ‘impossible’ olacağı iddiaları ilişkiyi tersine çevirir ya da değiştirir.

questions.passage: Studies of occupational health often compare death rates among employees in a particular industry with those of the general population. Surprisingly, such comparisons frequently suggest that even workers exposed to hazardous substances live longer than average. ---- For this reason, researchers now generally prefer to compare exposed workers with other employed people rather than with the population at large.
questions.text: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Hazardous substances have been banned in most industries since the 1970s.
Death rates in the general population have been falling for more than a century.
Workers are often reluctant to wear protective equipment in hot conditions.
Occupational health is one of the oldest branches of preventive medicine.
This is largely because people who are seriously ill or disabled are less likely to be in employment in the first place.
questions.explanation: Paragraf tehlikeli maddelere maruz kalan işçilerin bile ortalamadan uzun yaşıyor görünmesini şaşırtıcı bulur ve sonra işçilerin genel nüfus yerine başka çalışanlarla karşılaştırılmasının tercih edildiğini söyler; arada bu yanılgının nedenini, yani ağır hasta ya da engelli kişilerin zaten daha az istihdam edildiğini açıklayan cümle gerekir. Maddelerin ‘banned’ olması, nüfusta ölüm oranlarının ‘falling’ olması, koruyucu ekipman (‘protective’) ve dalın eskiliği (‘oldest’) bu karşılaştırma yöntemini açıklamaz.

questions.passage: In 1815 the British Parliament passed the Corn Laws, which restricted imports of cheaper foreign grain in order to protect domestic producers. ---- Manufacturers, by contrast, argued that the laws kept food prices, and therefore wages, artificially high, while encouraging other countries to retaliate against British exports. After a long campaign by the Anti-Corn Law League, the laws were finally repealed in 1846.
questions.text: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Their repeal is often seen as a turning point in Britain's move towards free trade.
The landowners who dominated Parliament at the time regarded the measures as essential to their prosperity.
Manufacturers also supported the laws, since many of them owned large estates.
Bread made up a large part of the diet of most working families.
The Anti-Corn Law League was founded in Manchester in 1838.
questions.explanation: Boşluktan sonraki ‘Manufacturers, by contrast’ ifadesi önceki cümlede yasaları destekleyen başka bir grubun görüşünün anlatılmasını gerektirir; bu grup Parlamento'ya hâkim olan toprak sahipleridir. Yasaların kaldırılmasının (‘repeal’) etkisi paragrafın sonuna aittir; imalatçıların da yasaları ‘supported’ ettiği iddiası ‘by contrast’ ile çelişir; ‘diet’ bilgisi karşıt bir görüş sunmaz; Birliğin ‘founded’ tarihi ise kampanyadan söz edilmeden erken gelir.

questions.passage: Sharks, which are fish, and dolphins, which are mammals, are only very distantly related. ---- Biologists call this process convergent evolution and regard it as evidence that similar environmental demands can produce similar solutions. Close examination, however, usually reveals telling differences: a shark's tail fin, for instance, is vertical, whereas a dolphin's is horizontal.
questions.text: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: Yet both have evolved streamlined bodies, dorsal fins and powerful tails suited to rapid swimming in open water.
Dolphins breathe air and must therefore return regularly to the surface.
Some species of shark have changed remarkably little over hundreds of millions of years.
Both animals are threatened by commercial fishing in many parts of the world.
Their most recent common ancestor is thought to have lived only a few thousand years ago.
questions.explanation: Paragraf köpekbalığı ve yunusun uzak akraba olduğunu söyler, ardından ‘this process’ ile benzer çözümlerin ortaya çıkmasına (yakınsak evrim) değinir; arada iki hayvanın akrabalığa rağmen benzer vücut yapıları geliştirdiğini anlatan ‘Yet both …’ cümlesi gerekir. Yunusların hava solumak için yüzeye çıkması (‘surface’), bazı köpekbalıklarının az değişmesi (‘changed’), ticari avcılık (‘commercial’) ve ortak atanın birkaç bin yıl önce (‘thousand’) yaşadığı iddiası ‘this process’ ifadesine zemin hazırlamaz; sonuncusu ayrıca uzak akrabalıkla çelişir.

questions.passage: According to the theory of the political business cycle, governments manipulate the economy in order to improve their chances of re-election. ---- Once the votes have been counted, however, the resulting inflation or deficits have to be addressed, so unpopular measures tend to be concentrated in the early part of a new term. Evidence for such cycles is mixed, and many economists believe that independent central banks have made them considerably harder to engineer.
questions.text: Paragrafta boş bırakılan yere hangisi getirilmelidir?
options: In the months before an election, for example, they may cut taxes or raise spending to boost employment and incomes.
Elections are held every four years in some countries and every five years in others.
The first independent central banks were established well over a century ago.
After an election, governments frequently reduce the number of ministries.
Voters in many democracies are said to pay little attention to economic news.
questions.explanation: Sonraki cümledeki ‘the resulting inflation or deficits’ ifadesi, enflasyona ve açığa yol açan bir uygulamanın daha önce anlatılmasını gerektirir: seçim öncesinde vergi indirimi ya da harcama artışı. Seçimlerin ‘four years’ aralıkla yapılması, ilk merkez bankalarının ‘established’ tarihi, bakanlık sayısının (‘ministries’) azaltılması ve seçmenlerin ekonomik haberlere ilgisizliği (‘attention’) böyle bir sonuca zemin hazırlamaz.

questions.passage: (I) When a small group of individuals establishes a new population, the genes it carries represent only a fraction of the variation present in the population it came from. (II) Charles Darwin, who visited several remote islands during the voyage of the Beagle, wrote at length about the plants and animals he collected there. (III) As a result, some variants that were rare in the source population may by chance become common in the new one, a phenomenon known as the founder effect. (IV) Several isolated communities, for example, show unusually high frequencies of particular inherited disorders that can be traced back to a handful of early settlers. (V) Because the effect arises by chance rather than through selection, the variants concerned need not be advantageous in any way.
questions.text: Paragrafta anlam bütünlüğünü bozan cümle hangisidir?
options: I
II
III
IV
V
questions.explanation: Paragraf küçük bir grubun yeni bir popülasyon kurduğunda kaynak popülasyondaki çeşitliliğin yalnızca bir kısmını taşımasını (kurucu etkisi), örneklerini ve rastlantısal niteliğini anlatır. II numaralı cümle Darwin'in Beagle yolculuğunda topladığı canlılara geçerek bu akıştan kopar; III'teki ‘As a result’ ancak I'den sonra anlam kazanır. I konuyu açar, III sonucu adlandırır, IV ‘for example’ ile örnek verir, V ise etkinin seçilimle değil şansla oluştuğunu belirtir.

questions.passage: (I) Sickle-cell disease occurs in people who inherit two copies of a particular variant of the haemoglobin gene. (II) Given the severity of the disease, one might expect natural selection to have eliminated the variant long ago. (III) People who carry only one copy, however, appear to be partly protected against severe malaria, which has historically killed large numbers of children in parts of Africa and Asia. (IV) Malaria is transmitted by mosquitoes, and bed nets treated with insecticide are among the most cost-effective means of preventing it. (V) In regions where malaria has long been common, this advantage has kept the variant at relatively high frequencies despite the cost to those who inherit two copies.
questions.text: Paragrafta anlam bütünlüğünü bozan cümle hangisidir?
options: I
II
III
IV
V
questions.explanation: Paragraf orak hücre varyantının ağır bir hastalığa yol açmasına karşın neden ortadan kalkmadığını, tek kopya taşıyanların sıtmaya karşı kısmen korunmasıyla açıklar. IV numaralı cümle sıtmanın sivrisinekle bulaşmasına ve cibinlikle önlenmesine geçerek varyantın sıklığı konusundan sapar. I hastalığı tanımlar, II soruyu kurar, III ‘however’ ile yanıtı verir, V ise ‘this advantage’ ile III'e bağlanarak sonucu açıklar.

questions.passage: (I) In a randomised trial, chance rather than the investigator determines which participants receive the treatment being tested. (II) This matters because doctors who choose patients themselves may, perhaps unconsciously, give a new treatment to those who seem most likely to recover. (III) For randomisation to work, however, the allocation must also be concealed until each participant has been enrolled; otherwise, recruiters who know the next assignment can still influence who receives it. (IV) Reviews comparing trials with and without adequate concealment have reported that the latter tend to show larger treatment effects. (V) The first trial widely described as randomised, which tested streptomycin against tuberculosis, was published in 1948.
questions.text: Paragrafta anlam bütünlüğünü bozan cümle hangisidir?
options: I
II
III
IV
V
questions.explanation: Paragraf randomizasyonun neden önemli olduğunu, işe yaraması için atamanın gizlenmesi gerektiğini ve gizleme yetersiz olduğunda etkilerin abartıldığını anlatır. V numaralı cümle ilk randomize denemenin tarihçesine geçerek atama gizliliğine ilişkin akıştan kopar. I yöntemi tanımlar, II ‘This matters’ ile gerekçesini verir, III ‘however’ ile ek koşulu getirir, IV ise ‘the latter’ ile bu koşulun ihmal edilmesinin sonucunu bildirir.

questions.passage: (I) Economists use the term rent-seeking for efforts to increase one's wealth by obtaining privileges from the state rather than by creating new value. (II) A firm that spends heavily on lobbying for a tariff to shield it from foreign competitors is a typical example. (III) The word 'rent' itself originally referred to the income that landowners received simply by virtue of owning land. (IV) Such spending is regarded as wasteful because the resources devoted to securing the privilege produce nothing of value for society as a whole. (V) Moreover, the competition for privileges may divert talented people away from productive activities such as innovation.
questions.text: Paragrafta anlam bütünlüğünü bozan cümle hangisidir?
options: I
II
III
IV
V
questions.explanation: Paragraf rant kollamanın tanımını, örneğini ve topluma maliyetini anlatır. III numaralı cümle ‘rent’ sözcüğünün kökenine geçerek akışı böler; IV'teki ‘Such spending’ ifadesi II'deki lobi harcamasına gönderme yaptığı için iki cümle arasında başka bir konu yer alamaz. I kavramı tanımlar, II örnek verir, IV bu harcamanın neden israf sayıldığını, V ise ‘Moreover’ ile ek bir maliyeti açıklar.

questions.passage: (I) Most new genes are thought to arise not from scratch but from copies of existing ones. (II) When a gene is accidentally duplicated during cell division, one copy can continue to perform the original function while the other is free to accumulate mutations. (III) Occasionally, these mutations give the spare copy a new and useful role, as appears to have happened with the genes that allow many primates, including humans, to see in full colour. (IV) Colour blindness is far more common in men than in women because the relevant genes are located on the X chromosome. (V) More often, however, the redundant copy acquires damaging mutations and eventually ceases to function altogether.
questions.text: Paragrafta anlam bütünlüğünü bozan cümle hangisidir?
options: I
II
III
IV
V
questions.explanation: Paragraf yeni genlerin var olan genlerin kopyalanmasıyla nasıl ortaya çıktığını ve fazladan kopyanın ya yeni bir işlev kazandığını ya da işlevini yitirdiğini anlatır. IV numaralı cümle renk körlüğünün erkeklerde neden daha sık görüldüğüne geçerek gen kopyalanması konusundan sapar; V'teki ‘More often, however’ III'teki ‘Occasionally’ ile karşıtlık kurar. I konuyu açar, II süreci anlatır, III nadir olumlu sonucu, V ise daha sık görülen olumsuz sonucu verir.

questions.text: Because the reaction is strongly exothermic, the reactor vessel must be cooled continuously in order to ---- the heat released before it damages the surrounding equipment.
options: conceal
duplicate
dissipate
overlook
acquire
questions.explanation: ‘Dissipate’ (dağıtmak, uzaklaştırmak) ısının ekipmana zarar vermeden ortamdan uzaklaştırılmasını anlatır; sürekli soğutma da bunu sağlar. ‘Conceal’ (gizlemek), ‘duplicate’ (çoğaltmak), ‘overlook’ (gözden kaçırmak) ve ‘acquire’ (edinmek) açığa çıkan ısıyla soğutmanın amacını anlatmaz.

questions.text: Certain minerals, such as quartz, are highly ---- to chemical weathering and therefore survive long after the surrounding rock has been broken down.
options: resistant
vulnerable
adjacent
identical
attributable
questions.explanation: ‘Resistant to’ (-e dayanıklı) ifadesi, minerallerin çevredeki kaya parçalandıktan sonra da varlığını sürdürmesini (‘therefore survive’) açıklar. ‘Vulnerable’ (savunmasız) tam ters anlam verir; ‘adjacent’ (bitişik), ‘identical’ (özdeş) ve ‘attributable’ (atfedilebilir) ayrışmaya karşı dayanıklılığı anlatmaz.

questions.text: The new nickel-based alloy retains its strength at temperatures that would cause conventional steel to ----, which makes it suitable for the blades of gas turbines.
options: coincide
prevail
accelerate
emerge
deform
questions.explanation: ‘Deform’ (biçimi bozulmak) yüksek sıcaklıkta sıradan çeliğin başına gelecek olanı anlatır; yeni alaşımın dayanımını koruması bununla karşıtlık kurar. ‘Coincide’ (çakışmak), ‘prevail’ (üstün gelmek), ‘accelerate’ (hızlanmak) ve ‘emerge’ (ortaya çıkmak) çeliğin ısı altında dayanımını yitirmesini anlatmaz.

questions.text: Measurements taken independently at three different laboratories proved remarkably ----, which suggested that the anomaly was a genuine physical effect rather than an instrumental error.
options: arbitrary
consistent
obsolete
contradictory
reluctant
questions.explanation: ‘Consistent’ (tutarlı) sonuçların birbirini doğrulamasını anlatır; bu da anomalinin cihaz hatası değil gerçek bir etki olduğunu düşündürür. ‘Contradictory’ (çelişkili) bu sonuca ters düşer; ‘arbitrary’ (keyfî), ‘obsolete’ (modası geçmiş) ve ‘reluctant’ (isteksiz) ölçümlerin birbirini doğrulamasını anlatmaz.

questions.text: Engineers ---- the probability of structural failure by subjecting thousands of simulated bridges to randomly varying loads on a computer.
options: abandoned
undermined
inherited
estimated
deprived
questions.explanation: ‘Estimated’ (tahmin ettiler, hesapladılar) bilgisayarda binlerce benzetimle bir olasılığın hesaplanmasına uyar. ‘Abandoned’ (vazgeçtiler), ‘undermined’ (zayıflattılar), ‘inherited’ (miras aldılar) ve ‘deprived’ (yoksun bıraktılar) bir olasılığın benzetimle belirlenmesini anlatmaz.

questions.text: Large volcanic eruptions can inject so much sulphur dioxide into the stratosphere that average global temperatures fall ---- for a year or two afterwards.
options: measurably
reluctantly
deliberately
unanimously
courteously
questions.explanation: ‘Measurably’ (ölçülebilir biçimde) sıcaklık düşüşünün ölçülebilecek kadar belirgin olduğunu anlatır. ‘Reluctantly’ (isteksizce), ‘deliberately’ (kasıtlı olarak), ‘unanimously’ (oybirliğiyle) ve ‘courteously’ (nazikçe) insan davranışını niteleyen zarflardır, sıcaklığın düşüşünü nitelemez.

questions.text: By the time the samples reached the laboratory, most of the volatile compounds in them ----, so the analysis had to be repeated with fresh material.
options: evaporate
have evaporated
will have evaporated
had evaporated
are evaporating
questions.explanation: ‘By the time … reached’ geçmişteki bir andan önce tamamlanmış eylemi ister; bu yüzden ‘had evaporated’ (past perfect) gelir. ‘Evaporate’ ve ‘are evaporating’ şimdiki zamandır; ‘have evaporated’ geçmişteki referans noktasına uymaz; ‘will have evaporated’ ise geleceğe aittir.

questions.text: Granite forms when magma cools slowly deep beneath the surface, ---- basalt forms when lava cools rapidly after it has erupted.
options: so that
whereas
unless
as if
in case
questions.explanation: Cümle yavaş soğuyan granit ile hızlı soğuyan bazaltı karşılaştırır; karşıtlık bağlacı ‘whereas’ gerekir. ‘So that’ amaç, ‘unless’ olumsuz koşul, ‘as if’ benzetme, ‘in case’ ise önlem bildirir; hiçbiri iki kayacın oluşumunu karşılaştırmaz.

questions.text: The catalyst was found to be most effective when the reaction mixture ---- at a temperature just below its boiling point.
options: will keep
has kept
had been keeping
is keeping
was kept
questions.explanation: Karışım sıcaklıkta tutulan şeydir, yani edilgen yapı gerekir; ana cümle de geçmiş zamandadır (‘was found’), bu yüzden ‘was kept’ doğrudur. ‘Will keep’, ‘has kept’, ‘had been keeping’ ve ‘is keeping’ etken yapılardır ve karışımı bir şeyi tutan özne yapar.

questions.text: ---- the high cost of the raw materials, the process has not yet been adopted on an industrial scale.
options: Owing to
Although
Provided that
So as to
Whereas
questions.explanation: Boşluktan sonra bir isim öbeği (‘the high cost’) gelir ve bu, sürecin benimsenmemesinin nedenidir; isimle kullanılan neden edatı ‘Owing to’ uygundur. ‘Although’, ‘Provided that’ ve ‘Whereas’ yan cümle ister; ‘So as to’ ise fiil ister ve amaç bildirir.

questions.text: Not only ---- the new detector far more sensitive than its predecessor, but it also consumes considerably less power.
options: it is
has it
is
it was
does it
questions.explanation: ‘Not only’ cümle başında devrik yapı ister; ‘sensitive’ sıfatıyla yardımcı fiil ‘is’ öne geçer: ‘Not only is the new detector…’. ‘It is’ ve ‘it was’ devrik değildir; ‘has it’ ve ‘does it’ ise hem fazladan özne içerir hem de sıfatla uyuşmaz.

questions.text: The engineer ---- design was eventually adopted for the new suspension bridge had initially been criticised by many of her colleagues.
options: who
which
whose
whom
that
questions.explanation: Boşluktan sonra gelen ‘design’ mühendise aittir; iyelik bildiren ilgi zamiri ‘whose’ gerekir. ‘Who’, ‘which’, ‘whom’ ve ‘that’ ardından doğrudan bir isim alıp sahiplik bildiremez.

questions.text: If the Earth's magnetic field ---- suddenly, the surface would be exposed to far higher levels of charged particles from the Sun.
options: disappears
has disappeared
will disappear
would disappear
were to disappear
questions.explanation: Ana cümledeki ‘would be exposed’ gerçek dışı bir varsayım (second conditional) kurar; koşul kısmında ‘were to disappear’ uygundur. ‘Disappears’ ve ‘will disappear’ gerçek koşula, ‘has disappeared’ ise tamamlanmış bir duruma aittir; ‘would disappear’ koşul yan cümlesinde kullanılmaz.

questions.text: Rarely ---- such a large meteorite been recovered intact, since most break apart on entering the atmosphere.
options: does
has
was
did
is
questions.explanation: ‘Rarely’ cümle başında devrik yapı ister; ‘been recovered’ yapısı present perfect edilgen olduğundan yardımcı fiil ‘has’ öne geçer. ‘Does’ ve ‘did’ yalın fiil ister; ‘was’ ve ‘is’ ise ‘been’ ile birlikte kullanılamaz.

questions.text: The equations describing the airflow around the wing are so complex that they can be solved only ---- powerful computers.
options: instead of
regardless of
apart from
by means of
on behalf of
questions.explanation: Denklemlerin hangi araçla çözüldüğü anlatılır; ‘by means of’ (aracılığıyla) bunu karşılar. ‘Instead of’ (yerine), ‘regardless of’ (-e bakmaksızın), ‘apart from’ (dışında) ve ‘on behalf of’ (adına) araç bildirmez.

questions.text: The inspectors recommended that the pipeline ---- every six months for signs of internal damage.
options: be inspected
inspects
has inspected
would inspect
is inspecting
questions.explanation: ‘Recommend that’ ardından yalın fiil (subjunctive) ister; boru hattı denetlenen şey olduğundan edilgen ‘be inspected’ gelir. ‘Inspects’, ‘has inspected’, ‘would inspect’ ve ‘is inspecting’ hem çekimli hem de etken yapılardır; boru hattını denetleyen özne yaparlar.

questions.text: Much of what we know about the Earth's deep interior ---- from the way seismic waves travel through it.
options: deriving
is derived
have derived
derive
to be derived
questions.explanation: Cümlenin öznesi ‘Much of what we know’ tekildir ve bilgi dalgalardan elde edilen şeydir; tekil edilgen ‘is derived’ gerekir. ‘Deriving’ ve ‘to be derived’ çekimli fiil değildir; ‘have derived’ ve ‘derive’ hem çoğul hem de etken yapılardır.

questions.text: The more carbon is added to iron, ---- the resulting steel becomes, although it also grows more brittle.
options: hard
hardest
as hard
the harder
so hard
questions.explanation: ‘The more …, the …’ yapısı iki karşılaştırmalıyı birbirine bağlar; ikinci kısımda ‘the harder’ gerekir. ‘Hard’ yalın sıfattır; ‘hardest’ üstünlük derecesidir; ‘as hard’ ve ‘so hard’ ise bu kalıbı tamamlamaz.

questions.text: Scientists remain uncertain ---- the anomaly reflects a flaw in the instrument or an entirely new physical phenomenon.
options: that
unless
which
so that
whether
questions.explanation: Cümlede ‘… or …’ ile iki olasılık sunulur ve belirsizlik (‘uncertain’) vardır; bunu ‘whether’ (-ip -mediği) karşılar. ‘That’ kesinlik bildirir, ‘unless’ koşul, ‘so that’ amaç bildirir; ‘which’ ise bir isme bağlanacak ilgi zamiridir.

questions.text: Having been fired in a kiln at over 1,000 °C, ----.
options: the clay hardens into a ceramic that will no longer dissolve in water
the potter must allow the kiln to cool down slowly
it is important for the workshop to be well ventilated
there are several changes in the structure of the clay
water evaporates rapidly from the surrounding air
questions.explanation: ‘Having been fired’ yapısının gizli öznesi fırınlanan şeydir; ana cümlenin öznesi de bu olmalıdır: ‘the clay hardens…’. Öznesi ‘potter’ olan cümle çömlekçiyi fırınlanmış gösterir; ‘it is important’ ve ‘there are’ ile başlayan cümleler kimin fırınlandığını belirtmez; ‘water evaporates’ ise suyu fırınlanmış gösterir.

questions.passage: Many molecules exist in two forms that are mirror images of each other, much as a left hand mirrors a right hand. These forms, known as enantiomers, contain exactly the same atoms joined in the same sequence, yet they cannot be superimposed on one another, a property chemists describe as chirality. In most physical respects, such as melting point and solubility, the two forms are indistinguishable; (1) ----, they often behave very differently inside living organisms, because enzymes and receptors are themselves chiral and therefore respond selectively to only one of the two shapes. One enantiomer of a compound may (2) ---- the familiar smell of spearmint, for instance, while its mirror image smells of caraway. In pharmaceuticals, the consequences can be far more serious, since one form of a drug may be therapeutically active and the other inactive or even harmful. For this reason, regulatory agencies now generally require each enantiomer to be characterised separately (3) ---- a new chiral drug is approved. Producing a single enantiomer, however, is technically demanding, because ordinary chemical reactions tend to yield equal mixtures of both forms. Considerable research (4) ---- to so-called asymmetric catalysis, in which a chiral catalyst steers a reaction towards one product, an approach (5) ---- earned its pioneers the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2001.

therefore

in other words

questions.passage: When molten rock cools, tiny grains of iron-rich minerals such as magnetite become magnetised in the direction of the Earth's magnetic field at that moment and preserve this orientation (1) ---- the rock remains undisturbed. Studies of such rocks revealed in the early twentieth century that the field has repeatedly reversed its polarity, (2) ---- that a compass needle would at times have pointed south rather than north. These reversals occur at irregular intervals, ranging from tens of thousands to millions of years, and the most recent one is thought to have taken place roughly 780,000 years ago. In the 1960s, magnetic surveys of the ocean floor uncovered parallel stripes of normally and reversely magnetised rock lying symmetrically on (3) ---- side of the mid-ocean ridges. This pattern was (4) ---- explained by the hypothesis that new crust forms continuously at the ridges and then moves outwards, recording each reversal much like a tape recorder. The discovery thus provided some of the most persuasive evidence for seafloor spreading and, (5) ----, for the theory of plate tectonics as a whole.
questions.text: (1) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: even if
so that
in case
unless
as long as
questions.explanation: Kayadaki manyetik yön, kaya bozulmadığı sürece korunur; süre ve koşul bildiren ‘as long as’ uygundur. ‘Even if’ (-se bile) bozulmamanın korumaya engel olduğunu ima eder; ‘so that’ amaç, ‘in case’ önlem bildirir; ‘unless’ ise anlamı tersine çevirir.

questions.text: Although nuclear fusion releases far more energy per kilogram of fuel than fission does, ----.
options: no fusion reactor has yet supplied electricity to a commercial grid
because the Sun is powered by the fusion of hydrogen nuclei
which requires temperatures of many millions of degrees
so that the waste it produces is far less radioactive
the first fission reactors were built in the 1940s
questions.explanation: ‘Although’ bir karşıtlık ister: Füzyon çok daha fazla enerji açığa çıkarsa da hiçbir füzyon reaktörü henüz ticari şebekeye elektrik vermemiştir. ‘Because’ ve ‘so that’ ile başlayanlar ana cümle kurmaz; ‘which requires’ ilgi cümlesidir; ilk ‘fission reactors’ın yapım tarihi ise karşıtlık kurmaz, konuyla bağı yoktur.

questions.text: Unless the water circulating in the cooling system is treated to remove dissolved minerals, ----.
options: the minerals had been removed before the water entered the pipes
since hard water contains high levels of calcium and magnesium
which is why distilled water was used in the experiment
scale will gradually build up inside the pipes and reduce their efficiency
whether the pipes are made of copper or of steel
questions.explanation: ‘Unless’ gerçek bir koşul kurar ve gelecekteki sonucu ister: Su arıtılmazsa borularda giderek kireç birikir ve verim düşer. ‘Had been removed’ geçmişte kalmış bir durumu anlatır ve koşula uymaz; ‘since’ ve ‘whether’ ile başlayanlar ana cümle değildir; ‘distilled’ suyu anlatan ilgi cümlesi de bağlanacak isim bulamaz.

questions.text: Fragments of meteorites known to have come from Mars are so scarce ----.
options: since they were ejected from the planet by large impacts
even though their composition matches that of Martian rocks
that every newly identified specimen attracts intense scientific interest
which have landed mainly in the deserts of North Africa
before scientists could analyse them in detail
questions.explanation: ‘So scarce’ yapısı ‘that’ ile kurulan bir sonuç cümlesi ister: Bu parçalar o kadar azdır ki yeni bulunan her örnek büyük ilgi çeker. ‘Since … ejected’ neden verir ama ‘so … that’ kalıbını tamamlamaz; ‘even though’ karşıtlık bildirir; ‘deserts’ ile biten ilgi cümlesi ve ‘before scientists’ ile başlayan zaman cümlesi de bu kalıba uymaz.

questions.text: ----, the authorities closed the bridge to heavy vehicles until the damaged cables could be replaced.
options: Unless the cables are replaced every few decades
Whereas suspension bridges are generally lighter than arch bridges
If the engineers had used a different kind of steel
So that heavy vehicles could cross the river more quickly
As soon as inspectors discovered that several steel cables had been weakened by corrosion
questions.explanation: Ana cümle köprünün hasarlı kablolar değiştirilene kadar kapatıldığını söyler; bunun zamanını ve nedenini, müfettişlerin kabloların korozyonla zayıfladığını fark etmesi verir. ‘Unless’ ile başlayan şimdiki zamanlı koşul geçmişteki eyleme uymaz; ‘Whereas’ ilgisiz bir karşılaştırma yapar; ‘If the engineers had used’ ‘would have’ ister; ‘So that heavy vehicles’ ise kapatma kararıyla çelişir.

questions.text: The higher a mountain range rises, ----.
options: its oldest rocks are usually found near its base
the faster it tends to be worn down by erosion
because tectonic plates collided millions of years ago
so that glaciers formed on its upper slopes
which makes it difficult for climbers to breathe
questions.explanation: ‘The higher …’ yapısı ikinci kısımda yine ‘the + karşılaştırmalı’ ister: Dağ ne kadar yükselirse aşınmayla o kadar hızlı yıpranma eğilimindedir. ‘oldest rocks’ ile kurulan cümle karşılaştırma kalıbını tamamlamaz ve yükseklikle bir sonuç ilişkisi kurmaz; ‘because tectonic’, ‘so that glaciers’ ve ‘which makes’ ile başlayanlar bu kalıbı tamamlamaz.

questions.text: Whereas metals conduct electricity because some of their electrons are free to move through the material, ----.
options: copper is widely used in electrical wiring for this reason
since electrons carry a negative electric charge
in insulators such as glass the electrons are tightly bound to individual atoms
which explains why metals feel cold to the touch
even if the current is switched off
questions.explanation: ‘Whereas’ iki durumu karşılaştırır: Metallerde elektronlar serbestken cam gibi yalıtkanlarda atomlara sıkıca bağlıdır. Bakırın ‘wiring’ için kullanılması karşıtlık değil, aynı düşüncenin sonucudur; ‘since electrons’ ve ‘even if the current’ ana cümle değildir; ‘cold to the touch’ ile biten ilgi cümlesi de karşılaştırmayı tamamlamaz.

questions.text: Scientists have been able to date the ancient eruption to a single year ----.
options: by counting the growth rings of trees that were killed by it
although the volcano is still active today
unless historical records describe it in detail
so that the surrounding villages could be evacuated
whereas the lava cooled slowly into basalt
questions.explanation: Bir patlamanın tek bir yıla tarihlendirilmesi, onun öldürdüğü ağaçların yıllık halkalarının sayılmasıyla mümkün olur; ‘by counting’ yöntemi verir. ‘Although the volcano is still active’ karşıtlık kurmaz; ‘unless historical records’ koşulu anlamı bozar; ‘evacuated’ ile biten amaç cümlesi eski bir patlamaya uymaz; ‘basalt’ karşılaştırması ise tarihlendirmeyle ilgisizdir.

questions.text: If the engineers had taken thermal expansion properly into account, ----.
options: the tracks will be inspected more often in summer
steel expands whenever it is heated
the tracks had buckled before the first trains arrived
they would replace the tracks next year
the railway tracks would not have buckled during the heatwave
questions.explanation: ‘If … had taken’ geçmişe ait gerçekleşmemiş bir koşuldur (third conditional); sonuç ‘would not have buckled’ olmalıdır. ‘Will be inspected’ gerçek koşula, ‘steel expands’ genel gerçeğe aittir; ‘had buckled’ sonuç kipini taşımaz; ‘would replace the tracks next year’ ise geçmiş koşulla uyuşmaz.

questions.text: ----, the laboratory had to be evacuated and the experiment was abandoned.
options: Provided that the safety equipment works properly
So that the samples remain uncontaminated
Unless the chemicals are stored correctly
When a leak of toxic gas was detected in the ventilation system
In order to measure the reaction rate more accurately
questions.explanation: Laboratuvarın boşaltılması ve deneyin bırakılması için bir neden ve zaman gerekir: Havalandırmada zehirli gaz sızıntısı fark edildiğinde. ‘Provided that’ ve ‘Unless’ ile kurulan şimdiki zamanlı koşullar geçmişteki olaya uymaz; ‘uncontaminated’ ve ‘accurately’ ile biten amaç cümleleri de boşaltmayı açıklamaz.

questions.text: Diamond and graphite are both composed entirely of carbon, ----.
options: which is why both are used in the cores of pencils
yet they differ greatly in hardness because their atoms are arranged in different ways
so that diamonds are formed under high pressure
although graphite is mined in several countries
unless they are heated to extremely high temperatures
questions.explanation: İkisinin de yalnızca karbondan oluşması beklentiyi doğurur; ‘yet’ ile sertliklerinin atom dizilişi nedeniyle çok farklı olduğu söylenerek karşıtlık kurulur. Her ikisinin ‘pencils’ içinde kullanıldığı bilgisi yanlıştır; ‘so that’ amaç bildirerek anlamı bozar; ‘mined’ ile biten karşıtlık konuyla ilgisizdir; ‘unless’ koşulu ise yapıyla ilgili bir sonuç vermez.

questions.text: Since sound travels much faster in water than in air, ----.
options: light also travels more slowly in water than in a vacuum
although whales communicate over long distances
underwater microphones register a distant explosion sooner than microphones in the air would
which was first measured in a Swiss lake in 1826
unless the water is very cold
questions.explanation: ‘Since’ bir neden verir; sonuç, sesin suda daha hızlı yayılması nedeniyle su altı mikrofonlarının uzak bir patlamayı daha erken algılamasıdır. Işığın ‘vacuum’daki hızı bu nedenin sonucu değildir; ‘although whales’ ve ‘unless the water’ ana cümle kurmaz; ‘Swiss lake’ ile biten ilgi cümlesi de bağlanacak bir isim bulamaz.

questions.text:
Aşağıdaki İngilizce cümlenin anlamca en yakın Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir?

Unlike most substances, water expands when it freezes, which is why ice floats on the surface of lakes rather than sinking to the bottom.
options: Su, donduğunda çoğu madde gibi büzüşür ve bu yüzden buz göllerin dibine çöker.
Çoğu maddenin aksine su donduğunda genleşir; buzun göllerin dibine batmak yerine yüzeyinde yüzmesinin nedeni budur.
Göllerin yüzeyindeki buz, suyun donarken genleşmesini engellediği için diğer maddelerden farklıdır.
Çoğu madde donduğunda genleşir, ancak su bu kuralın tek istisnası değildir.
Buzun göllerin yüzeyinde yüzmesi, suyun yoğunluğunun sıcaklıkla hiç değişmediğini gösterir.
questions.explanation: ‘Unlike most substances’ (çoğu maddenin aksine), ‘expands when it freezes’ (donduğunda genleşir) ve ‘which is why … rather than sinking’ (batmak yerine … nedeni budur) doğru karşılıkta eksiksizdir. Suyun ‘büzüşür’ dediği seçenek anlamı tersine çevirir; buzun genleşmeyi ‘engellediği’ ilişkisi cümlede yoktur; ‘istisnası’ ile kurulan seçenek ve yoğunluğun ‘değişmediğini’ söyleyen seçenek de özgün anlamı karşılamaz.

questions.text:
Aşağıdaki İngilizce cümlenin anlamca en yakın Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir?

The accuracy of the measurements depends largely on how carefully the instruments are calibrated before each experiment.
options: Her deneyden sonra aletlerin kalibre edilmesi, ölçümlerin doğruluğunu tamamen garanti eder.
Aletler ne kadar özenle kalibre edilirse edilsin ölçümler hiçbir zaman tam olarak doğru olmaz.
Deneylerin büyük kısmı, aletler kalibre edilmeden yapıldığı için hatalı sonuç vermiştir.
Ölçümlerin doğruluğu, deneyi yapan araştırmacının deneyimine aletlerden daha çok bağlıdır.
Ölçümlerin doğruluğu büyük ölçüde aletlerin her deneyden önce ne kadar özenle kalibre edildiğine bağlıdır.
questions.explanation: ‘Depends largely on’ (büyük ölçüde … bağlıdır), ‘how carefully’ (ne kadar özenle) ve ‘before each experiment’ (her deneyden önce) doğru karşılıkta vardır. Kalibrasyonun deneyden ‘sonra’ yapılıp doğruluğu ‘garanti’ ettiğini söyleyen seçenek, ölçümlerin ‘hiçbir’ zaman doğru olmadığı iddiası, deneylerin ‘hatalı’ sonuç verdiği bilgisi ve araştırmacının ‘deneyimine’ bağlılık özgün cümlede yoktur.

questions.text:

questions.passage:
For most of history, earthquakes were regarded as purely natural events, driven by the slow movement of tectonic plates and largely beyond human influence. It is now well established, however, that human activities can also trigger seismic activity, a phenomenon known as induced seismicity. The filling of reservoirs behind large dams, deep mining, geothermal energy projects and, above all, the disposal of wastewater produced during oil and gas extraction have all been linked to earthquakes in regions that were previously considered stable.
The underlying mechanism is relatively well understood. Many faults in the Earth's crust are already close to failure, held in place mainly by the friction between the rock surfaces on either side. When large volumes of fluid are injected deep underground, the pressure of the fluid within the pores and fractures of the rock increases. This elevated pore pressure effectively pushes the two sides of a fault apart, reducing the friction that holds them together and allowing stored tectonic stress to be released suddenly. In this sense, the injection does not create the energy of the earthquake; it merely unlocks energy that has accumulated over thousands of years.
The most striking example comes from the central United States, where the number of earthquakes of magnitude three or greater rose sharply after about 2009, coinciding with a dramatic increase in the underground disposal of wastewater. When regulators subsequently required operators to reduce injection volumes, the rate of earthquakes declined, a pattern that considerably strengthened the case for a causal link.
Nonetheless, predicting which injection sites will produce damaging earthquakes remains difficult, since the location and condition of deep faults are often poorly known. Many seismologists therefore advocate so-called traffic-light systems, under which operations are slowed or halted as soon as monitoring instruments detect small tremors, before larger ones can occur.

Muons are elementary particles that resemble electrons but are roughly two hundred times heavier. They are produced in great numbers high in the atmosphere when cosmic rays, energetic particles arriving from space, collide with the nuclei of air molecules. Although a muon survives for only about two millionths of a second before decaying, many travel so close to the speed of light that, owing to the relativistic slowing of time, they reach the ground; at sea level, roughly one passes through an area the size of a human hand every second.
What makes these particles useful to scientists is their remarkable penetrating power. Unlike visible light or X-rays, muons can pass through hundreds of metres of solid rock, gradually losing energy as they go. The denser and thicker the material along their path, the fewer of them emerge on the other side. By placing detectors beside or beneath a large structure and recording the number of muons arriving from different directions over weeks or months, researchers can therefore construct an image of its internal density, in much the same way that a medical X-ray reveals the bones inside the body. The technique has become known as muography.
Since the late 2000s, muography has been used to examine the interiors of volcanoes in Japan and Italy, revealing the position of magma channels near their summits that may influence future eruptions. In 2017, a team working at the Great Pyramid of Giza reported a large, previously unknown void above the monument's Grand Gallery, a finding that attracted worldwide attention, although the purpose of the space remains unclear. The method has also been applied to the inspection of nuclear reactors damaged in accidents and proposed for the screening of cargo containers.
Muography nevertheless has clear limitations. Because the natural flux of muons is fixed and comparatively low, acquiring a sharp image may take many months, and the technique cannot easily resolve fine details within very large objects.

Metne göre müonlar atmosferin üst katmanlarında oluşur, deniz düzeyinde (‘water molecules’) değil; elektronlardan hafif (‘lighter’) değil ağırdır; kayaya girene kadar bozunmadıkları (‘decay’) ve kozmik ışınların onları doğrudan taşıdığı (‘directly’) da söylenmez.

questions.passage:
Zeolites are crystalline minerals composed mainly of silicon, aluminium and oxygen, whose atoms are linked into rigid three-dimensional frameworks riddled with channels and cavities of molecular dimensions. Several dozen types occur naturally, often in rocks formed where volcanic ash has reacted with alkaline groundwater, but chemists have synthesised far more, each with a characteristic arrangement of pores. The name, derived from Greek words meaning 'boiling stone', refers to the observation, first made in the eighteenth century, that some of these minerals appear to boil when heated, as water trapped inside them is driven off.
Because the openings of their pores are uniform in size, zeolites can act as molecular sieves, admitting molecules that are small enough to enter while excluding larger ones. Moreover, the substitution of aluminium for silicon in the framework leaves a negative charge that must be balanced by positive ions, such as sodium or calcium, held loosely within the cavities. These ions can readily be exchanged for others in a surrounding solution, a property that explains the widespread use of zeolites in water softening, where calcium and magnesium are captured and replaced by sodium, and in laundry detergents, where they have largely replaced phosphates, compounds implicated in the excessive growth of algae in lakes and rivers.
Their most important industrial application, however, lies in catalysis. In petroleum refineries, zeolite catalysts break down large hydrocarbon molecules into the smaller ones that make up petrol, and because reactions can take place only within pores of a particular shape and size, the catalysts favour certain products over others. This shape selectivity, which offers a degree of control that few other catalysts provide, has made zeolites one of the most valuable groups of materials in the chemical industry, and the search for new frameworks tailored to specific reactions continues to expand.

questions.passage:
When the pressure in a flowing liquid drops below its vapour pressure, small cavities filled with vapour form within it, much as bubbles appear in water brought to the boil. Unlike boiling, however, this process, known as cavitation, results not from heating but from a local fall in pressure, such as occurs where water accelerates around the tips of a rapidly rotating propeller or through the narrow passages of a pump. The cavities typically exist for only a tiny fraction of a second. As soon as they are carried into regions of higher pressure, they collapse violently, and the surrounding liquid rushes inwards to fill the space they occupied.
For engineers, this collapse is a persistent source of trouble. When it takes place close to a solid surface, it produces minute jets of liquid and shock waves that strike the metal repeatedly. Over time, such impacts can pit and erode even hardened steel, gradually reducing the efficiency of pumps, turbines and ship propellers and eventually requiring costly repairs. Cavitation also generates considerable noise and vibration, a particular concern for submarines, which depend on remaining undetected. Designers therefore attempt to shape blades so that the pressure does not fall too far, to operate machinery within carefully defined limits or, in some cases, to coat vulnerable surfaces with more resistant materials.
Yet the same destructive energy can be put to productive use. Ultrasonic cleaning baths, for example, deliberately create cavitation to dislodge dirt from delicate components, and related effects are thought to contribute to some medical procedures that break up kidney stones. Certain high-speed underwater vehicles even surround themselves with a single large cavity of vapour, a technique called supercavitation, which greatly reduces the drag exerted by the water. In this sense, cavitation illustrates a recurring theme in engineering: a phenomenon that damages machines in one context may become a valuable tool in another.

questions.passage:
For most of the twentieth century, crystallographers worked on the assumption that every crystal consists of a basic unit of atoms repeated at regular intervals in three dimensions, rather like identical tiles covering a floor. A strict mathematical consequence of this periodic arrangement is that only certain kinds of rotational symmetry are possible: a crystal may look the same after being rotated by a half, a third, a quarter or a sixth of a full turn, but never by a fifth, just as a floor cannot be covered without gaps by regular pentagons.
In 1982, however, the materials scientist Dan Shechtman, examining a rapidly cooled alloy of aluminium and manganese under an electron microscope, obtained a diffraction pattern with sharp tenfold symmetry, implying an ordered structure with fivefold symmetry. Because the pattern contradicted established principles, his findings were initially met with considerable scepticism, and some prominent scientists dismissed them outright, suggesting that he had mistaken several overlapping ordinary crystals for a single new one. Only after other laboratories had reproduced the results and theorists had shown that atoms could be ordered without repeating, in a manner resembling the non-periodic tilings devised by the mathematician Roger Penrose, did these so-called quasicrystals gain acceptance. In 1992 the official definition of a crystal was broadened to include them, and in 2011 Shechtman was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
Since then, many quasicrystalline materials have been produced in laboratories, and a naturally occurring example was reported in 2009 in a rock sample now thought to have come from a meteorite. Quasicrystals tend to be hard, poor conductors of heat and resistant to sticking, properties that have led to their use in some non-stick coatings and in certain steels for surgical instruments. Perhaps their greatest significance, however, lies in the lesson they offer about science itself: a rule that appears firmly established may turn out to be narrower than it seemed.

Mikroskobun güvenilmez (‘unreliable’) olduğu ve bu metallerin alaşım (‘alloys’) oluşturmadığı söylenmez; diğer laboratuvarlar sonuçları çürütmemiş, yinelemiştir (‘different results’ yanlış); göktaşı (‘meteorite’) örneği ise 2009’da bulunmuştur.

questions.passage: Many modern medicines, including several treatments for cancer and rheumatoid arthritis, are biologics: large, complex molecules produced by living cells rather than by chemical synthesis. When the patent on a conventional drug expires, other manufacturers may produce generic copies that are chemically identical to the original. With biologics, (1) ----, exact replication is impossible, because even minor differences in the cell lines or manufacturing conditions can alter the final product. Copies of these drugs are therefore known as biosimilars, and regulators require evidence that they (2) ---- no clinically meaningful differences from the reference product in terms of safety and efficacy. Because developing a biosimilar is far more expensive than producing a generic drug, the price reductions it brings tend to be (3) ---- modest. Even so, health systems (4) ---- considerable sums since biosimilars first entered the market, savings that can be redirected (5) ---- other areas of care.
questions.text: (4) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: saved
had saved
will save
are saving
have saved
questions.explanation: ‘Since biosimilars first entered the market’ geçmişte başlayıp bugüne uzanan süreyi anlatır; ana cümlede ‘have saved’ (present perfect) gerekir. ‘Saved’ ve ‘had saved’ bu süreyi bugüne bağlamaz; ‘will save’ ve ‘are saving’ ise ‘since’ yapısıyla uyumsuzdur.

without
towards
beneath
despite
questions.explanation: ‘Redirect something towards’ (bir şeyi başka bir yöne aktarmak) kalıbı gerekir: tasarruflar bakımın başka alanlarına aktarılabilir. ‘Against’ karşıtlık, ‘without’ yokluk, ‘beneath’ konum, ‘despite’ ise zıtlık bildirir ve fiille anlamlı bir bağ kurmaz.

questions.passage: Delirium, an acute state of confusion that develops over hours or days, affects a substantial proportion of older patients admitted to hospital, particularly (1) ---- undergoing surgery or receiving intensive care. Unlike dementia, which progresses slowly, delirium tends to fluctuate during the day, (2) ---- it easy to miss during brief medical rounds. Its consequences are nevertheless serious: patients who experience it are more likely to stay in hospital longer, to lose their independence and to die in the following months. Although no medication has been shown to prevent delirium reliably, nurse-led programmes (3) ---- focus on simple measures appear to reduce its incidence considerably. These include keeping patients oriented to the time and place, encouraging them to walk, ensuring that they wear their glasses and hearing aids, and (4) ---- unnecessary noise at night so that normal sleep is preserved. Because nurses spend more time with patients than any other professional, they are (5) ---- placed to recognise the early signs of the condition.
questions.text: (1) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: that
those
them
which
whose
questions.explanation: ‘Patients’ ismini tekrar etmemek için çoğul gösterme zamiri ‘those’ kullanılır: ‘particularly those undergoing surgery’ (özellikle ameliyat olanlar). ‘That’ tekildir; ‘them’ nesne zamiridir ve sıfat-fiille niteleneme; ‘which’ ve ‘whose’ ise arkalarından çekimli fiil ya da isim ister.

makes

what

where
whom

options: amplifying
tolerating
recording
imitating
minimising
questions.explanation: Normal uykunun korunması (‘so that normal sleep is preserved’) için gece gereksiz gürültünün azaltılması gerekir: ‘minimising’. ‘Amplifying’ (artırmak) amaçla çelişir; ‘tolerating’ (katlanmak), ‘recording’ (kaydetmek) ve ‘imitating’ (taklit etmek) uykuyu korumaya hizmet etmez.

questions.text: (5) numaralı boşluğa hangisi gelmelidir?
options: well
hardly
poorly
rarely
barely
questions.explanation: ‘Well placed to do something’ (bir şeyi yapmak için iyi konumda olmak) kalıbı gerekir; hemşireler hastalarla en çok zaman geçirdiği için belirtileri fark etmeye en uygun kişilerdir. ‘Hardly’, ‘poorly’, ‘rarely’ ve ‘barely’ olumsuz anlam taşır ve ‘because’ ile verilen gerekçeyle çelişir.

questions.text: While moderate coffee consumption is regarded as safe for most healthy adults, ----.
options: it had been banned in several countries during the seventeenth century
individuals who experience palpitations after drinking it may be advised to reduce their intake
so that the caffeine is absorbed more slowly by the stomach
unless it was drunk without sugar or milk
because coffee beans are grown mainly in tropical regions
questions.explanation: ‘While’ burada zıtlık kurar: kahve çoğu kişi için güvenli sayılsa da çarpıntı yaşayanlara tüketimi azaltmaları önerilebilir. Yasaklandığını söyleyen ‘seventeenth century’ cümlesi zaman uyumunu bozar; ‘absorbed’ ile amaç bildiren yapı ana cümle kurmaz; ‘sugar’ ile ilgili koşul ve kahvenin ‘tropical’ bölgelerde yetiştiği bilgisi zıtlığı tamamlamaz.

questions.text: Cardiac rehabilitation programmes, ----, have been shown to lower the risk of further heart problems.
options: as if patients had never had a heart attack
so much that hospitals cannot afford them
who had been discharged from hospital the previous week
which combine supervised exercise with education about diet and medication
unless patients will refuse to take part
questions.explanation: Ara cümle programları tanımlayan bir ilgi cümlesi olmalıdır: ‘which combine supervised exercise …’. ‘As if’ ile kurulan karşılaştırma ve ‘afford’ ile kurulan derece yapısı öznenin ardına anlamlı biçimde yerleşmez; ‘discharged’ içeren ‘who’ cümlesi ise kişiler için kullanılır ve programları niteleyemez; ‘refuse’ içeren koşul ise ‘unless’ ile gelecek zaman kullanarak dilbilgisini bozar.

questions.text: If a patient's oxygen saturation falls below the target range, ----.
options: the nurse should inform the responsible physician without delay
the nurse would have informed the physician immediately
oxygen had been discovered in the eighteenth century
although the patient had been breathing normally
which is measured with a small clip on the finger
questions.explanation: Birinci tip koşul (‘If … falls’) şimdiki ya da gelecek zamanlı bir sonuç ister: hemşire sorumlu hekime gecikmeden haber vermelidir. ‘Would have informed’ üçüncü tip koşula aittir; oksijenin ‘discovered’ edilmesi konuyla ilgisizdir; ‘breathing’ içeren ‘although’ yapısı ana cümle kurmaz; ‘clip’ ile biten ilgi cümlesi de bağlanacak isim bulamaz.

questions.text: ----, the body loses heat almost entirely through the evaporation of sweat from the skin.
options: Unless the person is exercising vigorously
Since the skin is the largest organ of the body
Even if the air is much colder than the skin
When the surrounding air is hotter than the skin
So that the core temperature can rise
questions.explanation: Ortam havası deriden sıcaksa vücut ışıma ve iletimle ısı veremez, ısıyı neredeyse yalnızca terin buharlaşmasıyla atar; bu yüzden ‘When the surrounding air is hotter than the skin’ doğrudur. ‘Vigorously’ içeren koşul, derinin en büyük organ olduğu (‘largest’) gerekçesi ve havanın ‘colder’ olduğu durum bu sonucu açıklamaz; ‘core temperature’ın yükselmesi amacı da ısı kaybıyla çelişir.

questions.text: Many medicines are given by injection rather than by mouth ----.
options: which the patient swallowed with a glass of water
even if they had been absorbed completely in the gut
so that the liver can inactivate them before they act
as soon as the first syringe was invented
because they would be broken down by digestive enzymes before reaching the bloodstream
questions.explanation: Pek çok ilaç, sindirim enzimleri tarafından kana ulaşmadan parçalanacağı için ağızdan değil enjeksiyonla verilir. ‘Swallowed’ içeren ilgi cümlesi enjeksiyonla çelişir; bağırsakta tümüyle emilme (‘absorbed completely’) varsayımı gerekçe olamaz; karaciğerin ilacı etkisizleştirmesi (‘inactivate’) amaç olamaz; ilk şırınganın icadı (‘syringe’) ise zaman uyumunu ve mantığı bozar.

questions.text: Only after the patient's medication history had been reviewed ----.
options: the doctors realised that her dizziness was a side effect of her blood pressure tablets
the doctors had recognised that her tablets were causing her dizziness
realising the doctors that her tablets caused her dizziness
did the doctors realise that her dizziness was a side effect of her blood pressure tablets
that the doctors would realise the cause of her dizziness
questions.explanation: Cümle ‘Only after’ ile başladığı için ana cümlede devrik yapı gerekir: ‘did the doctors realise …’. ‘The doctors realised’ devrik değildir; ‘recognised’ ile kurulan ‘had’ seçeneği hem devrik değildir hem de zaman sırasını bozar; ‘realising’ ile başlayan yapıda çekimli fiil yoktur; ‘would realise’ içeren ‘that’ yan cümlesi de ana cümle oluşturmaz.

questions.text: Dental X-rays expose patients to only a very small dose of radiation; ----.
options: therefore, they are the main cause of cancer in children
nevertheless, dentists are advised to take them only when they are clinically justified
for example, sunlight contains no radiation at all
otherwise, the patient would not have been treated
in other words, X-rays cannot pass through the teeth
questions.explanation: Dozun çok küçük olması ile yine de yalnızca gerekli olduğunda çekilmesinin önerilmesi arasındaki ilişkiyi ‘nevertheless’ kurar. Çocuklardaki kanserin ana nedeni olduğu iddiası (‘main cause’) küçük dozla çelişir; güneş ışığının hiç radyasyon içermediği (‘sunlight’) yanlıştır ve örnek değildir; ‘otherwise’ ile kurulan geçmiş koşul ilgisizdir; ışınların dişten geçemediği (‘cannot pass’) da ilk cümleyi açıklamaz.

questions.text: The more closely patients adhere to their prescribed treatment, ----.
options: the more expensive was the medication
they are less likely to be readmitted
the less likely they are to be readmitted to hospital
so that they will be readmitted less often
as long as their doctors had explained it
questions.explanation: ‘The more …, the less …’ paralel karşılaştırma yapısı ikinci bölümde de ‘the + karşılaştırma’ ister: ‘the less likely they are to be readmitted’. ‘Expensive’ içeren seçenek zaman uyumunu bozar ve anlamsızdır; ‘the’ olmadan kurulan ‘they are less likely’ yapıyı tamamlamaz; ‘so that’ ile amaç ve ‘explained’ içeren koşul da paralel yapıya uymaz.

questions.text: ----, the kidneys release a hormone that stimulates the bone marrow to produce more red blood cells.
options: Unless the blood carries too little oxygen
Although the tissues are receiving plenty of oxygen
Since the kidneys had been damaged by an infection
So that blood pressure drops during the night
When the oxygen content of the blood falls
questions.explanation: Böbrekler kandaki oksijen azaldığında kemik iliğini uyaran bir hormon (eritropoetin) salgılar; bu yüzden ‘When the oxygen content of the blood falls’ doğrudur. ‘Unless … too little oxygen’ ilişkiyi tersine çevirir; dokuların bol oksijen aldığı (‘plenty’) durum bu tepkiyi gerektirmez; ‘damaged’ böbrek gerekçesi zaman uyumunu bozar ve mantıksızdır; gece kan basıncının düşmesi (‘during the night’) ise ilgisiz bir amaçtır.

questions.text: Public health campaigns tend to be most effective ----.
options: unless they had been funded by the government
which were launched in the twentieth century
when they are tailored to the beliefs and circumstances of the communities they target
so that people stopped smoking immediately
even though nobody pays any attention to them
questions.explanation: Kampanyaların en etkili olduğu koşulu bildiren zaman yan cümlesi gerekir: hedefledikleri toplulukların inançlarına ve koşullarına göre uyarlandıklarında. ‘Funded’ içeren koşul zaman uyumunu bozar; ‘launched’ ile kurulan ilgi cümlesi bağlanacak isim bulamaz; ‘smoking’ ile amaç yapısı geçmiş zamanla uyumsuzdur; kimsenin ilgilenmemesi (‘nobody’) ise etkililik fikriyle çelişir.

questions.text: Some medicines that can be bought without a prescription ----.
options: that doctors would never have prescribed to children
whose effects lasting only a few minutes
which pharmacists recommend them to every customer
may interact dangerously with drugs that a patient is already taking
having been sold in supermarkets for many years
questions.explanation: Öznenin (‘Some medicines that …’) bir yüklemi olmalıdır: ‘may interact dangerously …’. ‘Never have prescribed’ içeren seçenek ikinci bir ilgi cümlesidir ve yüklem yoktur; ‘lasting’ çekimli fiil değildir; ‘recommend them’ ilgi cümlesinde gereksiz zamir kullanır; ‘supermarkets’ içeren ortaç öbeği de cümleyi tamamlamaz.

questions.text:
Aşağıdaki İngilizce cümlenin anlamca en yakın Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir?

Grapefruit juice can raise the concentration of certain drugs in the blood because it inhibits an enzyme in the intestine that normally breaks them down.
options: Greyfurt suyu, bağırsaktaki enzimleri uyararak bazı ilaçların kandan daha hızlı temizlenmesini sağlar.
Bazı ilaçlar, bağırsaktaki bir enzimi baskıladıkları için greyfurt suyuyla birlikte alınmamalıdır.
Greyfurt suyunun kandaki derişimi, bağırsakta bulunan bir enzim tarafından belirlenir.
Greyfurt suyu bazı ilaçların etkisini azaltabilir; çünkü bu ilaçlar bağırsakta emilmeden önce parçalanır.
Greyfurt suyu, normalde bazı ilaçları parçalayan bağırsaktaki bir enzimi baskıladığı için bu ilaçların kandaki derişimini artırabilir.
questions.explanation: ‘Inhibits an enzyme … that normally breaks them down’ (normalde onları parçalayan bir enzimi baskıladığı için) ve ‘can raise the concentration’ (derişimini artırabilir) doğru karşılıkta eksiksizdir. Enzimleri ‘uyararak’ ilacı daha hızlı temizlediğini söyleyen seçenek anlamı tersine çevirir; enzimi ilaçların baskıladığını ve greyfurt suyuyla ‘alınmamalıdır’ diyen seçenek özneyi değiştirir; greyfurt suyunun kendi derişiminin ‘belirlenir’ olması ve etkinin ‘azaltabilir’ biçiminde verilmesi de cümlede yoktur.

questions.text:
Aşağıdaki İngilizce cümlenin anlamca en yakın Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir?

Although tooth enamel is the hardest substance in the human body, it cannot regenerate once it has been lost.
options: Diş minesi insan vücudundaki en sert madde olduğu için kolayca kaybedilmez ve kendini yenileyebilir.
Diş minesi kaybedildiğinde, vücut onu daha sert bir maddeyle yeniden oluşturur.
Diş minesi insan vücudundaki en sert madde olmasına karşın bir kez kaybedildiğinde yenilenemez.
İnsan vücudundaki en sert madde olan diş minesi, yalnızca çocuklukta yenilenebilir.
Diş minesi yenilenemediği için insan vücudundaki en sert madde olarak kabul edilir.
questions.explanation: ‘Although’ (-mesine karşın) ve ‘cannot regenerate once it has been lost’ (bir kez kaybedildiğinde yenilenemez) doğru karşılıkta vardır. Minenin ‘kendini’ yenileyebildiğini söyleyen seçenek anlamı tersine çevirir; vücudun mineyi yeniden ‘oluşturur’ olması ve ‘çocuklukta’ yenilenmesi cümlede geçmez; yenilenememeyi sertliğin nedeni olarak ‘kabul’ eden seçenek ise zıtlığı neden-sonuca çevirir.

questions.text:
Aşağıdaki İngilizce cümlenin anlamca en yakın Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir?

The risk of a heart attack appears to be highest in the early morning hours, when blood pressure and heart rate rise sharply after waking.
options: Sabahın erken saatlerinde uyanan kişilerde kan basıncı ve kalp hızı daha düşük olduğu için kalp krizi riski azalır.
Kalp krizi geçirenlerin çoğu, sabah uyandıklarında kan basınçlarının düştüğünü bildirmektedir.
Kalp krizi riskinin sabah saatlerinde arttığı düşünülse de kan basıncı ve kalp hızı uykudan sonra değişmez.
Kalp krizi riski, uyandıktan sonra kan basıncının ve kalp hızının keskin biçimde yükseldiği sabahın erken saatlerinde en yüksek düzeyde görünmektedir.
Uyandıktan hemen sonra kan basıncını ölçmek, kalp krizi riskini belirlemenin en güvenilir yoludur.
questions.explanation: ‘Appears to be highest’ (en yüksek düzeyde görünmektedir), ‘in the early morning hours’ ve ‘rise sharply after waking’ (uyandıktan sonra keskin biçimde yükseldiği) doğru karşılıkta eksiksizdir. Riskin ‘azalır’ olduğunu söyleyen seçenek anlamı tersine çevirir; hastaların basınç düşüşünü ‘bildirmektedir’ ifadesi ve basıncın uykudan sonra ‘değişmez’ olduğu iddiası cümleyle çelişir; ölçümün en ‘güvenilir’ yol olması ise cümlede yoktur.

questions.text:
Aşağıdaki İngilizce cümlenin anlamca en yakın Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir?

Nurses working in palliative care aim not to cure the disease but to relieve pain and to improve the quality of life of patients and their families.
options: Palyatif bakımda çalışan hemşireler, ağrıyı dindirmenin yanı sıra hastalığı tamamen iyileştirmeyi de amaçlar.
Hastaların aileleri, palyatif bakım hemşirelerinin yalnızca ağrı kesici vermesini bekler.
Hemşirelerin yaşam kalitesi, palyatif bakımda hastaların ağrısıyla doğrudan ilişkilidir.
Palyatif bakımda çalışan hemşireler hastalığı iyileştirmeyi değil, ağrıyı dindirmeyi ve hastalarla ailelerinin yaşam kalitesini artırmayı amaçlar.
Palyatif bakımda hastalığı iyileştirmek mümkün olmadığından hemşireler ailelerle hiç ilgilenmez.
questions.explanation: ‘Not to cure … but to relieve pain and to improve the quality of life’ (iyileştirmeyi değil, ağrıyı dindirmeyi ve yaşam kalitesini artırmayı) yapısı doğru karşılıkta korunmuştur. Hastalığı ‘tamamen’ iyileştirmeyi de amaçladığını söyleyen seçenek ‘not … but’ zıtlığını bozar; ailelerin ‘bekler’ olduğu iddiası, hemşirelerin yaşam kalitesinin ‘ilişkilidir’ diye verilmesi ve ailelerle ‘ilgilenmez’ ifadesi özgün cümlede yoktur.

questions.text:
Aşağıdaki İngilizce cümlenin anlamca en yakın Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir?

The extent to which a drug reaches the systemic circulation after it is taken by mouth is referred to as its bioavailability.
options: Bir ilacın sistemik dolaşımdan ne kadar sürede atıldığı, biyoyararlanımını belirleyen tek etkendir.
Ağızdan alınan ilaçların sistemik dolaşıma hiç ulaşmaması biyoyararlanım sorunu olarak bilinir.
Biyoyararlanım, bir ilacın ağızdan alınmak yerine damardan verilmesini gerektiren durumdur.
Bir ilacın ağızdan alındıktan sonra etkisini ne kadar hızlı gösterdiği, o ilacın gücünü belirler.
Bir ilacın ağızdan alındıktan sonra sistemik dolaşıma ulaşma derecesi, o ilacın biyoyararlanımı olarak adlandırılır.
questions.explanation: ‘The extent to which a drug reaches the systemic circulation’ (sistemik dolaşıma ulaşma derecesi) ve ‘is referred to as’ (olarak adlandırılır) doğru karşılıkta vardır. İlacın dolaşımdan ‘atıldığı’ süreyi anlatan seçenek, dolaşıma hiç ‘ulaşmaması’ durumunu tanımlayan seçenek, ‘damardan’ verilmeyi gerektiren durum ve ilacın ‘gücünü’ belirleyen hız bilgisi cümlenin tanımına uymaz.

questions.text:
Aşağıdaki İngilizce cümlenin anlamca en yakın Türkçe karşılığı hangisidir?

Atrial fibrillation is the most common sustained disturbance of heart rhythm, and its prevalence rises steeply with age, so that it affects a considerable proportion of people over eighty. In this condition, the electrical impulses that normally spread across the upper chambers of the heart, the atria, in an orderly wave become chaotic, and the atria quiver rather than contract effectively. Many patients experience palpitations, breathlessness or fatigue, but a substantial number have no symptoms at all, and the disorder is discovered only incidentally, for instance during a routine examination.
The principal danger of atrial fibrillation lies not in the irregular heartbeat itself but in its effect on blood flow. Because the atria no longer empty completely, blood may stagnate, particularly in a small pouch of the left atrium known as the appendage, and form clots there. If such a clot is carried into the circulation, it can lodge in an artery of the brain and cause a stroke. Strokes associated with atrial fibrillation tend to be more severe and more often fatal than those arising from other causes.
For this reason, the management of the condition centres on stroke prevention. Oral anticoagulants, which reduce the ability of the blood to clot, lower the risk of stroke substantially, but they also increase the likelihood of bleeding. Clinicians therefore weigh the two risks against each other for each patient, using scoring systems that take into account factors such as age, high blood pressure, diabetes and previous strokes. For many decades, warfarin was the only widely used option, and it required frequent blood tests and careful attention to diet. Newer agents, which act on specific clotting factors, need less monitoring and have made treatment considerably more convenient, although they are not suitable for every patient, notably those with mechanical heart valves.

Periodontal disease, a chronic inflammation of the tissues that surround and support the teeth, is one of the most widespread conditions in adult populations, and its severe form is a leading cause of tooth loss in later life. It begins when bacteria accumulate in a sticky film, known as plaque, along the gum line. If the plaque is not removed by regular brushing and cleaning between the teeth, the gums become red, swollen and prone to bleeding, a reversible stage called gingivitis. In susceptible individuals, however, the inflammation gradually extends deeper, destroying the ligaments and bone that anchor the teeth, which may eventually become loose.
Over the past three decades, researchers have increasingly asked whether the consequences of periodontal disease are confined to the mouth. Large observational studies have repeatedly found that people with the condition are more likely to suffer from cardiovascular disease, and the relationship with diabetes appears to run in both directions: poorly controlled blood sugar worsens gum inflammation, and severe gum inflammation seems to make blood sugar harder to control. Several mechanisms have been proposed. Bacteria from inflamed gums can enter the bloodstream during everyday activities such as chewing, and inflammatory molecules produced in the gums may contribute to a low-grade inflammation throughout the body.
Nevertheless, association is not the same as causation. Smoking, poor diet and low income are risk factors for both gum disease and heart disease, and they may account for much of the link between the two. Trials in which patients receive intensive periodontal treatment have produced encouraging but limited results: in people with diabetes, such treatment has been followed by modest improvements in blood sugar control, whereas convincing evidence that it prevents heart attacks or strokes is still lacking. Most specialists therefore recommend good oral hygiene for its own sake, while cautioning against claims that a toothbrush can protect the heart.

When a person who has been lying down stands up, gravity immediately pulls roughly half a litre of blood or more downward into the veins of the legs and abdomen. As a result, less blood returns to the heart, the amount pumped with each beat falls, and blood pressure begins to drop. That most people notice nothing more than a fleeting sensation of light-headedness is owed to a rapid correction mechanism known as the baroreceptor reflex.
Baroreceptors are stretch-sensitive nerve endings located chiefly in the walls of the carotid arteries in the neck and of the aorta. When blood pressure falls, these vessel walls are stretched less, and the receptors reduce the rate at which they send signals to the brainstem. The brainstem interprets this change as a warning and, within a few seconds, increases the activity of the sympathetic nervous system. The heart beats faster and more forcefully, while blood vessels in the limbs and abdomen constrict, pushing blood back towards the heart and restoring an adequate supply to the brain.
In some people this compensation is inadequate. Orthostatic hypotension, usually defined as a sustained fall in blood pressure within three minutes of standing, can cause dizziness, blurred vision and fainting. It becomes more frequent with age, as arteries stiffen and the reflex grows less sensitive, and it is also common in people with diabetes or Parkinson's disease, conditions that can damage the nerves involved. Medication is a further and frequently overlooked cause: drugs that lower blood pressure, relax blood vessels or increase urine production may all exaggerate the fall. Because a faint can lead to serious injuries such as fractures in older adults, clinicians often recommend simple measures, such as rising slowly, drinking enough fluid and reviewing existing prescriptions, before considering additional drugs.

When a person who has been lying down stands up, gravity immediately pulls roughly half a litre of blood or more downward into the veins of the legs and abdomen. As a result, less blood returns to the heart, the amount pumped with each beat falls, and blood pressure begins to drop. That most people notice nothing more than a fleeting sensation of light-headedness is owed to a rapid correction mechanism known as the baroreceptor reflex.
Baroreceptors are stretch-sensitive nerve endings located chiefly in the walls of the carotid arteries in the neck and of the aorta. When blood pressure falls, these vessel walls are stretched less, and the receptors reduce the rate at which they send signals to the brainstem. The brainstem interprets this change as a warning and, within a few seconds, increases the activity of the sympathetic nervous system. The heart beats faster and more forcefully, while blood vessels in the limbs and abdomen constrict, pushing blood back towards the heart and restoring an adequate supply to the brain.
In some people this compensation is inadequate. Orthostatic hypotension, usually defined as a sustained fall in blood pressure within three minutes of standing, can cause dizziness, blurred vision and fainting. It becomes more frequent with age, as arteries stiffen and the reflex grows less sensitive, and it is also common in people with diabetes or Parkinson's disease, conditions that can damage the nerves involved. Medication is a further and frequently overlooked cause: drugs that lower blood pressure, relax blood vessels or increase urine production may all exaggerate the fall. Because a faint can lead to serious injuries such as fractures in older adults, clinicians often recommend simple measures, such as rising slowly, drinking enough fluid and reviewing existing prescriptions, before considering additional drugs.
